frames show Kay'l alone against SCENE 55's cast of three programs' actors
(Kay'l 49, the Demon 57, the Meca 58 - `A_1_KaylArrives`, `A_2_DemonLook`,
`C_1_MecaComes`) and AREA 222's three attached passers-by.

**Severity B** for the port (nothing a script decides changes), but it is the
first thing a person sees.

**Fix shape (T20 in the plan)**: a `std::vector<Staged>` keyed by actor id
in place of the `speaker*` set - geometry, textures, meshes, face, and a pose
SOURCE resolved per frame: (a) the running scene program whose
`Started.actor` is this actor (clip + path + offset, the existing code moved
into a per-character function), else (b) the conversation line's `.3DM` when
this actor is its speaker (the face too), else (c) the idle: the bank's
default state clip at frame 0, stood at the placement's pos/facing seated on
the walkable floor. The texture pool becomes `worldTex + each staged
character's textures` with a per-character material base, the same scheme as
`worldTexBase`. In adventure mode the controller's body stands in for the
player's id. Confirmed by RENDERING (a frame during `A_2_DemonLook` with the
Demon at 7605 -80 2980 and Kay'l both drawn) and by the summary line
counting staged bodies; the headless half is 40's check.

`todo/options-config.md`:

```md
# Graphical options, first as a config file

A reader's ask: skybox/fog and the graphical options (detail, crowd density,
...), "first with a config file, options menu is for later".

The two turned out to be one topic. Rows **3, 4, 5, 6 and 7** of the game's own
options table are *Distance de clipping*, *Affichage du ciel*, *Affichage des
ombres*, *Niveau d'activité dans les rues* and *Niveau de détail* - so the sky
and the clip/fog distance ARE option rows, and building either without the
option plumbing means building its toggle twice.

## The schema is the game's, not ours

**`GetPrivateProfileStringA` is not only the `.TAG` logger.** The engine reads
a `[Preferences]` section - 65 keys - and also `[Debug]` and `[User]` (with an
`id`, and per-developer names ANTOINE, CHRISTOPHE, FABIEN, FRANCOIS, GUEST,
MANU, OLIVIER). No `.ini` ships in `gamedata/`, so there is nothing to read
from a real install; what the binary gives us is the **key names**, which is
what a config file should use rather than anything invented here.

The 65 are in `verify.py: preferences keys`. The ones this topic wants:

| key | what |
|---|---|
| `clipdistance` | option row 3, choices 25 / 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 |
| `displaysky` | option row 4, Non/Oui |
| `displayshadows` | option row 5, Non/Oui - **read and drawn 2026-09-08**, `ASSETS` 4d |
| `SoftwareMode`, `GFXCard`, `screen_x`, `screen_y`, `window` | the device rows 2 and 8 |
| `music`, `DialogAttenuation`, `FxAttenuation`, `AmbientAttenuation` | the audio rows 10-12 |
| `displayframerate`, `debug_zones`, `display_path`, `viewer`, ... | the debug set |

**Two settings have no ini key**: the crowd density (row 6) and the level of
detail (row 7). `displaypassersclock` is a DEBUG display, not the density - the
labels mislead, and the exact strings had to come out of the data section
rather than IDA's truncated names (`aDisplaypassers` is really
`displaypassersclock`, `aAmbientattenua` is `AmbientAttenuation`). Their
apply-hooks write globals; density's is the one `Slider_Init` reads as
`39 * (5 - density) * h[3]`.

**They are not menu-only, though - this file said so and was wrong.** Having no
ini key is not the same as not persisting. The **save file's 3496-byte header
is the settings block**, and the density and the level of detail are two bytes
of it (GAME_STATE 8a, `verify.py: settings block`). So the game keeps its
options in **two** places, not one, and a port needs to know which is which:

| | the `.ini` | the save header |
|---|---|---|
| what | 65 `[Preferences]` keys, `[Debug]`, `[User]` | 21 fields + the three binding tables |
| written by | the installer / by hand | `Game_WriteSave`, on **every** slot save |
| read by | `GetPrivateProfileStringA` at boot | `SaveDir_Load`, behind the `OMK_SAVE` magic |
| holds | boot and device settings, and 3 of the 5 graphical rows | all 74 option rows' state |

They overlap: `clipdistance`, `displaysky` and `displayshadows` are in both.
The ini is what the game boots with and the header is what the options menu
edits, so the header is the LATER of the two and wins for anything a player has
touched. There is one header for all 256 slots.

Which is why the two shipped saves are evidence and not just fixtures: they
differ in exactly two of those 3496 bytes, and both are settings a player
changed - clip distance 200 against 150, crowd density 4 against 3.

## Steps

| # | step | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the reader: `[Preferences]` with the game's own key names | **DONE** 2026-09-05 |
| 2 | wire what the port already has - density, clipdistance | **DONE** 2026-09-05 |
| 2b | read the settings out of a save header too, and let it win | **DONE**, with step 2 |
| 3 | the sky: establish whether one exists in the data at all | **DONE** 2026-09-05 - and drawn |
| 4 | fog | **DONE** 2026-09-05 - drawn, both backends |
| 5 | the SHADOWS, row 5 - and row 7's level of detail, which says how many | **DONE** 2026-09-08 - read (`Actor_DrawShadow` 0x00467E20) and drawn; `docs/ASSETS.md` 4d |

Step 3 is research and may end in "narrowed": `PORTING` records that fog has
**no reachable evidence tier**, because the captures cannot validate pixel
values. The one hard datum so far points at no sky in an interior - the
dialog-402 captures are black where the render has holes, "because the game
does not clear to a sky either" - but that is an apartment and says nothing
about a street.

**That sentence about fog needs splitting in two, and step 2 is what split
it.** PORTING's ruling is about a pixel's VALUE, and it stands. The fog's
EXISTENCE and its parameters are a different question and they are now read
out of the code, at the same decision level as the blend modes already ported:
the game draws **linear** fog (`D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGTABLEMODE` = 3) at density
1.0, from `clipdistance x 39.37 x 0.25` to `clipdistance x 39.37`, coloured
from the scene's `+336` through `FOGCOLOR`, skipped for key bits `0x2080` and
doubled for `0x800`. So step 4 is not research any more - it is a renderer
change with a written spec, and only its APPEARANCE stays untestable.


## Step 4, done - the list is finished

The fog is drawn, in both backends, and the reading turned up the thing the
step actually hinged on: **the fog colour is BLACK**.

`Scene_Load3DO` memsets the scene object and `sub_44E830` then writes
`a1[84] = 0` - which is `+336`, the fog colour - explicitly, and nothing else
in the decompilation writes that field on a scene. (Three greps hit `+336`;
all three are other structs at the same offset, the collision CLAUDE.md 1
warns about.) So the shipped fog DARKENS toward the horizon rather than hazing
it - which is what a domed city at night wants, and what hides the hard edge
step 2's clip distance would otherwise leave. The two go together, and that is
why they were one piece of plumbing.

One mode colours it: `dword_93082C == 1` gives R 40, G 80, B 64 (a murky
green) with a 15.0 m clip distance, entered when a camera with flag 0x800
passes a player-derived height and flagging the player's own node. Consistent
with underwater; recorded as a reading, not a finding.

Implementation: the fog is a field of the renderer boundary's `View`, and the
two bucket-key exclusions (0x2080 unfogged, 0x800 doubled) are applied where
the key is - `renderer.cpp` and `vkrender.cpp`, the same rule in both. On
Anekbah at a 25 m clip it moves 42.9% of the Vulkan frame and 46.1% of the
software one. `--fog 0|1`, `--fog-colour r,g,b`.

`verify.py: engine fog` measures a white quad at ten known depths through the
boundary, so no set's geometry is in the answer; shown to fail three ways -
the end read from the 0.95 split, the 0x800 doubling dropped, and the 0x2080
exclusion forgotten.

**A note on how long this took to find.** All four steps' screenshots were
rendered through VULKAN without my noticing - the viewer picks it up by
default on this machine - so the software fog measured 0 changed pixels for
several rounds while being perfectly correct. The lesson is CLAUDE.md 5's,
one level out: when a render does not change, check WHICH renderer ran before
checking the code.

## Step 3, done - and the answer is yes

A sky exists, ships, and is now drawn. It is **not** a skybox or a dome: it is
a flat painted CEILING, 864 corners in a 12x12 grid with every vertex at
Y = 401.09, scaled 12.5x and hung 2250 units up, following the camera in x and
z and never in y. Which is what a domed city has.

The AREA chunk's `+133` names it and 17 of the 259 areas do; 242 name none,
which is what interiors should look like. Six models ship, plus a seventh
(`jansky`) that nothing names. The single texture on each is called `ciel1` or
`ciel2` and one mesh is `TOITCIEL`, so the files name themselves and no
inference was needed.

The mechanism is in `docs/ASSETS.md`, "The sky". One detail matters beyond this
step: `Area_LoadMiscModel` sets mesh flag `0x10000`, whose line in
`Render_SubmitMesh` is an ASSIGNMENT (`state = 0x800`) rather than an OR — so
the sky's bucket state is exactly 0x800, which keeps it out of the far bucket
AND doubles its fog range. Step 4 needs that.

Drawn in `omk-play`, off with `--sky 0`; turning row 4 off moves 6.3% of the
frame on Anekbah's street start. `verify.py: the sky`, shown to fail by reading
`+134` instead of `+133` and by making the probe report a non-flat plane.

## Step 2, done

**One option turned out to size four things.** The clip distance is in METRES
and the world unit is an inch, so the engine converts with 39.37007874015748
and hands `D` to `sub_440BE0(scene, D, 1)`, which writes `+340 = D`,
`+328 = D*0.25` and `+332 = D*0.95`. Those are, in order: `sub_48D3B0`'s
visible-set radius **and** the fog END; `bucketKey`'s nearSplit **and** the fog
START; and `bucketKey`'s farSplit. (The fog ends at `D`, not at the 0.95 split
- two different numbers, and reading the wrong one is a silent 5%.) The full
chain is in `docs/ASSETS.md`, "Where the two splits come from".

`engine/src/platform/settings.h` resolves the three sources in the engine's own
order - defaults from `sub_41F4C0`, then `[Preferences]`, then the save
header - and records which one supplied each field, because a setting that
silently came from the wrong place shows up only as "the config file does
nothing". The two rows with no ini key keep this port's own `[Options]`
section, at the ini's precedence level, so a save still wins.

**And a third section, `[Enhancements]`, for what the original never had**
(2026-09-08, the reader's rule: anything not in the original stays optional,
behind a launch flag or a config category of its own). Its first key is
`antialiasing = N` — MSAA on the Vulkan backend, `--aa N` on the command
line, OFF by default, which the software reference ignores because the
original's ANTIALIAS state is explicitly off (`docs/ASSETS.md` 4). Nothing
in the save header can carry it. `verify.py: engine: anti-aliasing`.
The second key is `texturefiltering = nearest|bilinear|trilinear`
(`--filter M`) with `anisotropy = N` (`--anisotropy N`), and
`uiscaling = nearest|linear` (`--ui-scaling M`) filters the interface's own
stretch, and `clipdistance = 0` lifts row 3's cap altogether (`--clip 0`),
same rules; `todo/enhancements.md` carries the list. The last one is
measured there and buys no pixel at the option's own 200 m maximum, in any
of the four cities.

Wired: **the crowd density** goes to `Session::setStreetActivity`, and **the
clip distance** drives a real visible-set walk in `omk-play` - the distance
half of `sub_48D3B0`, run per set mesh over runs of consecutive corners
precomputed at the load. Anekbah's five choices give 68 / 242 / 565 / 902 /
1264 mesh runs drawn of 1632, and an absurd distance culls 0. The four SIDE
planes are deliberately left out: they are the camera's business rather than
the option's, and a wrong plane sign deletes the world silently.

Two things worth knowing from doing it:

* **the density is a SPACING, not a count** (`39 * (5 - level) * h[3]`), and
  the walker pool caps at 200 - so on Anekbah levels 2, 3 and 4 all saturate
  and only level 0 (138 walkers) looks different. The port is faithful; the
  option simply has less room than its five labels suggest.
* **the clip distance without the fog looks wrong**, and that is the argument
  for step 4. At 25 m the far buildings are gone behind a hard black edge -
  which is exactly the edge `FOGEND = clipdistance` exists to hide.

`omk-play --config <ini>` and `--clip <metres>`; a `--save`'s header supplies
both otherwise, and an explicit flag beats both. `verify.py: settings
resolve`, shown to fail with the precedence inverted and with the fog end read
from the 0.95 split.

## Step 1, done

`engine/src/platform/options.*` reads an ini the way the Win32 profile API
does - case-insensitive sections and keys, `;`/`#` comments, a missing file
falling back rather than failing - and carries the 65 `[Preferences]` key
names. `Non`/`Oui` are understood beside `0`/`1`, since that is what the
French build's menu writes. A key under `[Preferences]` the engine never reads
is REPORTED, because a typo in a hand-written file is otherwise silent.

`verify.py: options file` asserts the 65 the binary reads, that the port's
table is the same SET and not merely the same size, and the reader's behaviour
on a file with a `[User]` section, mixed case, a French `Non`, a comment and a
misspelt key. Shown to fail by misspelling one key in the port's table: the
counts stay 65 and 65 while the set comparison goes False.

Nothing is wired to the engine yet - that is step 2.

## 1. The handler, read

`tables/vm_opcodes.json` gives op 92 handler **0x00404590**, length 2, tag
`OBJECTS`. It has no `proc` label and is not in `readable/` or `Runtime.exe.c`
(the CLAUDE.md §1 trap — nothing calls it, it is a dword in the dispatch table),
so it was read with `python3 tools/asmfn.py --op 92`. In order:

| step | the assembly | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mov dl,[eax]` / `mov dh,[eax-1]` / `movsx esi,si`; `test esi,4000h` → `movsx esi,[eax+esi*2+2]` | one int16 operand, the usual `0x4000` indirect bit through the parameter block at `ctx+0x24` |
| 2 | `mov eax, dword_6A05E0` … `jnz loc_404779`, with `or byte [ecx+28h],10h` before it | **`g_ScriptDryRun` skips the whole handler**, announcement included. The `ctx+0x28 |= 0x10` bit is set either way |
| 3 | `push offset aObjects` / `push esi` / `call sub_40EC70` | `Dbg_LogTagged(id, "OBJECTS")` — the announcement the golden traces record |
| 4 | `cmp esi,0FFFFFFFFh; jz` | `-1` returns before anything is read |
| 5 | `push esi; call sub_409AE0` | `ObjectRecord_Read(id)` → the 1304-byte `IAM\OBJECT` record in `ebx` |
| 6 | `mov eax,[dword_930724+194h]`; `cmp eax,3` / `cmp eax,0Fh` → `sprintf(buf,"{C}%s",ebx+118h)`, else a `rep movsb` of the same field | the SUBTITLE, from `rec+280` (the description). `+0x194` on `g_PlayerActorRec` is int slot **101 = `ACTOR_STATE`**, so the `{C}` prefix is conditional on the player being in state 3 or 15 |
| 7 | `lea esi,[ebx+0Eh]`; `sprintf(dword_4E6C30,"%s.ADP",esi)` | **the stem is `rec+14`** |
| 8 | `if (dword_93072C && dword_4E6C88) { I2D_FreeBitmap; clear both; [player+194h] = 1 }` | a media bitmap already up is torn down first, and the player leaves the image state |
| 9 | `cmp word ptr [ebx+2],10h; jnz loc_404701` → `sub_40BB40(stem)`, `sprintf("IMAGES\\%s")`, `I2D_LoadBitmap`, `[player+194h] = 0Ah` | **kind 16 is a DOCUMENT**: a full-screen bitmap and `ACTOR_STATE` **10** (`ImageScreen`, `src/actor/state.h:68`). `sub_40BB40` appends the constant at `0x004C0D24` = `".BMP"`. **This arm plays no audio at all** |
| 10 | `repne scasb` … `cmp ecx,4; jbe loc_404763` | `strlen(name) <= 4` is REFUSED — an empty stem builds `".ADP"` and nothing plays |
| 11 | `cmp eax,544F565Ah` (`'ZVOT'`) / `cmp eax,504F565Ah` (`'ZVOP'`) → copy the 13 bytes at `0x004C0868` over the name | **the substitution.** `dd 474E494Ah, 3346464Fh, 5044412Eh, db 0` = **`"JINGOFF3.ADP"`**. A raw dword compare, so it is **case-sensitive** |
| 12 | `push offset dword_4E6C30; call sub_41B200` | the play |
| 13 | `Mem_Free(rec)`; `Subtitle_Show(unk_4E6268)` | |

And `sub_41B200` (`readable/src/04_sys.c:5869`) is **not the sound bank**:

```c
if (byte_91030C)                       /* the audio system is up */
{
    Morph_Stop();                      /* <- ONE media voice at a time */
    Morph_ResetTracks(0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    sub_42BC10(0); sub_42CC30(1);
    Morph_SetAudioFormat(0x5640u, 1u, 30);   /* 22080 Hz, MONO, 30 fps */
    sprintf(Buffer, "VOICEOFF\\%s", a1);
    Morph_Start(Buffer, 0);
}
```

A voice-over goes through the **morph streamer** — the same one a `.3DM`
dialogue line uses — with no morph tracks, one channel. The leading
`Morph_Stop` is why the port keeps one handle and stops the previous shot.
`byte_91030C` is the audio-system flag, set in `Game_Init` and also gating
`Music_PlayTrack`; the port ignores it for the same reason `MusicPlayer` does.

The other caller of `sub_41B200` is `Game_HandleEvent` **case 47**
(`readable/src/01_file.c:1844`): reading a document shows `rec+280` with an
`{I255000000}` colour prefix and plays **`JINGOFF2.ADP`**.

## 2. What the data then says — and the finding

**`docs/CUTSCENES.md` §5 and `verify.py: cutscene music` say the cutscene voices
"cannot be played from this tree". The two numbers they rest on are right and
the conclusion is wrong.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ZVO objects (`IAM\OBJECTS.TAG` name begins `ZVO`) | **561** |
| …whose `+14` stem names a shipped `gamedata/VOICEOFF` file | **10** |
| …whose stem begins `ZVOT`/`ZVOP`, so the engine plays **`JINGOFF3.ADP`** | **520** |
| …genuinely silent: no file, no substitution | **31** |
| files in `gamedata/VOICEOFF` | **17** |

`JINGOFF3.ADP` ships (22949 bytes) and is **real audio, not silence**: 45898
mono samples, 2.082 s, peak 24889, rms 3463. It is the placeholder sting the
shipped build substitutes for an unrecorded line. So **530 of the 561 voice
objects produce audio in the original**, and the port now reproduces which.

Of the 17 files: 10 are named by an object stem, `JINGOFF2` and `JINGOFF3` by
the executable, and **five are orphans** no path the engine can build reaches —
`JINGOFF1.ADP`, `133205.ADP`, `ZVOPG001.ADP`, `ZVOU001.ADP`, `ZVOp201.adp`.
(The last two are interesting: `ZVOPG001` would be substituted away by its own
`ZVOP` prefix even if an object named it, and `ZVOp201`'s lowercase `p` would
*not* be — the compare is a dword.) They join `pluie.wav`, options page 12 and
the six dead spell recipes on the shipped-and-unreachable list.

**The Impasse cutscene's four voices all play**: 142 `ZVOD001` (3.36 s) and 141
`ZVOM010` (17.52 s) ship; 404 `ZVOT001` and 410 `ZVOT002` take the JINGOFF3
substitution (2.08 s each).

## 3. `media.play` announces — and the traces are a TIER-4 oracle for it

`tables/vm_announce.json` row 92: `{"domain": "OBJECTS", "field": 0}`. So yes,
op 92 announces, to `OBJECTS`, field 0, and the accessor a viewer polls is
**`Session::announced()`** (`src/script/area.h:370`), which is append-only —
`announced_` is never cleared — so a cursor is the whole mechanism.

**Better than expected**: `aObjects`, the literal the handler pushes, is at
**0x004C0844**, and the image contains **exactly one** `push offset aObjects`
(`Runtime.exe.asm:5528`; the address is fixed by the `aCS`/`aSAdp_0`/`aImagesS`
run between it and `dword_4C0868` at 0x4C0868). Every other `OBJECTS` announcer
pushes a different copy. So **a trace line naming `004c0844 "OBJECTS"` is
`media.play` and nothing else**, and the existing captures already carry the
engine's own media ids:

```
$ grep '004c0844 "OBJECTS"' traces/impasse-walk.log | ...
997 142 141 404 410 405 406 741 742 716 715 717 718 719 720 740 744 739 749
746 745 748 751 750 747 743 407 411 170 465 611 673 425 792 793 794
```

102 announcements across the eight non-empty traces, 56 distinct, **56 of 56**
resolving to a ZVO-tagged object through this rule. The Impasse cutscene's
first four after the ubiquitous 997 are **142, 141, 404, 410** — exactly the
task's four, in order. And its one kind-16 id, **715 "ZVO G001 TITRE"**, has
`gamedata/IMAGES/zvog001.bmp` on the disc: the document arm, exercised by a capture.

*(997 is `ZVO P660 Vide Pas Traduire` — "empty, do not translate" — and it
appears in every trace including `menu-noinput.log`. It has a `ZVOP` stem, so
the engine plays the jingle for it. Recorded, not explained away.)*

### 3a. THE ONE THING THE SESSION CANNOT TELL THE VIEWER — a proposed accessor

`omk::Announced` is `{std::string domain; std::int32_t value;}` and carries **no
opcode**, while **ten** opcodes announce to `OBJECTS`: 49, 50, 51, 52, 66, 67,
76, 77, **92**, 143. A domain-only filter would fire a voice on every
`inventory.add`.

**Minimal proposal for whoever owns `src/script/area.h` (T11, or wave B's
T16).** One defaulted field and one word at the push site — no other call site
changes, since `Announced{domain, value}` still aggregate-initialises:

```cpp
 struct Announced {
     std::string  domain;
     std::int32_t value = 0;
+    // WHICH handler narrated it. `Announced` was domain+value until a viewer
+    // needed to tell `media.play` (92) from the nine other opcodes that
+    // announce to OBJECTS; the golden traces distinguish them by the string
+    // LITERAL's address, which a port has no equivalent of.
+    std::uint8_t op = 0;
 };
```
```cpp
 // area.cpp, Session::record
-            announced_.push_back({it->second.domain, c.fields[f]});
+            announced_.push_back({it->second.domain, c.fields[f], c.op});
```

**Until that lands the port is not blocked, and the fallback is measured rather
than assumed.** `VoiceOverPlayer::poll` is a template with
`if constexpr (requires { a.op; })`: with the field it takes op 92 only and is
exact; without it, `domain == "OBJECTS"` plus a ZVO tag name. Over the whole
world-script corpus — both archives' zone scripts, their second tables and the
`+4` startup scripts — op 92 has **2605** sites and **all 2605** name a ZVO
object, while the other nine have **1584** between them and **exactly one**
names a ZVO object: `inventory.remove_all 111` ("ZVO P006 Rien Partic"), AREA 65
at pc 3564. **One false play in the whole shipped game**, named here so nobody
has to find it again. The template flips to exact with no caller change.

---

## 4. What was delivered

`omk::VoiceOverLibrary` — `IAM/OBJECT` (through the existing
`script/objects.h` reader) plus `IAM/OBJECTS.TAG` (a 25-line ini scan; the
handler never opens it, so it is optional and only `isVoiceObject` degrades).

* `resolve(fs, id) -> VoiceOver{object, objectName, stem, image, file,
  substituted, path, shipped}` — steps 4–11 above, in the handler's order;
* `decode(fs, tables, v) -> std::vector<int16_t>` — mono, 22050, via the
  existing `adpcmDecode`; `decodeById` for a one-line caller;
* `zvoObjects/shippedVoices/jingleVoices/silentVoices/voiceFiles` — the five
  counts, **-1** (not 0) when no `.TAG` was loaded, so a check fails loudly;
* `isVoiceObject` / `taggedVoice` — the permissive and the strict form.

`omk::VoiceOverPlayer(lib).poll(announced)` — the newly announced media ids,
in order, once each.

`engine/tools/voice_probe.cpp`:

```
$ build/voice_probe ../fr ../tables
objects records 1002
counts zvo 561 shipped 10 jingle 520 silent 31 files 17
voice 142 stem ZVOD001 file ZVOD001.ADP substituted 0 shipped 1 image 0 samples 74014 seconds 3.357 fnv 4ad934f3 name "ZVO D001 T'attendais"
voice 141 stem ZVOM010 file ZVOM010.ADP substituted 0 shipped 1 image 0 samples 386352 seconds 17.522 fnv b5b45b6d name "ZVO M010 Agression"
voice 404 stem ZVOT001 file JINGOFF3.ADP substituted 1 shipped 1 image 0 samples 45898 seconds 2.082 fnv fcc6da1f name "ZVO T001"
voice 410 stem ZVOT002 file JINGOFF3.ADP substituted 1 shipped 1 image 0 samples 45898 seconds 2.082 fnv fcc6da1f name "ZVO T002"
poll got 2 142 404 repoll 0 cursor 4
```

It takes no output path and writes nothing, so there is no `safeOutputPath`
call to make; the only path it builds (`VOICEOFF/...`) is read through DataFs.

**TIER declared in three places (PORTING B2)**: `src/audio/voiceover.h`'s
header comment, the check docstring in §5, and the `engine/README.md` coverage
row in §8. **4** for the resolution (the traces' own media ids), **3** for the
decode (differenced against `tools/adp.py`), **2** for the corpus partition and
the filter's collision rate, **6** for the two arms the port resolves but does
not draw (the `{C}` subtitle, the kind-16 bitmap), and **no tier at all** for
loudness or placement — `Morph_Start` hands the buffer to DirectSound and that
law is the device's (B5).

## 5. The check — `verify.py: engine voice over`

Runs in **0.46 s**. Paste as-is; it needs nothing from verify.py beyond
`ROOT`, `os`, `re`, `sys`, `glob`, `struct`, `subprocess` and `O`
(`omkdata`), all of which are already at module scope.

```python
def c_engine_voice_over():
    r"""`engine/`'s VOICE-OVER path - VM opcode 92 `media.play` (`voice_probe`).

    A cutscene's spoken lines are not in its scene data: a world script fires
    `media.play <OBJECTS id>` and handler **0x00404590** turns that object's
    `IAM\OBJECT` record into a file name. The port now does the same, so the
    viewer can play them.

    THE RULE, read from the assembly (`tools/asmfn.py --op 92`) in the order
    the handler applies it:

      * `if (g_ScriptDryRun) return;` - a dry-run pass does not even announce;
      * `Dbg_LogTagged(id, "OBJECTS")`, then `if (id == -1) return;`
      * `rec = ObjectRecord_Read(id)`, and the SUBTITLE from `rec+280`, with a
        `{C}` prefix when the player's `ACTOR_STATE` is 3 or 15;
      * `sprintf(name, "%s.ADP", rec+14)` - **the stem at +14**;
      * `if (rec[+2] == 16)` - kind 16 is a DOCUMENT: `IMAGES\<stem>.BMP`
        (the ".BMP" constant is at 0x004C0D24), `I2D_LoadBitmap`, and the
        player goes to `ACTOR_STATE` **10**, `ImageScreen`. No audio at all;
      * else `if (strlen(name) <= 4) skip` - an empty stem gives ".ADP" and
        is refused - and then, if the name's first four bytes are `ZVOT` or
        `ZVOP` (a raw dword compare, so case-sensitive), the first 13 are
        overwritten with the constant at **0x004C0868**, which is
        `"JINGOFF3.ADP"`;
      * `sub_41B200(name)`: `Morph_Stop()`, `Morph_SetAudioFormat(0x5640, 1,
        30)` - 22080 Hz, **MONO** - `sprintf("VOICEOFF\\%s")`, `Morph_Start`.
        So a voice-over goes through the MORPH streamer, not the sound bank,
        and the leading `Morph_Stop` is why there is one media voice at a time.

    **The substitution is the finding, and it revises `cutscene music` above.**
    That check asserts 561 ZVO objects with 10 shipped files and concludes the
    voices "cannot be played from this tree". 561 and 10 are right; the
    conclusion is not. **520 of the 561 have a ZVOT/ZVOP stem**, so the engine
    plays `JINGOFF3.ADP` for them - which ships, and is a 2.08 s sting, not
    silence (peak 24889, rms 3463 over 45898 samples). Only **31** are
    genuinely silent. 10 + 520 + 31 = 561, and the partition is asserted here.

    TIER (PORTING B1/B2), declared here, in `src/audio/voiceover.h` and in the
    `engine/README.md` coverage row:

      * **4** for the resolution. `media.play` is one of the 49 announcing
        handlers and its `"OBJECTS"` literal, `aObjects` at **0x004C0844**, has
        exactly ONE `push offset` in the image (Runtime.exe.asm:5528) - so a
        trace line naming that address is `media.play` and nothing else. The
        captures therefore hand over the engine's own media ids: **102**
        announcements over the eight non-empty traces, **56 distinct**, and
        **56 of 56** resolve to a ZVO-tagged object through this rule.
        `traces/impasse-walk.log` opens the Impasse cutscene with
        **142, 141, 404, 410** in that order, which is what the port has to
        play, and its one kind-16 id (**715**, "ZVO G001 TITRE") has its
        `gamedata/IMAGES/zvog001.bmp` on disc - the document arm, exercised by the
        capture.
      * **3** for the decode: the four FNV-1a hashes below are over the decoded
        int16 stream and are re-derived by `tools/adp.py` here. B1's warning
        applies in full - both sides descend from one reading of `sub_483200` -
        but note WHAT it catches, because the third mutation below is exactly
        that case: mono and stereo produce the SAME sample count and different
        hashes.
      * **2** for the corpus partition and for the announcement filter's
        measured collision rate.
      * **6** for the two arms the port does not perform: the `{C}` subtitle
        and the kind-16 bitmap are resolved and reported, and nothing draws
        them.

    THE ANNOUNCEMENT FILTER, and its one known false positive. `Session::
    announced()` carries a `.TAG` domain and a value and **no opcode**, and TEN
    opcodes announce to `OBJECTS` (49, 50, 51, 52, 66, 67, 76, 77, 92, 143). So
    `VoiceOverPlayer` falls back to `domain == "OBJECTS"` plus a ZVO tag name,
    which is measured rather than assumed: over the whole world-script corpus
    (both archives' zone scripts, second tables and `+4` startup scripts) op 92
    has **2605** sites and **all 2605** name a ZVO object, while the other nine
    have **1584** between them and **exactly one** names a ZVO object -
    `inventory.remove_all 111` ("ZVO P006 Rien Partic") in AREA 65 at pc 3564.
    One false play in the shipped game. `todo/pending/E1.md` proposes the
    one-field `Announced::op` that makes it exact.

    SHOWN TO FAIL (B4). Three mutations of `src/audio/voiceover.cpp`, each
    built and run through this check:

      * **the stem offset** - `r.stem` (+14) replaced by `r.name` (+24), which
        is what "read the record's next string" looks like. Every ZVO record's
        +24 is EMPTY, so the built name is ".ADP", the length refusal fires,
        and the counts go `shipped 10 -> 0`, `jingle 520 -> 0`,
        `silent 31 -> 561`; all four Impasse voices decode 0 samples.
      * **the JINGOFF3 substitution** dropped - `jingle 520 -> 0`,
        `silent 31 -> 551`, and 404/410 resolve to `ZVOT001.ADP` /
        `ZVOT002.ADP`, which do not ship: 45898 samples -> 0. This is the
        mutation that puts the check back on `cutscene music`'s old story.
      * **stereo instead of mono** - every sample COUNT is unchanged (the codec
        yields two samples a byte either way) and every FNV moves:
        `4ad934f3 -> 8547d932`, `b5b45b6d -> 952e87aa`,
        `fcc6da1f -> 450febed`. A count-only assertion cannot see this, which
        is why the hash is here.
    """
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    fr = omkpaths.data_root()
    if not (os.path.isdir(eng) and os.path.isdir(fr)):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ or gamedata/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "voice_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"
    r = subprocess.run([binp, fr, os.path.join(ROOT, "tables"), "142", "141",
                        "404", "410", "715"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return ("no run",), ("ran",), "voice_probe must run"
    L, voices = {}, {}
    for ln in r.stdout.splitlines():
        f = ln.split()
        if not f:
            continue
        if f[0] == "voice":
            voices[int(f[1])] = f
        else:
            L[f[0]] = f
    def g(key, *idx):
        f = L.get(key, [])
        return tuple(f[i] if i < len(f) else None for i in idx)
    def v(oid, *keys):
        f = voices.get(oid, [])
        return tuple(f[f.index(k) + 1] if k in f else None for k in keys)

    # ---- the independent side: the same rule in Python --------------------
    import adp, dialog_triggers as T, dialog_disasm as D
    d = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "gamedata/IAM/OBJECT"), "rb").read()
    tags = O.TAGS["OBJECTS"]
    zvo = [i for i in range(len(d) // 2048) if (tags.get(i) or "").startswith("ZVO")]
    stem = lambda i: d[i * 2048 + 14:i * 2048 + 24].split(b"\0")[0].decode("cp1252")
    vo = {f.upper() for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(ROOT, "gamedata/VOICEOFF"))}
    jingle = [i for i in zvo if stem(i)[:4] in ("ZVOT", "ZVOP")]
    ship = [i for i in zvo if i not in jingle and (stem(i).upper() + ".ADP") in vo]
    pyc = (len(zvo), len(ship), len(jingle),
           len(zvo) - len(ship) - len(jingle), len(vo))

    def fnv(b):
        h = 2166136261
        for x in b:
            h = ((h ^ x) * 16777619) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        return "%08x" % h
    def pcm(fn):
        raw, _ch = adp.decode(
            open(os.path.join(ROOT, "gamedata/VOICEOFF", fn), "rb").read(), False)
        return str(len(raw) // 2), fnv(raw)

    # ---- the corpus: who announces OBJECTS, and about what ----------------
    FIELD = {49: 1, 50: 1, 51: 1, 52: 1, 66: 0, 67: 1, 76: 0, 77: 0, 92: 0, 143: 0}
    zset = set(zvo)
    m92 = mzvo = other = ozvo = 0
    for name in ("AREA", "SCENE"):
        for k, b in sorted(T.archive(os.path.join(ROOT, "gamedata/IAM", name)).items()):
            rr = T.LAYOUT[name](b)
            ps = []
            if rr:
                ps += [p for _rec, _f, p in T._scripts_from_records(b, rr[0], rr[1])]
                ps += [p for _rec, _f, p in T._second_table(name, b)]
            s4 = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 4)[0] if len(b) > 8 else 0
            if s4:
                ps.append(s4)          # the chunk's +4 startup script
            for p in ps:
                ops, st = D.disasm(b, p, len(b))
                if st != "ok":
                    continue
                for _pc, op, raw in ops:
                    if op not in FIELD:
                        continue
                    f = FIELD[op]
                    if len(raw) < 2 * (f + 1):
                        continue
                    val = struct.unpack_from("<h", raw, 2 * f)[0]
                    if op == 92:
                        m92 += 1
                        mzvo += val in zset
                    else:
                        other += 1
                        ozvo += val in zset

    # ---- the traces: the engine's own media ids (tier 4) ------------------
    #
    # `aObjects` at 0x004C0844 has ONE `push offset` in the image, so this
    # address is `media.play` and no other OBJECTS announcer.
    pat = re.compile(r'004c0844 "OBJECTS",[0-9a-f]+ "(-?[0-9]+)"')
    tid, impasse = [], []
    for fn in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "traces", "*.log"))):
        got = [int(m.group(1)) for ln in open(fn, errors="replace")
               for m in [pat.search(ln)] if m]
        tid += got
        if fn.endswith("impasse-walk.log"):
            impasse = got
    tzvo = sum(1 for i in set(tid) if i in zset)
    head = tuple(impasse[1:5])         # after the 997 nearly every trace opens with

    got = (
        g("counts", 2, 4, 6, 8, 10),
        pyc,
        v(142, "file", "samples", "fnv"),
        v(141, "file", "samples", "fnv"),
        v(404, "file", "substituted", "samples", "fnv"),
        v(410, "file", "substituted", "samples", "fnv"),
        v(715, "image", "file", "samples"),
        g("poll", 2, 3, 4, 6, 8),
        (m92, mzvo, other, ozvo),
        (len(tid), len(set(tid)), tzvo, head),
    )
    want = (
        ("561", "10", "520", "31", "17"),
        (561, 10, 520, 31, 17),
        ("ZVOD001.ADP",) + pcm("ZVOD001.adp"),
        ("ZVOM010.ADP",) + pcm("ZVOM010.adp"),
        ("JINGOFF3.ADP", "1") + pcm("JINGOFF3.ADP"),
        ("JINGOFF3.ADP", "1") + pcm("JINGOFF3.ADP"),
        ("1", "-", "0"),
        ("2", "142", "404", "0", "4"),
        (2605, 2605, 1584, 1),
        (102, 56, 56, (142, 141, 404, 410)),
    )
    return got, want, \
        "the ZVO partition (objects, shipped, JINGOFF3-substituted, silent) " \
        "and the VOICEOFF file count; the two Impasse voices that ship and " \
        "the two that take the jingle, sample-exact against tools/adp.py; " \
        "the kind-16 document arm playing nothing; the announcement filter " \
        "consuming each id once; media.play sites, all naming a ZVO object, " \
        "against the other nine OBJECTS opcodes' single collision; and the " \
        "golden traces' own media ids, with the Impasse cutscene's first four"
```

Restored and re-run: `OK`. **The binary was relinked for every mutation** — the

## 6. The `play.cpp` hook (E2 owns the file)

Three additions. **Where**: `engine/backends/sdl/play.cpp`, in the viewer's
frame loop, immediately **after** the `session.musicTrack()` block that follows
`session.frame()` (~line 1680 as the file stands) — the same place music is
polled, and after the frame so a script that fires `media.play` this frame is
heard this frame.

```cpp
// (a) with the other includes, near "audio/music.h"
#include "audio/voiceover.h"
```

```cpp
// (b) beside `adpcmTables` / `music`, once, before the loop
omk::VoiceOverLibrary voiceLib;
voiceLib.load(fs);
omk::VoiceOverPlayer voices(voiceLib);
int voiceShot2 = -1;              // the ONE media voice, per Morph_Stop
```

```cpp
// (c) THE HOOK - right after the music block
//
// `media.play` is an EVENT, not a level like music: each announcement is one
// play, and `sub_41B200` opens with `Morph_Stop()`, so a second one CUTS the
// first. That is the whole of the engine's policy here.
for (const int mediaId : voices.poll(session.announced())) {
    const auto vo  = voiceLib.resolve(fs, mediaId);
    const auto pcm = voiceLib.decode(fs, adpcmTables, vo);
    std::printf("media.play %d (%s) -> %s%s, %.2f s\n", mediaId,
                vo.objectName.c_str(),
                vo.file.empty() ? (vo.image ? "IMAGES\\" : "nothing")
                                : vo.file.c_str(),
                vo.substituted ? " [JINGOFF3 substitution]" : "",
                static_cast<double>(pcm.size()) / omk::kAdpcmRate);
    front.stopSound(voiceShot2);
    voiceShot2 = pcm.empty() ? -1
        : front.playSound(resampleToDevice(pcm, 1, omk::kAdpcmRate, 44100));
}
```

Notes for whoever lands it:

* **keep the handle**, and stop it where a new area or a conversation starts —
  `front.stopSound(voiceShot2); voiceShot2 = -1;` beside the existing
  `session.loadArea(...)` call and beside the dialogue's own
  `front.stopSound(voiceShot)`. A voice-over and a dialogue line are two
  different shots and the engine would never have both: `Morph_Stop` is one
  player.
* **`voices.skip(session.announced())` right after `session.loadArea(...)`** if
  the backlog of an area's startup announcements should not all fire at once.
* `resampleToDevice(pcm, 1, ...)` — **channels is 1**. `Morph_SetAudioFormat`
  says mono, and `resampleToDevice` duplicates it to both device channels.
* the `printf` is the useful half while there is no subtitle layer: it names
  the object, the file and whether the jingle was substituted.

## 9. A paragraph for `docs/CUTSCENES.md` — REPLACING the "missing voices" text

The current §"Music, and the missing voices" says the voices "cannot be played
from this tree" and cites 10 of 561. Suggested replacement for that paragraph
(the music paragraph above it is untouched and still correct):

> **The voices are mostly PLACEHOLDERS, and that is a decision in the engine
> rather than a gap in the tree.** `media.play` (op 92, handler `0x00404590`)
> builds `<rec+14>.ADP` from the `IAM\OBJECT` record its `OBJECTS` operand
> names, and then does one more thing before playing it: **if the name's first
> four bytes are `ZVOT` or `ZVOP` it overwrites the first thirteen with the
> constant at `0x004C0868`, which is `"JINGOFF3.ADP"`.** The compare is a raw
> dword, so it is case-sensitive. That is **520 of the 561** ZVO objects, and
> `gamedata/VOICEOFF/JINGOFF3.ADP` ships — 45898 mono samples, 2.08 s, peak 24889,
> real audio and not silence. So the partition is **10 objects with their own
> shipped file, 520 that play the jingle, and 31 that are genuinely silent**;
> the earlier reading of this section had the first two numbers right and the
> conclusion wrong. The Impasse cutscene's four voices all sound: 142
> (`ZVOD001`, 3.36 s), 141 (`ZVOM010`, 17.52 s), and 404 / 410 (`ZVOT001` /
> `ZVOT002`) as the jingle.
>
> The play itself is not the sound bank. `sub_41B200` calls `Morph_Stop()`,
> `Morph_SetAudioFormat(0x5640, 1, 30)` — 22080 Hz, **mono**, 30 fps — and
> `Morph_Start("VOICEOFF\\<name>")`, so a voice-over runs through the same
> streamer a `.3DM` dialogue line does, with no morph tracks. The leading
> `Morph_Stop` means **one media voice at a time**: a second `media.play` cuts
> the first.
>
> Two arms of the same handler are not audio at all. A record of **kind 16** is
> a DOCUMENT: the handler builds `IMAGES\<stem>.BMP`, loads it as a full-screen
> bitmap and puts the player in `ACTOR_STATE` **10** (`ImageScreen`). And every
> call shows a SUBTITLE from the record's `+280` description, prefixed `{C}`
> when the player is in state 3 or 15. `traces/impasse-walk.log` exercises both
> paths: object **715** ("ZVO G001 TITRE") is kind 16 and
> `gamedata/IMAGES/zvog001.bmp` is on the disc.
>
> `gamedata/VOICEOFF` holds 17 files. Ten are named by an object stem, `JINGOFF2` (the
> document cue, `Game_HandleEvent` case 47) and `JINGOFF3` by the executable
> itself, and **five are orphans** — `JINGOFF1.ADP`, `133205.ADP`,
> `ZVOPG001.ADP`, `ZVOU001.ADP`, `ZVOp201.adp` — that no path the engine can
> build reaches, the `pluie.wav` shape of §3b in `docs/ASSETS.md`.
>
> `engine/src/audio/voiceover.{h,cpp}` ports all of this and
> `verify.py: engine voice over` asserts it, including against the golden
> traces' own `media.play` announcements. The dialogue voice remains a
> different thing and is present: per-frame ADPCM inside each line's `.3DM`.

`verify.py: cutscene music`'s docstring needs the same correction — its "That
is a fact about the data, not a gap in the reading" paragraph should gain a
sentence pointing at `engine: voice over` for the 520. **Its numbers do not
change** (561 and 10 are both still right), so only the prose moves.

## 10. One correction to a file I was not allowed to edit

`engine/src/script/objects.h`, the `+2 kind` comment, says:

```
//     +2    int16     kind   -1 voice-only pseudo-object (the 561 `ZVO` rows)
```

**That is wrong on both halves.** Over the 1002 records, `kind == -1` occurs
**34** times, not 561; and the 561 ZVO-tagged objects split
**526 kind 0 / 34 kind -1 / 1 kind 16**. The identity of a voice object is its
`IAM\OBJECTS.TAG` name, not `+2` — and `+2` matters to `media.play` only in
that **16 is the document arm**. Suggested:

```
//     +2    int16     kind   -1 and 0 carry no inventory behaviour (the 561
//                            ZVO voice rows are 526 of kind 0, 34 of -1 and
//                            one of 16); 1..6 guns, 7..11 their ammunition,
//                            12 seteks (money), 13 rings, 15/16 documents.
//                            `media.play` (op 92) branches on 16: a kind-16
//                            record is a full-screen `IMAGES\<stem>.BMP`
//                            rather than a `VOICEOFF\<stem>.ADP`.
```

## 11. What I could NOT establish

* **Whether `Announced` should grow `.op`, or a dedicated list.** §3a proposes
  the field; I could not measure the cost because `area.*` was T11's. The
  fallback is measured and the template flips with no caller change.
* **Why the subtitle is CENTRED in states 3 and 15.** `{C}` is settled —
  `docs/UI.md` line 1224 and `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` line 890 both give it as
  one of the four alignments, centring — so the handler centres the subtitle
  exactly when the player's `ACTOR_STATE` is 3 (shoot mode) or 15, and
  left-aligns it otherwise. **What is open is WHY those two states**: 3 is
  `Shoot_Enter`'s and 15 is not named in `src/actor/state.h`'s list beyond its
  number. I did not trace `Subtitle_Show` (`sub_41E040`) to see what else
  differs, and the port draws no subtitle, so nothing here depends on it.
* **Why object 997 ("ZVO P660 Vide Pas Traduire" — *empty, do not translate*)
  is announced in every capture, `menu-noinput.log` included.** It has a `ZVOP`
  stem, so the engine plays the 2 s jingle for a voice explicitly marked empty.
  Either it is a deliberate "clear the subtitle" call whose jingle is an
  accident of the substitution rule, or the substitution is narrower than the
  assembly reads. The assembly is unambiguous and the corpus cannot separate
  the two, so it is recorded, not resolved.
* **Whether the `strlen <= 4` refusal ever fires in the shipped game.** No ZVO
  object has an empty stem, so it is a dead branch against this corpus; ported
  anyway and recorded rather than trimmed.
* **How loud, and where.** `Morph_Start` hands the buffer to DirectSound; the
  attenuation and pan law has no reachable tier (PORTING B5), the same position
  the audio row already takes.

```

    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    if not os.path.isdir(eng) or not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "gamedata/ANIMS")):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ or gamedata/ANIMS absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s", "build/player_probe"], cwd=eng,
                       capture_output=True, text=True)

        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"

## 4. `docs/ASSETS.md` - text

Under "The walker - how an actor actually moves", a new bullet after the
`Walk_GroundResponse` one:

* **where the forward motion comes from - the CLIP.** `sub_45C680`
  (0x0045C680), the tail of `Cef_TickChannel`, case 1 (state 1 and 11..16):
  `sub_45CE90` -> `Anim_SetFrame(node, clip, prevFrame, frame, &d)` ->
  `Anim_RootDelta(clip, node+156, prev, cur)` sums the root's 12-byte
  position keys over `(prev, cur]` (fractional ends scaled: the head
  `(ceil(prev) - prev) * key[ceil(prev)]`, the whole keys, the tail
  `(cur - floor(cur)) * key[floor(cur)+1]`; both ends inside one key,
  `(cur - prev) * key[ceil(prev)]`) and rotates the sum by the 3x3 at
  node+156 - which is **actor+288, the facing matrix**
  `Matrix3x3_FromEulerAngles(+416,+420,+424)` rebuilt every frame in
  `Actors_TickAll` and installed on the node by `sub_437140(node,
  actor+288)` in `Actor_LoadModel`. The delta moves the node and is added to
  +244/+252 (and +248 only in states 11..14). `H1AVNT`'s `H_WALK` root
  carries 28 keys of 2.5-3.3 in/frame (2.1 m/s), `H_RUN` 20 of 7.4 (5.6
  m/s), `H_STAND` 1 (a sway); the root SHIFT blocks (0x80) are the
  phase-matched hand-overs between gaits (junction 11: run -> walk at
  -3.33/frame over frames 1..4) and the sidesteps. `Actor_ApplyMotion` then
  undoes the position delta since the last safe stance and hands it to
  `Actor_Move`, so the clip proposes and the collision disposes.
* **turning is the `.CTL`.** Left/right (word bits 0/1) open `H1AVNT`'s
  group-global entries 9/10 - a TURN `(0..1, 0, +-5, 0)` with flag 0x100,
  applied WHOLE by the walker-edge loop every tick the bit is held (5
  degrees a frame in place) - and, from `H_STAND`, the exact-match aliases
  19/20 into `H_SDLROT`/`H_SDRROT`, a turning clip whose window turn (flag
  0x40, 29_win32.c 330-410: the frames advanced inside `[start, end)` times
  the per-frame rate, through `Cef_ApplyTurn`) turns 4.75 degrees a frame.
  `Actor_ApplyMotion`'s 1/8-per-frame steer toward the motion direction is
  INERT for a root-driven walk: the delta was rotated by the facing it would
  steer toward.
* **nothing held is the idle word.** `sub_4A7A20` (0x004A7A20): `*word = 0;
  if (!held) *word = 0x40000000;` - and the stop edges are entries whose +4
  only FORBIDS bits (`0x20000` = `0x8000 << 2`, forward released), which
  `Cef_InputMatches` opens on any word without bit 2, the idle word
  included. The same function swaps bits 0 and 1 under channel flag 8 - the
  reverse gait reverses left and right.
* **the queue's lone idle is DROPPED**, 29_win32.c 306-312: before a
  pressed word is pushed, `if (n == 1 && (queue[0] & 0x40000000)) { queue[0]
  = 0; n = 0; }`, and under state flag 0x20000000 a queue longer than one is
  cut to one. `engine/src/actor/channel.cpp` carries neither (found
  2026-09-02 by the player controller, which shadows the first).

Under "The camera modes", after the table:

**How mode 0 follows, read from the tick** (`sub_417CF0`, 04_sys.c 3672,
and its two resolvers). `Camera_LoadParams` puts the preset's eye offset at
+176 and target offset at +124 when their subjects are not -1, the fov at
+48, and the three trailing shorts at +136 (`f42`), +188 (`f44`), +192
(`f46`). Every frame, for any mode but 13: the absolute slots are copied to
the live eye (+52) and target (+64); `sub_415D10` sets the target to
`subjectPos - R(subjectEuler) * targetOffset`, chasing it by `dt / f42` (1
-> 2; a snap while flags & 0x81); `sub_415E60` chases a private Euler triple
(+76) toward the subject's by `dt / f46`, snapping any component within 0.1
degrees, and sets the eye to `subjectPos - R(+76) * eyeOffset`, chasing by
`dt / f44`. `sub_414F30` supplies the subject: `+244..+252` and
`+416/+420/+424` of the actor at +144 (subject type 0). So mode 0's row -
`(0,0,-118.11) / (0,0,0) / 75 / 3, 8, 8` - is a target a third of the way
per frame, a yaw an eighth, and an eye an eighth of the way to 3.00 m behind
the lagged yaw. **Not read to the end**: `sub_414520` case 0 (`sub_413C00`)
gives the mode flags 4|8|0x10 and tunables (+312/+316 = -0.7 x the actor's
height at +276, +300 = 1.2, +320 = 8, +324 = 4); flag 8 runs `sub_417070`,
271 lines that ray-test from the target toward the eye (`sub_444810`) and
pull the camera in and up to 0.7 x height behind a wall; flag 0x10 runs
`sub_416450`, a floor clamp re-probed when the subject drops more than two
inches. A world camera whose eye subject is 0 takes the same path (case 12
-> LABEL_19), so SCENE 55's camera 0 - eye (-1, 26, -119), target just
ahead - IS a mode-0 camera with its own offsets. `engine/src/actor/player.h`
ports the resolve and the lag and labels the two passes unported.

## 6. For the channel's owner - `engine/src/actor/channel.cpp`

Two lines of `Cef_TickChannel`'s commit are missing from `CefChannel::tick`
(the block after `if (word != lastInput_)`), and one convention differs:

1. `LABEL_75` (29_win32.c 306-312): `if (n == 1 && (queue[0] &
   0x40000000)) { queue[0] = 0; n = 0; }` - a lone idle word is dropped
   before the push. Without it a pressed word queues BEHIND the idle word
   `setBankGroup`/`resetQueue` seed and the machine stalls until something
   pops it.
2. Under the CURRENT state's flag 0x20000000 with `n > 1`, the queue is cut
   to 1 (`count = 1`) instead of pushed.
3. `tick(dt, 0)` substitutes the queue front for a zero code. The engine's
   polled word is never 0 - `sub_4A7A20` makes it 0x40000000 when nothing is
   held - so a caller driving from a keyboard must pass `kIdleInput`; the
   controller does. The AI path is unaffected (it injects).

`PlayerController` shadows (1) - a reset counted in `stats().queueResets`, or
a pressed word that `findTransition` says opens an edge while no transition
happened, triggers `injectInput({word})` - and can drop the shadow when (1)
lands. `verify.py: engine actor states` cannot see either, since its sweep
injects.

## 7. For wave B - the zone scan

`PlayerController::pos()` (the feet, on the walker's floor) and `facing()`
(degrees, the +420 convention: forward `(sin y, -cos y)`) are plain
accessors; `euler()` is the triple. `Actor_TickNpc` calls `Actor_ScanZones`
after `Actor_ApplyMotion`, so the scan belongs after `tick()`. In `play.cpp`
the controller lives in `player` and `adventure` says whether it ticked
this frame.

## 8. What was seen

The deterministic chain, headless and software-rendered:

plays the intro and the whole Impasse cutscene unchanged (the seven editings

5773** - the beat `C_3_KaylsUp` ending, seven frames after the last editing
- prints

    ADVENTURE MODE - the player is HO1_FN (the DB player record) on H1AVNT
    (the DB player record); 1539/1595 tracks resolve; 105 walkable triangles
    of AIMPASSE; standing at 6705 -79 3191 facing 340 (from the last player

The snapshots (`engine/build/e2/snaps/snap-<frame>.png`, converted with

picture; which surface it is against the game's own frame is not checked.

```

# T1 — interpreter: division, the shared fetch on 8/14–17/71, `var.set.random`

Issues 1, 4, 20, 35 of `todo/iam-script-engine.md`. Files touched:
`engine/src/script/interp.h`, `engine/src/script/interp.cpp`, and the new
probe `engine/tools/vm_probe.cpp`. Nothing else was edited.

## 1. What changed

* **Division truncates** (`divTrunc`, replacing `divFloor`). Op 34's handler at
  `0x402750` pops the top into `eax`, the word under it into `edi`, and runs
  `cdq; idiv edi`; `var.div` (22, `0x402390`) runs `Var_Get(var)` over the
  popped top the same way. x86 `idiv` truncates toward zero. The two guards are
  the PORT's, labelled in the code: `b == 0` returns 0 and `INT_MIN / -1`
  returns the wrapped negation — both raise #DE in the engine, a crash rather
  than a decision.
* **The shared fetch on every 16-bit field.** `push.i16` (8, `0x401D70`),
  the variable index of 14/15/16 (`0x401F70`/`0x401FE0`/`0x402070`), both
  fields of 17 (`0x402110`) and both of 71 (`0x403950`) now go through
  `fetch16`. **Correction to the brief:** op 15's VALUE goes through the fetch
  as well — its handler runs `cmp ax,0FFFFh; test ah,40h; movsx eax, word ptr
  [ecx+eax*2+2]` a second time for the value — so a `set.var.i16` value can
  be indirect. Only 14's int8 and 16's int32 are read raw. The `interp.h`
  comment that named 4, 6, 10, 18, 42 as the only fetchers is rewritten.
* **The fetch's index is offset by one word — and that changes what issue 20
  says is pushed.** Every fetching handler reads
  `movsx eax, word ptr [block + eax*2 + 2]`: index 0 is the block's SECOND
  word. `Message_RunHandlers` (`0x00409420`) fills the 8-byte block as
  `args[0] = message id, args[1] = sender`, so `push.i16 0x4000` pushes the
  **sender**, not the message id. The corpus settles it independently: every
  one of the 59 shipped operands with the bit (see §4) is
  `push.i8/i16 <constant>; push.i16 0x4000; eq; jmp_if_false`, with constants
  such as 173, 346, 410 (actor ids, under message 3) and 3, 100, 10, 88
  (object ids, under message 4) — a script subscribed to message 3 has
  nothing to learn from the number 3. `tools/sim`'s docstring already says
  "offset by one element"; the port's `fetch16` now does `params_[i + 1]`, and
  `setParams` is documented as taking the block **as the engine fills it**,
  `{message id, sender}`. T2's message dispatch should pass exactly that.
* **`var.set.random` (120) implemented.** The real handler is at `0x405480`
  (the pre-split block is the function after it — CLAUDE.md §1's trap):
  three fetches — lo, hi, VARIABLE — then, unless the dry-run flag is set,
  `Var_Set(var, Random_NoRepeat(lo, hi))`. `Random_NoRepeat` (`0x0041D6B0`,
  `readable/src/05_sys.c`) returns lo when lo == hi and otherwise redraws
  `lo + rand() % (hi - lo + 1)` until it differs from `dword_4E7E8C`, the
  previous result. Ported as `Interpreter::randomNoRepeat` over a
  **process-global** xorshift32 and a process-global last draw — global
  because `rand()`'s seed and `dword_4E7E8C` are: the passer-by line one
  script drew is the one the next script cannot draw. `seedRandom(s)` is
  static, sets the state and forgets the last draw, so a seeded run is one
  fixed sequence (`o3de/particles.h`'s argument: WHERE randomness enters is
  ported, not which numbers). `hi < lo` returns lo — the port's choice where
  the engine takes a zero or negative modulus. The call is recorded as
  `{lo, hi, var}` (resolved) when `record_ && !recordAll_`, like 64/65/71.
* **`setRandomWrites(bool)`**, default on. Off, 120 records and does not
  write — the fourth "compare like with like" switch, and §3 says why it is
  needed.

## 3. The corpus sweep — and a decision for the coordinator

`run_scripts` (built privately, then from the shared tree once it compiled
again; both binaries print the same) against `tools/sim`, mirroring
`c_engine_scripts`'s comparison in a scratch script:

| run | slots | in order | status agree | end | dialog | calls cpp/py | DB identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random writes **off** | 5958/5958 | 5958 | 5958 | 5818 | 140 | 18584/18584 | **yes** |
| random writes **on** (default) | 5958/5958 | 5958 | 5939 | 5799 | 159 | 18728/18584 | no — 2 bytes, vars 113 and 119 |

So the division and the fetch changes agree with `tools/sim` over the whole
corpus — no shipped site divides a negative, and the 59 indirect operands
compare an absent parameter (0 here, 16384 in the sim) against an id and are
false either way. **Every one of the 197 diverging slots with writes on is a
script containing op 120** (attributed by decoding each one): 19 of them now
end at `dialog.start` instead of `end` — the passer-by lines the random branch
was never taking — and 144 more stubbed calls are recorded.

`verify.py: engine: scripts` will therefore FAIL after integration unless one
of these lands. Both are outside T1's files:

* **(a) one line in `engine/tools/run_scripts.cpp`**, in both `Interpreter`
  constructions: `vm.setRandomWrites(false);` beside
  `vm.setUiOpenSuspends(false);` (the private copy that produced the first row
  is exactly this). The check's numbers then stay
  `(5958, 5958, 5958, 5958, 5818, 140, 18584, 18584, True)`.
* **(b) the same generator in `tools/sim/vm.py`**, which is the stronger end
  state — the DB comparison would then cover the 256 random sites too. The
  transcription, module-level so it is one state per process as the port's is:

  ```python
  _RNG = [1]          # xorshift32; Interpreter::rng_
  _LAST = [0]         # dword_4E7E8C; Interpreter::lastRandom_

  def seed_random(s):
      _RNG[0] = s or 1; _LAST[0] = 0

  def random_no_repeat(lo, hi):
      """Random_NoRepeat 0x0041D6B0: in [lo, hi], never the previous draw."""
      if hi <= lo:
          _LAST[0] = lo; return lo
      n = hi - lo + 1
      while True:
          x = _RNG[0]
          x ^= (x << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF; x ^= x >> 17; x ^= (x << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
          _RNG[0] = x
          r = lo + (x >> 8) % n
          if r != _LAST[0]:
              _LAST[0] = r; return r
  ```

  and in `VM.step`, before the "everything else" fall-through:

  ```python
  if op == 120:                             # var.set.random lo hi var
      lo, p = self._fetch16(code, start + 1)
      hi, p = self._fetch16(code, p)
      v, _  = self._fetch16(code, p)
      self.setvar(v, random_no_repeat(lo, hi))
      T.call(name, (lo, hi, v)); return pc
  ```

  With that, the expected tuple becomes
  `(5958, 5958, 5958, 5958, 5799, 159, 18728, 18728, True)` — provided both
  sides start from seed 1 / last 0 and run the slots in the same order, which
  they do. I have not run (b); the numbers are the port's side of it.

If the sim also grows the fetch on 8/14/15/16/17/71 (it reads those raw), the
first row is unchanged — the corpus cannot tell.

## 4. Findings beyond the brief

* **`set.var.i32` (16): the table says 5 operand bytes, the handler reads 6.**
  `0x402070` fetches the 2-byte variable, then `mov eax, esi; add esi, 4` and
  assembles four bytes (`mov cl,[eax]; dh,[eax+1]; inc eax; inc eax;
  dl,[eax]; shl 16; dl,[eax+1]; shl 24`). `tables/vm_opcodes.json` row 16:
  `length 5, table_says 5, corrected false`; `dialog_disasm.LEN_FIX` has no
  entry. **0 shipped world scripts use op 16**, so the corpus cannot see it,
  and the probe shows it: the port reads the four value bytes (var5 = -7) and
  then advances by the table's 5, landing on the value's last byte as an
  opcode. For **T8** (tables + `LEN_FIX`): add `16: 6`. The interpreter needs
  no change once the table is right.
* **Count of indirect operands: 59, not 22.** Deduplicated by
  (archive, chunk, pc) over `tools/sim.world_scripts()`, all 59 are
  `push.i16 0x4000` in seven scripts — AREA 2 (msg 3), 61 (3), 141 (3),
  144 (2); SCENE 56 (3); GLOBAL records 0 and 8 (4) — each immediately
  compared against a constant with `eq; jmp_if_false`. The 22 in issue 20 may
  be a different dedupe; the method here is in the numbers above. No other
  opcode carries the bit anywhere (the sweep's DB identity with writes off is
  the corroboration: had one existed, the resolved index would have moved a
  write).
* **Op 34 `div` has 0 sites in the world corpus** (74 of `var.div`), so the
  truncation fix can only ever be tested by the probe.
* **`recordAll_` narration is still the raw halves.** With the bit set the
  engine's `Dbg_LogTagged` logs the resolved value (`push edi` after the
  fetch); the narration here records `0x4000`. No trace reaches a message
  handler today (issue 8), so nothing compares it yet. Worth a line when T2
  dispatches messages live.
* **`FILE_FORMATS.md` line ~819** says the handler runs "with
  `{message id, sender}` as parameters" — true of the block, but the only
  parameter a script can reach through operand `0x4000` is the sender. Doc
  paragraph in §7.

## 5. The check — `tools/verify.py`

Registration line, beside `("engine: scripts", ...)`:

```python
    ("engine: vm probe",   c_engine_vm_probe,   "script/interp.h; SCRIPT_VM"),
```

```python
def c_engine_vm_probe():
    r"""SCRIPT_VM: five handler rules through `tools/vm_probe.cpp` that the
    corpus sweep cannot see.

    Written 2026-09-02 against the interpreter as it stood, and its first run
    FAILED every line below except the reseed and writes-off ones:

      div       `cdq; idiv` (op 34 at 0x402750, `var.div` 22 at 0x402390)
                truncates toward zero: -7/2 = -3. The port had Python's
                floor after `tools/sim`: -4. Zero divisor -> 0 is the port's
                choice where the engine faults. No world script uses op 34
                and none divides a negative, so only this can test it.
      push.i16  op 8 (0x401D70) runs the shared fetch; `0x4000` is the
                parameter block's word at +2 - the SENDER for a message
                handler - and the port pushed the constant 16384.
      set.var   14/15/16 fetch the variable index; 15 fetches its VALUE as
                well; 17 fetches both. Read raw, an indirect index wrote
                variable 0 (16384 masked) and an indirect value stored 16385.
      scene.load 71 (0x403950) fetches both fields: the recorded call is
                the resolved pair and the state carries it.
      random    120's real handler (0x405480, not the pre-split block)
                writes Random_NoRepeat(lo, hi) (0x0041D6B0): in range, never
                the previous draw, lo when lo == hi; the port left the
                variable at 0 (0/50 in range, 49 consecutive repeats).

    The `set.var.i32` line is printed and not asserted: the table gives 16 a
    length of 5 where the handler reads 6, and that is the table's fix.
    """
    import re
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    tbl = os.path.join(ROOT, "tables", "vm_opcodes.json")
    if not (os.path.isdir(eng) and os.path.exists(tbl)):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ or tables/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "vm_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"
    r = subprocess.run([binp, tbl], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return ("no run",), ("ran",), "vm_probe must run"
    div34, div22, push, vars_, scene, rnd, reseed, off, lohi = {}, {}, None, {}, None, None, None, None, None
    for ln in r.stdout.splitlines():
        f = ln.split()
        if not f: continue
        if f[0] == "div34":       div34[(int(f[1]), int(f[2]))] = int(f[4])
        elif f[0] == "div22":     div22[(int(f[1]), int(f[2]))] = int(f[4])
        elif f[0] == "push.i16":  push = (int(f[4]), int(f[8]))
        elif f[0] == "set.var.i8":
            vars_ = {int(k): int(v) for k, v in re.findall(r"var(\d+)=(-?\d+)", ln)}
        elif f[0] == "scene.load":
            scene = (int(f[5]), int(f[6]), int(re.search(r"sceneOfArea\(12\)=(-?\d+)", ln).group(1)))
        elif f[0] == "random" and f[1] == "[3,5]":
            rnd = (f[5], int(f[7]), int(f[9]), int(f[11]))
        elif f[0] == "random" and f[1] == "reseeded":
            reseed = f[3]
        elif f[0] == "random" and f[1] == "writes-off":
            off = (f[3], int(f[5]))
        elif f[0] == "random" and f[1] == "lo==hi":
            m = re.search(r"var9=(-?\d+).*var11=(-?\d+) recorded (-?\d+) (-?\d+) (-?\d+)", ln)
            lohi = tuple(int(v) for v in m.groups())
    return (div34.get((-7, 2)), div34.get((7, -2)), div34.get((-7, -2)), div34.get((-7, 0)),
            div22.get((-7, 2)), div22.get((7, -2)), div22.get((-7, 0)),
            push, vars_.get(77), vars_.get(3), vars_.get(4), scene, rnd, reseed, off, lohi), \
           (-3, -3, 3, 0, -3, -3, 0,
            (77, -1), -5, -9, -5, (12, 34, 34), ("50/50", 0, 3, 50), "identical",
            ("var9=0", 50), (9, 42, 42, 42, 11)), \
           "op 34 -7/2, 7/-2, -7/-2 and -7/0; op 22 the same three; push.i16 " \
           "0x4000 with params {3,77} and 0xFFFF; set.var.i8 through an indirect " \
           "index, set.var.i16 through an indirect VALUE, set.var.var through " \
           "both; scene.load's resolved record and state; 50 draws of " \
           "var.set.random in [3,5]: in range, no consecutive repeat, all three " \
           "values, all recorded; a reseed repeats the sequence; writes off " \
           "leaves the variable and records; lo == hi returns lo and an " \
           "indirect lo/hi/var resolves"
```

## 7. Doc paragraphs

For `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md`, under the operand fetch:

> **The indirect index is offset by one word.** Every fetching handler reads
> `movsx eax, word ptr [block + eax*2 + 2]` after clearing bit `0x4000`, so
> operand `0x4000` names the parameter block's *second* int16. For a message
> handler `Message_RunHandlers` (0x00409420) writes `args[0] = message id,
> args[1] = sender`, and the value a script sees is therefore the **sender** —
> which is what the 59 shipped indirect operands want: each is
> `push <constant>; push.i16 0x4000; eq; jmp_if_false` with the constant an
> actor id (173, 346, 410 … under message 3) or an object id (3, 100, 10, 88 …
> under message 4). A script subscribed to message 3 has nothing to learn from
> the number 3. The fetch runs on every 16-bit field, not only variable
> indices: `set.var.i16` (15) fetches its value, `set.var.var` (17) and
> `scene.load` (71) both of theirs, `push.i16` (8) its immediate.
> `verify.py: engine: vm probe`.

> **Division truncates.** `div` (34, 0x402750) and `var.div` (22, 0x402390)
> are `cdq; idiv`: -7/2 is -3, and a zero divisor is a #DE fault, not a value.
> `tools/sim` and, until 2026-09-02, `engine/` used floor division; no shipped
> world script divides a negative (74 `var.div` sites, 0 `div`), so the corpus
> could not tell them apart.

> **`var.set.random` (120).** The handler is at 0x405480 — `clean/`'s block
> for 120 is the function *after* it (CLAUDE.md §1's trap). Three fetches, lo,
> hi and the variable, then `Var_Set(var, Random_NoRepeat(lo, hi))`;
> `Random_NoRepeat` (0x0041D6B0) returns lo when lo == hi and otherwise redraws
> `lo + rand() % (hi - lo + 1)` until it differs from the previous result
> (`dword_4E7E8C`, one global for the process). 256 shipped sites, each
> followed by a `case` on the variable — the passer-by lines and ambient
> variations. `engine/` draws from a seeded xorshift32 with the same no-repeat
> memory: where randomness enters is ported, not which numbers.

For `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` §5b3, after "`{message id, sender}` as parameters":

> — of which a script can reach only the sender: the operand fetch indexes the
> block from its second word (SCRIPT_VM).

For `tables/README.md` / `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md`'s operand-length list (T8's
call): op 16 `set.var.i32` is 6 bytes (2 + 4), the table's 5 is wrong, and no
shipped script exercises it.

## 1. `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md`

**"### Operand encoding" — rewritten.** The shared fetch (`sub_401AA0`
0x00401AA0 and its inlined copies) indexes the block at `ctx+36` **from its
second word** — `movsx eax, word ptr [edx+eax*2+2]` — so operand `0x4000` is
`args[1]`. `Message_RunHandlers` writes `args[0] = message id, args[1] =
sender`, so `push.i16 0x4000` pushes the **sender**. The corpus is the
independent half: all **59** indirect operands in the world scripts are
`push.i16 0x4000`, all 59 sit in the 7 scripts that are message subscriptions
(AREA 2/61/141 msg 3, AREA 144 msg 2, SCENE 56 msg 3, GLOBAL msg 4 and 20), and
each is compared with `cmp.eq` against an actor id (173, 187 …) or an object id
(3, 100, 385, 775 …) — never a message id. `Script_NewContext` zeroes `ctx+36`
everywhere else, so no other script *could* carry the bit. Also here: the
verified list of the **91** opcodes that run the fetch (89 from the blocks, plus
op 6 whose block is empty and op 120 whose block is the wrong function), the
note that 15's value / 17's and 71's both fields / 47's three all go through it,
and that only `0xFFFF` is excluded so any other negative operand would be taken
as an index. *(Correction to issue 20, which read `0x4000` as the message id;
T1 reached the same correction from the port side.)*

**New: "## The context status word, and what resumes a parked script".** The
eleven values of `ctx+22`, who writes each and what writes 1 back — events 2
(fight), 3 (object/move), 4 (camera), 5 (screen), `Script_Pump`'s tail (8 and
10), `Script_ProcessActions` (9), with the pump's tail quoted. **Status 5 is in
the table and marked unresolved**: `Area_Transition` mode 0 state 4 writes it
into the *superseded* caller and nothing found writes it back. Then the ten
opcodes that write the word (3, 45, 46, 58, 60, 62, 70, 89, 96, 126) with the
value each writes — including that 96 parks **only when the travel is
non-zero** and 126 unconditionally — and why op 152's apparent eleventh write is
its unbounded block. Then the activate dedupe (`ctx+32` cleared in
`Script_Execute`'s `LABEL_8` only when an activate finishes at status 0, so the
rule is "no second activate while the first is unfinished"), the **one-shot
latch** (bit 15 latches the slot into the 4↔5 ping-pong between the pump and
event 7 — it does **not** free the zone while the player stands in it), and the
**`Script_Pump` state-2 transcription fix** (the dry run decides only whether
the press is consumed; action 2 is queued on both outcomes).

**Corrected in place:** "starting a conversation ends the tick" — it ends it for
**that one context**; the pump's loop carries on and the world stops on the
*next* frame at `if (g_DialogState != 1)`.

**New: "### 93 — `actor.stat.set`, the opcode named after its side effect".**
Handler 0x00404790, three fetched fields (actor / property / variable),
`Var_Get(field 2)` then `Actor_SetProperty` on **both** arms; `Hud_ShowValue` is
the player arm's first call and the source of the old name, but it returns 0 for
anyone but the player and for properties 4/5 while the write happens either way.
The exact mirror of 86. The op-93 rows in the two hand-written tables are
renamed with it.

**New: "## The area transition — `Area_Transition`'s state machine".** The two
resident slots (`0x0069BC40`, two 16-byte rows of {AREA block, SCENE block,
area id, scene id}, everything walking both), the 8-dword block at
`dword_6A0600`, the five modes (op 47, op 48, `Script_QueueAction`'s action 3,
`Script_Pump`'s tail, event 3) and every state edge as a table; the departure
and arrival objects as objects of the **outgoing** block; op 45's status-8 park
and the `dword_4C0130` deferral that makes `Script_Execute` refuse any further
45/47; **the resident-return branch of `Area_LoadIntoSlot` that never reaches

**New: "## Messages, and the handler's parameter block".** Event 43 (**28 sites**

## Findings on the way (corrections to what batch 1 / T10 wrote)

1. **The load does NOT take "at least nine pump frames".** Cases 2–8 are
   gated on `sub_41EFA0`, which is the async file reader's "queued read
   served" test (`Offset == 0 && served == queued`), and only the `.3DO` SET is
   read through it — `Area_LoadIntoSlot` sets mode 1 before `Area_Load`, and
   case 2 sets mode 0 right after the set, so the `.SCX`, map, actors, props,
   `.ani` and slider track are read synchronously and cases 2..9 all run in
   the one `Area_TickLoad` call that finds the set served. The set streams at
   `ElementSize = 0x20000` bytes per `sub_41F320` call, which sits at the end
   of the frame function after `I2D_Flush`. So a transition takes
   **ceil(set bytes / 131072)** frames: Anekbah 2099056 → 17, AImpasse 33392 →
   1, jaunpur 2103652 → 17. `Music_SetFadeMode` is misnamed: it is
   `Async_SetMode` (its only effect is `dword_4E91C0` and `ElementSize`; the
   name came from `Game_HandleEvent` case 9 wrapping `Music_PlayTrack` in
   mode 2 / mode 0, which is the music STREAM's slice). Worth a rename in
   `readable/` (not my file). The boot load is mode 0 and takes 0 frames,
   which is what the port always did.
2. **The active row is switched by event 9, not by the transition.**
   `Area_TickLoad` case 9 sets `dword_69BC60`/`dword_69BC64` only for the
   duration of the two `Script_NewContext` calls and restores them. The switch
   is `Game_HandleEvent` case 9 — raised by `Walk_ProbeGround` (0x00467030)
   and `sub_459AA0` when the decor under the actor changes to a slot in state
   2 — which toggles the row, re-registers the zones and plays the area's own
   music (`AREA +142`). The transition machine only shows (`sub_419AF0`) and
   hides (`sub_419A90`) decors. Ported as `playerOnArea(area)`; the walker
   (E2) should call it when the ground decor changes; until then
   `placeActorAt` raises it for a teleport into the other slot's area, and
   the completion arms raise it for the destination when nothing has
   (RECONSTRUCTION, labelled in `areaTransition`'s `hideOutgoing`).
3. **441 of the 448 object-carrying `area.goto` sites are zone ENTER scripts**
   (record field 0), 7 activate, 1 in SCENE — not activate scripts. The
   objects are door pairs: AREA 0 zone 3 is `area.goto 201, 153, 240` and
   153/240 are `ported43open`/`ported43close` (linked, on set piece
   `Ported43`). So a door zone is: walk in → the destination streams → the
   door opens (on the outgoing scene) → the leave when the player's feet cross
   the quad → the door closes → the caller resumes. 409 of 448 pairs resolve
   in the source `.SCX` by object id (the earlier 416 counted differently).
4. **`area.goto X -1 -1` at state 8 is a no-op that returns 1** (mode 0 case 8
   with `a6 == -1` → `LABEL_17`): a script that transitions twice without an
   `area.arrive` between does nothing the second time. `requestArea` (the
   probe entry) therefore issues the `area.arrive` for the caller-less
   request before a second request.
5. **The intro's `AREAS 222` is op 47 and its `AREAS 118` is op 48** —
   `traces/intro.log` shows the pushes from `0x4c0790` and `0x4c0798`; AREA
   118's `+4` script tail is `area.goto 222 -1 -1 / scene.load 222,55 /
   actor.goto_address 654 / area.arrive 118 / end`. The `engine: intro`
   docstring's "`area.goto 222` stages a load, the caller runs on to its
   `scene.load`" is now literally what happens, one slice later.
6. `Zones_RegisterAll`'s prune only touches contexts with a zone id
   (`+42 != -1`); an area's STARTUP context that has ended stays in its table
   entry, at status 0, until its slot is evicted or `scene.load`/`unload`
   frees the SCENE's. So table entries are consumed by startup scripts across
   the whole play, which matters for the 32-entry cap.
7. SCENE 55's startup runs `player.become 49` at pc 1225 (the Impasse's
   Kay'l), which is why a restart probe reads the player as 49 before the
   restart and 136 after (AREA 118's `player.become 136` runs again in the
   restart frame).

## How the park is done without an interpreter change

`Script_Execute` needs the opcode BEFORE dispatch (the 45/47 refusal) and the
status word AFTER it (the transition's 9/10, the preload's 8). The
interpreter runs a whole script per call, so `Session::execute` hands it a
span that ends at the current instruction's last operand byte: it executes
that one instruction, fails the next fetch with `PcOutOfRange` and reports the
pc it reached (a jump target included; `steps >= 2` separates "executed one"
from "the chunk ends inside the instruction"). One `resume` call per
instruction; the scripts are tens of instructions a frame and the probe runs
in 0.4 s. No change to `interp.*` was needed, so nothing was delivered for T12.
If a `RunStatus::AreaOp` is ever wanted it would remove the per-instruction
call, nothing else.
