## Doc text

**docs/SCRIPT_VM.md**, replacing "### The load takes frames":

> ### The load takes frames — as many as the SET has 128 KiB slices
>
> `Area_Load` sets `dword_4E6D8C = 1` and calls `Area_TickLoad` once; cases
> 2–8 each return 0 unless `sub_41EFA0` (0x0041EFA0) passes. That function
> is not a load-screen timer: it is the engine's asynchronous file reader —
> its own error strings name it `Async_LoadDuringFrame` — reporting that the
> queued read has been served (`Offset == 0 && served == queued`, then
> `fclose`). `Music_SetFadeMode` (0x0041EFF0) is misnamed and is
> **`Async_SetMode`**: 1 sets `ElementSize = 0x20000`, 2 sets `0x10000`, 0
> reads synchronously. `Area_LoadIntoSlot` sets mode 1 before `Area_Load`
> and case 2 sets mode 0 straight after the set, so **only the `.3DO` set
> streams** — `o3de_LoadScene` queues its whole size — and `sub_41F320`,
> called at the end of every frame after `I2D_Flush`, reads one slice. Once
> the set is served, cases 2..9 (the `.SCX`, the map, the misc model,
> `Actors_SpawnFromTables`, `Scene_LoadProps`, the `.ani`, the slider track,
> the startup scripts and `Zones_RegisterAll`) run in **one** pump tail. So a
> transition takes ceil(bytes / 131072) frames: Anekbah's 2099056-byte set
> 17, AImpasse's 33392-byte set 1, and the boot (`State_Apply`'s `Area_Load`
> in mode 0) 0. The caller of a no-object `area.goto` resumes the frame after
> that, and the outgoing area's contexts and zones run throughout. (Ported
> 2026-09-02, `verify.py: engine: area transition`.)
>
> ### Which row is ACTIVE is the player's feet, not the transition
>
> `Area_TickLoad` case 9 sets `dword_69BC60`/`dword_69BC64` to the loaded
> slot only around its two `Script_NewContext` calls and restores them. The
> switch is `Game_HandleEvent` **case 9** — `dword_69BC64 = area; if the
> other row is occupied: dword_69BC60 = 1 - dword_69BC60; Zones_RegisterAll;
> play AREA +142 if it differs` — raised by `Walk_ProbeGround` (0x00467030)
> and `sub_459AA0` when the decor under the actor changes to a slot in state
> 2. The transition machine only SHOWS (`sub_419AF0`, state 2,
> `o3de_InsertScene`) and HIDES (`sub_419A90`, state 1) decors, and its
> completion arms hide "the non-active row's area" — which is the area left
> exactly because event 9 has already moved the row under the player.
>
> ### The objects are doors
>
> 441 of the 448 `area.goto` sites with objects are zone **enter** scripts;
> AREA 0's zone 3 is `area.goto 201, 153, 240` and the objects are
> `ported43open` and `ported43close`, a linked pair animating set piece
> `Ported43`. The walk (`Area_Transition`): the destination streams into the
> other slot while the player stands in the door zone; the tail shows its
> decor and starts the OPEN on the outgoing scene (state 5); event 3 at its
> end (7); the zone's LEAVE — `Script_QueueAction(ctx, 3)` when his feet
> cross the quad — starts the CLOSE (9); its end resumes the script. A second
> `area.goto X -1 -1` at state 8 — loaded and resumed, no `area.arrive` yet —
> is accepted and does nothing (mode 0 case 8, `a6 == -1`).

## What is RECONSTRUCTION, labelled in the source

* The leave on a transition caller without a zone scan: issued the frame the
  departure object ends (`areaTransition` mode 4 case 5; `queueLeave`
  comment). Off with `setLeaveFromZones(true)`.
* Event 9 with no walker: `placeActorAt` raises it for a teleport into the
  other slot's area; the completion arms raise it for the destination when it
  is still the other row (`hideOutgoing`).
* A transition object that is not resident (or no scene loaded) "ends" the
  next frame (`startTransitionObject`, program -2) — the engine would wait on
  it until the 60 s watchdog; the same policy `ObjectWait` already takes.
* One `SceneRunner`: the departure/arrival objects run on the outgoing scene
  (kept until the transition completes), then the destination's `.SCX` is
  loaded fresh; the engine holds both scenes. The viewer draws ONE set
  (`setName()` = the shown slot), so during the door beats the destination
  set is drawn and the outgoing one is not, where the engine has both linked.
* The slice count is a data-constrained model of I/O pacing (the file size
  over `ElementSize`); the engine's count depends on nothing else, but no
  capture times a load, so it is tier 6 with a tier-2 input.
* `requestArea`'s implicit `area.arrive` for a second caller-less request.
* The watchdog is 1800 frames (60 s at 30 fps) rather than wall-clock.
* `hideSet` on the shown slot swaps the drawn set to the other slot (one
  drawable set), and `showSet` is only the slot switch; the fog block
  (`sub_41D380`) and `sub_41D4D0`/`sub_41D3F0` at case 9 are not modelled.

## Not established

* Whether the engine reaches mode 3 case 2 (a leave queued while the load is
  still streaming, state 1 → 2) in play — the arm clears the block WITHOUT
  resuming the caller (status stays 10) and only the watchdog would; ported as
  read, not exercised by the probe.
* Status 5 (a superseded caller) — written, never resumed; as T10 recorded.
* Which slot `Message_RunHandlers` is given (`postMessage` searches the
  ACTIVE slot; the batch-1 version searched the shown area; both agree until
  event 9 and a message land in the same frames).
* `sub_419B50()` in event 9 (called before the toggle) — not read.
* The trace's `AREAS` string addresses vs IDA's `aAreas` labels: the asm
  listing puts the first `push offset aAreas` inside a label-less block that
  `awk` attributes to `sub_401C50`; the trace (op 47 → `0x4c0790`) is what
  the port follows. Nothing here depends on it.
* The port's `Program` ends the door animation (`0x03000008` on a set piece)
  in the frame it starts, so f1 and f2 take one frame each in the probe; how
  long `ported43open` runs in the engine is the object runtime's question,
  not the Session's.

## 1. The invariant the batch asked for: `engine: execute` holds

The corpus sweep must stay DB byte-identical to `tools/sim`, because the reference
stubs the same opcodes. Reproduced exactly as `tools/verify.py c_engine_execute` computes it
(the parse of `run_scripts`'s output, the `SIM.world_scripts()` walk, `GS.load()`, the
nine-tuple):

```
got  (5958, 5958, 5958, 5958, 5818, 140, 18584, 18584, True)
want (5958, 5958, 5958, 5958, 5818, 140, 18584, 18584, True)
PASS
```

And a stronger statement: the whole `run_scripts` output file — every slot's status,
step count and recorded op bytes, then the 8192-byte DB — is **byte-identical to the
output of the pre-edit binary** built from the same tree before any of this was written
(`MD5 d5b24cdc02be6d5bf3d46481275994a1`, both files, `cmp` silent). The sweep switch
being off puts every one of the twenty opcodes back on the stub recorder path,
literally the same code.

**The switch is load-bearing, shown.** A variant of `run_scripts` with the two
`setWorldWrites(false)` lines removed (compiled from a `sed` copy in the scratchpad
against the same objects) executes the same 5958 slots — 5818 reach `end`, 140 stop at
`dialog.start` — and its final DB differs from the reference in **88 bytes**: 35 in the
carried list (+848), 8 in the memo list (+1396), 18 in the player record (+60..+336)
and 27 across **14 variables** (22, 87, 135, 146, 147, 167, 168, 169, 227, 270, 537,
571, 598, 653); its recorded-call stream is 99 bytes longer, i.e. scripts took
different arms. That is the divergence the switch exists to hold back, and it is
exactly the state `tools/sim` does not model.

## 2. What each handler says — and where the issue text was wrong

Every arm in `interp.cpp` names its handler; this is the evidence behind the five
readings that differ from `todo/iam-script-engine.md`. Handler blocks are
`clean/_vmhandlers.json` at the address `clean/_vmsummary.json` gives the opcode
(**the issue's addresses for 75, 69 and 93 — 0x40ACB0, 0x40AC40, 0x404840 — are inside
the blocks, not their entries: 0x40AC90, 0x40AC20, 0x404790**; the blocks for 49, 50 and
51 are polluted with the preceding function's jump tables and tails, CLAUDE.md 1's
trap, and the handler starts at the `push` run after them).

### 2a. `sub_41A140` is `Actor_ReleaseObject(index, remove)`, not `Actor_SetState`

Issue 34 reads op 69 as `Actor_SetState(actor, 0)`. `readable/src/04_sys.c` names
0x0041A140 `Actor_ReleaseObject(a1, a2)`: it unlinks the object slot the live actor
record links at `+41*4`, and the second argument chooses between **re-parenting the
node to the world at the slot's stored placement** (`a2 == 0`: the prop is dropped
where it was) and **freeing it** (`a2 == 1`: `sub_418DC0(4, slot)`, `o3de_FreeScene`).
So 69 and 68's found arm DROP, and 68's not-found arm REMOVES:

```
op 68 (0x40AAF0)                                  op 69 (0x40AC20)
  call sub_419E00        ; Actor_Player               call sub_40D760   ; Scene_FindObjectIndexById
  call sub_41A350        ; Actor_HeldObjectSlot       call sub_41A350   ; Actor_HeldObjectSlot
  cmp  ebx, -1 ; jz end                              cmp  eax, -1 ; jz end
  ... prop record by SLOT (below) ...                push 0 ; push esi
  found & state bit 0:                               call sub_41A140   ; Actor_ReleaseObject(idx, DROP)
    push 0 ; push ebp ; call sub_41A140  ; DROP      call sub_40B190   ; Actor_FindById(id)
    and edi, ~2 ; call sub_40AFC0        ; state &= ~2   mov word ptr [eax+10Eh], 0FFFFh
    call sub_41CC20                      ; Object_HideFromScene
  else:
    mov word_4E6CA0[ebx*2], 0FFFFh
    push 1 ; push ebp ; call sub_41A140  ; REMOVE
  call sub_40AEE0 ; call sub_40B190 ; mov word ptr [eax+10Eh], 0FFFFh
```

### 2b. The AREA prop table is at `+44`/`+74`, not `+8`; 68 matches the SLOT at `+0`

Issue 30 says "the resident AREA's `+8` array". All three handlers that walk it read
`Area_Block(area)` then **`mov edx, [eax+2Ch]` / `movsx eax, word ptr [eax+4Ah]`** —
+44 and +74, which is what `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` "the prop table" already says — then
`Area_GetLoadedScene` → `Scene_Block` → `[eax+0Ch]` / `[eax+2Ah]` (+12 / +42). And
the field compared differs: 67 and 76 hold an OBJECTS id and compare
`movsx ebx, word ptr [edx+2]`; **68 holds the player's SLOT and compares
`movsx edi, word ptr [edx]`** — the record's `+0`, the runtime slot `Scene_LoadProps`
writes there. A port that matched 68 by id would release the wrong prop whenever two
records share an id, and never notice on a still frame.

### 2c. `inventory.remove_all 0, -1` can never remove anything

Op 52's `id == -1` arm (`loc_40A7D8`; **37 shipped sites, every one `0, -1`**) walks
the parallel 56-byte cache for entries whose `+0x24` bit 1 is set — that is the
`IAM\OBJECT` record's `+4` flag copied at cache `+32`, and `objects.h` names bit 1
"lost on reincarnation" — and then looks for the entry to remove with

```
loc_40A836:
    cmp     word ptr [ecx], 0FFFFh      ; the operand -1, constant-folded
    jz      short loc_40A849            ; -> remove at this index
    inc     eax ; add ecx, 2
    cmp     eax, esi                    ; esi = the stored count
    jl      short loc_40A836
    jmp     loc_40A8D9                  ; next entry
```

The compiler folded the opcode's own operand into the inlined find, so it searches
the first `count` ids for the TERMINATOR — which by construction sits at index
`count`, never inside. The removal at `loc_40A849` is unreachable. So the
reincarnation clean-out the scripts ask for 37 times **does nothing in the shipped
game**, and `GameState::listRemoveAll(list, -1)` (T6) returns 0 for the same reason
from the other side. Recorded rather than "fixed": the port reproduces the engine.

### 2d. `Actor_SetProperty`'s clamp is UNSIGNED: `-5` becomes 200

From `Runtime.exe.asm` at 0x0040B8D0, every 200-clamp is
`cmp esi, 0C8h ; jbe short …`, and Argent's is `cmp esi, 0FFFFh ; jbe` — `jbe`, not
`jle`. A script that subtracts damage past zero and writes it back through
`actor.stat.set` heals the actor to full. The port's `writeActorProperty` compares the
value as a `uint32_t`; `verify.py`'s probe asserts `-5 → 200` (§4, mutation 2 flips
it to a signed compare and the line reads −5).

### 2e. Op 93 writes on BOTH arms; the player's `+0xAA` is the HUD flash's argument

Issue 33 reads the player arm as `sub_41CE50(playerIndex, ?, field 2, value)` "on the
player record +0xAA". `sub_41CE50` is `Hud_ShowValue(index, property, value,
currentVie)` — 0x0041CE50 in `readable/src/04_sys.c`, which returns 0 for anyone but
the player and for properties 4 and 5 and otherwise starts the HUD flash — and
`movsx edx, word ptr [ecx+0AAh]` is the player record's **current Vie** passed as its
fourth argument, so the flash can show old against new. The write is the
`call sub_40B8D0` (`Actor_SetProperty`) that follows on both arms:

```
    call    sub_40E530          ; Var_Get(var)  -> esi
    cmp     edi, -1 ; jnz other
      call sub_419E00 ; Actor_Player
      movsx edx, word ptr [ecx+0AAh]   ; g_PlayerRecord + 170
      push edx ; push esi ; push ebp ; push eax
      call sub_41CE50           ; Hud_ShowValue(idx, prop, value, vie)
      jmp  both
    other:
      call sub_40D6A0           ; Scene_FindObjectRecord(slot, id) ; mov di, [eax]
    both:
      ... {prop, value, index} on the stack
      call sub_40B8D0           ; Actor_SetProperty
```

### 2f. The rest, as transcribed (no disagreement with the issues)

* **75** (0x40AC90): `Actor_HeldObjectSlot(Actor_Player())`; `jl` / `cmp eax, 32h ; jge`
  guard the slot to 0..49; `movsx eax, word_4E6CA0[eax*2]` else `or eax, -1`; then
  `Script_StoreVar` and `or byte ptr [esi+28h], 2` (the context flag, not modelled —
  nothing in the port reads ctx+40 yet, issue 7).
* **86** (0x404230): three fetches; `-1` → `Actor_Player()`, else
  `Scene_FindObjectRecord(dword_69BC60, id)` and `mov ax, [eax]` (the index, or the
  Win9x null page when the id is not in the 20-byte table); `Actor_GetProperty`
  over `{prop, ?, index}`; `Var_Set(var, block+8)`. **459 of 460 sites name the
  player**; the one that does not is AREA 141 pc 20369, `589, 7 (Type Spectre), 472`.
* **91** (0x404530): `Var_Set(var, Actor_IdBySlot(Actor_Player()))`.
* **49/50/51/52**: T6's reading, wired to T6's `listHas / listAdd(…, listRefusesDuplicates)
  / listRemove / listRemoveAll`. Field order of 49 is list, object, variable (T6's
  correction of issue 29).
* **128** (0x405810): four fetches — from, to, count variable, result variable;
  `n = Var_Get(count)`, `-1` → `ObjectList_Count(from)`; clamped to that count and to
  `ObjectList_Capacity(to) - ObjectList_Count(to)`; `dword_4C0B64 = from`; n times
  `ObjectList_InsertFront(to, cache[from][0].id)` + `ObjectList_RemoveAt(from, 0)`; then
  `Var_Set(result, n)` unless result is −1; `dword_4C0B64 = -1`. A negative n moves
  nothing (`test ebp, ebp ; jle`) and is stored as is. 3 sites, all SCENE 7:
  `(0, 1, 270, 270)` twice and `(1, 0, 270, 270)`.
* **110–115**: T6's reading; 111 → `timerStop`, 112 → `timerStart` (the table's names
  are inverted; the arms follow the mechanism). 113 is `lea` ×5 ×5 ×5, `shl 3` = ×1000.
  **Op 110 has one shipped site** — AREA 59 pc 12337, `110, 114 12, 113 900, end` —
  over the 5958-slot corpus; T6's "0" was over the smaller convention.
* **67** (0x40A9D0): actor, object; `Scene_FindObjectIndexById(actor)`; prop record by
  id, AREA then SCENE; `Actor_FindById(actor)->+10Eh == object` → nothing; else
  `Actor_HoldObject(index, rec+0)` when a record was found with `+0 != -1`, and
  `+10Eh = object` either way. **No prop-state write** — issue 30's "67 and 98 edit the
  same records" holds for 67's `+270` only.
* **76** (0x40ACF0): object; record by id; `ObjectState_Get(+16h) ; test al, 1` →
  `ObjectState_Set(+16h, state | 2)` and `Object_ShowInScene(+0)`. No record: the
  handler falls to `loc_40AD8A: xor esi, esi` and reads `[esi+16h]` — address 0x16,
  which Win9x maps (the real-mode IVT), so the shipped game reads garbage there
  rather than faulting. The port does nothing on a miss.
* **98** (0x404DB0): object, address; `sub_40AF00(object)` → its slot in the id table;
  `sub_41C270(slot, &pos)`, `sub_41C2C0(slot)`; `Address_Find(address, area)`
  (`sub_40A2C0`); `sub_41D050`; `sub_41CF50(slot, &pos)`. World positioning, no DB or
  chunk-record write — it is output, and the port hands it to the hook and records it.

## 3. The design, and what is DB and what is hook

`Actor_FindById` (0x0040B190) opens

```c
result = g_PlayerRecord;                       // g_GameDB + 60
if (i16(g_PlayerRecord, 272) == a1 || a1 == -1) return result;
```

before it scans a chunk. So for the player — named `-1`, or by the id the DB record
carries at `+272` — the stat block, the held-object field (`+270`, DB `+330`) and the
identity are inside the 8192-byte block, and `player.become` writes `+272` there
(`rep movsd` of the whole record) while a save restores it. That makes
`Actor_IdBySlot(Actor_Player())` and DB `+332` the same number at every moment a
script could ask, so **91, and 86/93/67/68/69 on the player, run on `GameState`
alone with no hook** — 736 of 784 sites of 93 and 459 of 460 of 86. The hook
interface therefore has no `playerId()`; a Session that installs nothing still
gets the player's stats moved.

`WorldHooks` (`hooks.h`) is one virtual per engine function the handlers call
(`Actor_GetProperty`/`SetProperty` on a non-player record, the record's `+270`,
`Actor_HeldObjectSlot`, `word_4E6CA0[slot]` and its clear, `Actor_ReleaseObject`,
`Actor_HoldObject`, `Object_ShowInScene`/`HideFromScene`, the prop walk by slot and by
id, `object.place_at`), each defaulting to "no record / nothing", and **a null pointer
means stub, as before** for 75, 67, 68, 69, 76, 98 and for 86/93 on a non-player.

`props.h` is the pure half a Session calls on its resident chunk copies: the three
table walks (`findPropById` / `findPropBySlot` at +44/+74 and +12/+42;
`findCharacterRecord` at +40/+72 and +8/+40; `findActorRecord` at +56/+80 and
+24/+48), `readActorProperty` (the getter's 24 value cases), `writeActorProperty` (the
setter's 12 cases with the unsigned clamps and the `+260` ammunition array indexed by
the high word), and `+270`. `Session::actorRecord` in `area.cpp` is the duplicate of
`findActorRecord` and can be replaced by it when T11's rewrite lands (§6).

`setWorldWrites(false)` puts ALL twenty back on the stub recorder path. When on, the
recorded call carries the RESOLVED fields in the handler's own order, which is the
order `tables/vm_announce.json` indexes (49/50/51/52/67 field 1, 76 field 0, 93 field
2) — no shipped operand of any of these carries the indirect bit, so the recorded
fields are byte-for-byte what the raw path recorded.

---

## 4. The probe, and the falsification record (PORTING B4)

`build/worldops_probe ../fr ../tables/vm_opcodes.json` prints 70 `label value`
lines. Its first run, against the interpreter with the API present and every arm
absent — the port as it stood — **failed 51 of the 70**. The 19 that passed are the
ones a stub passes by construction: the `*.untouched` and `used.nohooks` lines (the
variable keeps its seed), the five `off.*` lines, `has.7` (0 either way),
`remove_all.*` (nothing to remove because nothing was added), the two data-only
`prop.*` lines, and four "nothing happens" negatives. The before/after outputs are
kept beside this file's evidence in the scratchpad and reproduced here in short:

```
                            before   after            before   after
has.6                          0       1     used.none              77      -1
add.dup.list0.count            2       4     used.held              77     360
add.dup.list0.front            6     300     hold.calls              0       1
add.dup.list2.count            0       1     hold.field             -1     360
remove.one.count               2       3     release.actor.drop.calls 0     1
transfer.all.moved             0       2     show.state              1       3
transfer.all.list1.front     176     171     show.calls              0       1
timer.fresh.elapsed           77       0     release.drop.calls      0       1
timer.flags.running            1      12     release.hide.calls      0       1
timer.running.elapsed         77    3000     release.player.field  360      -1
timer.expired.elapsed         77  900000     release.remove.calls    0       1
timer.stopped.flags            1      29     release.clearslot.calls 0       1
player_id.fresh               77      -1     npc.vie.set             0      42
player_id.become              77     136     npc.argent.clamp        0   65535
stat.player.vie.neg            0     200     npc.ammo.slot2         -1      17
stat.player.argent             0   65535     place.calls             0       1
```

Two targeted mutations, each restored afterwards (binary deleted, forced relink):

| mutation | moves |
|---|---|
| op 50 refuses duplicates on lists 0/1 instead of 2/3 (`!listRefusesDuplicates`) | `add.dup.list0.count` 4 → **3**, `add.dup.list2.count` 1 → **2**, `remove.one.count` 3 → 2 |
| `Actor_SetProperty`'s clamp as a SIGNED compare | `stat.player.vie.record` and `stat.player.vie.neg` 200 → **−5** |

**And the trap in B4 bit, in a new form.** After `cp`-ing the kept sources back and
rebuilding, the probe still printed BOTH mutations: the restored `.cpp` landed in the
same second as the mutated `.o`, and Apple's `make` is GNU make 3.81, which compares
whole seconds and rebuilds only on strictly-newer — so neither object was recompiled
and the "restored" binary was the mutated one. `touch` a second later, delete the
binaries, rebuild: probe identical to the recorded after-output, sweep identical to
the baseline. B4 says "delete the binary as well as the object"; on this machine
the object itself can be the stale link, and the tell is a diff that shows a
mutation you have already reverted.

### The check — insert beside `c_engine_vm_probe`

```python
def c_engine_world_ops():

## 5. What stays stubbed, and what could not be established

1. **`Inventory_Insert`'s kind gate (T6's gap 7), measured now.** Op 50 in the
   engine loads the `IAM\OBJECT` record and `Inventory_Insert` (0x004098E0) decides:
   kinds 12 (seteks) and 13 (rings) go to `Object_ApplyEffect` — Argent / Anneaux on
   the player record — and take **no slot**; ammunition (7..11) merges into a carried
   gun of kind−5 when there is one; a gun (2..6) already carried takes no second slot
   and instead swallows the carried ammunition packs of its kind. Over the 473
   shipped `inventory.add` sites: **27 add seteks, 14 add ammunition, 9 add guns**
   (the rest are kind 0/1/14/15/16, which take a slot). The port takes a slot for
   all 473. `objects.h` has the kinds, flags and `effectProperty`, and `props.h` now
   has the setter with the Argent clamp, so the money half is ~30 lines behind a
   `WorldHooks::objectRecord(id)` (or a `GameState`+`ObjectRecord` overload) — left
   for a slice that reads `Object_ApplyEffect` (0x409780) properly.
2. **List 3, the shop stock**, is not in the DB and not modelled by `GameState`
   (T6): 23 `has_object` and 25 `inventory.add` sites name it; `has_object 3, x`
   always writes 0 here where the engine reads the shop's per-area `ObjectList_Load`.
3. **Op 86 on a property that fills the pointer slot** (0 `Sexe`, 5 sites) or on an
   actor no 20-byte record names: the engine stores stack garbage; the port leaves the
   variable. Not reproducible, not pretended.
4. **`ctx+40` bit 2**, which 75 sets: no reader in the port yet (issue 7 owns the
   context flag word).
5. **The 3D half of 67/68/69/76/98** — `Actor_HoldObject`, `Actor_ReleaseObject`'s
   re-parenting, `Object_ShowInScene`, the placement — is the hook's, and the Session
   text in §6 only RECORDS them; drawing a held or dropped prop is frontend work.
6. **Not established: what the 88-byte divergence with world writes ON means for
   the golden traces.** The five captures are order-only announcements and none
   of the twenty opcodes changes what is announced, so the traces cannot see
   this slice; its tier is 2 (the corpus counts, the dead −1 arm, the clamp read
   from the image) and 3 against T6's independent transcription of the list
   functions, never 4.

## 6. The Session side — `WorldHooks` for `area.{h,cpp}`, to paste

Written against `area.h` as it stands (one `curArea_`, `sceneOverArea(state_,
curArea_)`, chunks re-read from the archive per call). T11 is giving the Session two
resident slots with staged loads; the only adaptation is that the two writable copies
below become per-slot and `loadProps()` runs in `Area_TickLoad`'s case 9 (the
engine's `Scene_LoadProps(area, scene, 1)` call site) instead of at the end of
`loadArea`. Everything else is chunk-relative.

### area.h — includes and private members

```cpp
#include "script/hooks.h"
#include "script/props.h"
#include <array>
#include <map>
#include <set>

    // ---- the world the opcodes reach beyond the DB (script/hooks.h) ------
    //
    // The engine edits its LOADED BLOCKS in place - `Actor_SetProperty` writes
    // the chunk's 276-byte record, 67/68/69 write its +270, `Scene_LoadProps`
    // writes the prop record's +0 - and frees them on unload, so those edits
    // live exactly as long as the block. These are the resident AREA and the
    // SCENE over it as writable copies, made when the area loads, dropped
    // when it goes; `props.h` walks them.
    std::vector<std::byte> areaCopy_, sceneCopy_;
    // `word_4E6CA0`: the 50 object slots' OBJECTS ids, -1 free. `Scene_
    // LoadProps` fills it from the prop tables (first free slot, AREA then
    // SCENE); the unload writes -1 back for every record's slot.
    std::array<int, 50> objectSlotIds_{};
    // `Actor_HeldObjectSlot`: which slot an actor holds, by id; -1 = player.
    std::map<int, int> heldSlot_;
    // `Object_ShowInScene` / `HideFromScene`: the slots linked into the scene.
    // What a frontend draws props from.
    std::set<int> shownSlots_;
    // What the hooks were asked to do in 3D and did not: for a frontend.
    struct PropEvent { const char* what; int actor; int slot; int address; };
    std::vector<PropEvent> propEvents_;

    class Hooks final : public WorldHooks {
    public:
        explicit Hooks(Session* s) : s_(s) {}
        bool getActorProperty(int actor, int property, std::int32_t& out) override;
        bool setActorProperty(int actor, int property, std::int32_t value) override;
        int  heldObjectField(int actor) override;
        void setHeldObjectField(int actor, int objectId) override;
        int  heldObjectSlot(int actor) override;
        int  objectIdInSlot(int slot) override;
        void clearObjectSlot(int slot) override;
        void releaseObject(int actor, bool remove) override;
        void holdObject(int actor, int slot) override;
        void showObject(int slot) override;
        void hideObject(int slot) override;
        bool propBySlot(int slot, PropRef& out) override;
        bool propById(int id, PropRef& out) override;
        void placeObjectAt(int objectId, int address) override;
    private:
        Session* s_;
        // `Actor_FindById` over the two copies (the DB's own record is the
        // interpreter's): a writable span on the record, empty when none.
        std::span<std::byte> record(int actor);
        // `Scene_FindObjectRecord`: the 20-byte table, AREA then SCENE. 86/93
        // read garbage in the engine when this misses; the hook refuses.
        bool inObjectTable(int actor) const;
    };
    Hooks hooks_{this};
    // `Scene_LoadProps(area, scene, 1)`: hand out the slots and fill +0.
    void loadProps();
    // The unload's `word_4E6CA0[rec+0] = -1` over both tables.
    void unloadProps();
```

And in `Ctx`'s three creation sites — `queueStartup`, `postMessage`, and the one at
line 185 — right after `c->vm.setObjectWaitSuspends(objWait_);`:

```cpp
    c->vm.setHooks(&hooks_);
```

### area.cpp

```cpp
// ---- the resident copies ------------------------------------------------
//
// Called where `loadArea` / `finishAreaTransition` / `reloadScene` settle the
// resident pair (T11: the slot's Area_TickLoad case 9). The AREA copy and the
// SCENE copy are the blocks `Area_Block` / `Scene_Block` return, and every
// per-record edit the handlers make lands in them.
void Session::loadProps() {
    unloadProps();
    areaCopy_.clear(); sceneCopy_.clear();
    if (curArea_ >= 0) {
        const auto areaFile = readFile(iam_ + "/AREA");
        const auto areas = IamArchive::open(areaFile);
        const auto ab = areas.chunk(static_cast<std::size_t>(curArea_));
        areaCopy_.assign(ab.begin(), ab.end());
    }
    const auto sc = sceneOverArea(state_, curArea_);
    if (sc != -1) {
        const auto sceneFile = readFile(iam_ + "/SCENE");
        const auto scenes = IamArchive::open(sceneFile);
        const auto sb = scenes.chunk(static_cast<std::size_t>(sc));
        sceneCopy_.assign(sb.begin(), sb.end());
    }
    // `Scene_LoadProps` (0x00409FC0): for every prop record whose state has
    // bit 0, the FIRST free entry of word_4E6CA0 (-1 when all 50 are taken)
    // takes the id and the record's +0 takes the slot; bit 1 links it into
    // the scene. AREA's table first, then the SCENE's.
    const auto walk = [&](std::vector<std::byte>& chunk, ChunkKind kind) {
        if (chunk.empty()) return;
        const std::size_t po = kind == ChunkKind::Area ? 44 : 12;
        const std::size_t co = kind == ChunkKind::Area ? 74 : 42;
        const std::span<const std::byte> b(chunk);
        if (b.size() < co + 2) return;
        const std::size_t p = u32at(b, po);
        const int n = i16at(b, co);
        if (n <= 0 || p + 24u * static_cast<std::size_t>(n) > b.size()) return;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            const std::size_t o = p + 24u * static_cast<std::size_t>(i);
            const int id = i16at(b, o + 2), idx = i16at(b, o + 22);
            if (!(state_.propState(idx) & 1)) continue;
            int slot = -1;
            for (int k = 0; k < 50; ++k)
                if (objectSlotIds_[static_cast<std::size_t>(k)] == -1) { slot = k; break; }
            if (slot >= 0) objectSlotIds_[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] = id;
            chunk[o]     = static_cast<std::byte>(slot & 0xFF);
            chunk[o + 1] = static_cast<std::byte>((slot >> 8) & 0xFF);
            if (slot >= 0 && (state_.propState(idx) & 2)) shownSlots_.insert(slot);
        }
    };
    objectSlotIds_.fill(-1);
    walk(areaCopy_, ChunkKind::Area);
    walk(sceneCopy_, ChunkKind::Scene);
}

void Session::unloadProps() {
    objectSlotIds_.fill(-1);
    shownSlots_.clear();
    heldSlot_.clear();
}

// ---- the hooks ------------------------------------------------------------

std::span<std::byte> Session::Hooks::record(int actor) {
    if (auto o = findActorRecord(s_->areaCopy_, ChunkKind::Area, actor))
        return std::span<std::byte>(s_->areaCopy_).subspan(*o, kActorRecordSize);
    if (auto o = findActorRecord(s_->sceneCopy_, ChunkKind::Scene, actor))
        return std::span<std::byte>(s_->sceneCopy_).subspan(*o, kActorRecordSize);
    return {};
}

bool Session::Hooks::inObjectTable(int actor) const {
    return findCharacterRecord(s_->areaCopy_, ChunkKind::Area, actor).has_value() ||
           findCharacterRecord(s_->sceneCopy_, ChunkKind::Scene, actor).has_value();
}

bool Session::Hooks::getActorProperty(int actor, int property, std::int32_t& out) {
    if (!inObjectTable(actor)) return false;
    const auto r = record(actor);
    return !r.empty() && readActorProperty(r, property, out);
}

bool Session::Hooks::setActorProperty(int actor, int property, std::int32_t value) {
    if (!inObjectTable(actor)) return false;
    const auto r = record(actor);
    return !r.empty() && writeActorProperty(r, property, value);
}

int Session::Hooks::heldObjectField(int actor) {
    const auto r = record(actor);
    return r.empty() ? -1 : heldObjectOf(r);
}

void Session::Hooks::setHeldObjectField(int actor, int objectId) {
    const auto r = record(actor);
    if (!r.empty()) setHeldObjectOf(r, objectId);
}

int Session::Hooks::heldObjectSlot(int actor) {
    const auto it = s_->heldSlot_.find(actor);
    return it == s_->heldSlot_.end() ? -1 : it->second;
}

int Session::Hooks::objectIdInSlot(int slot) {
    return slot >= 0 && slot < 50 ? s_->objectSlotIds_[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] : -1;
}

void Session::Hooks::clearObjectSlot(int slot) {
    if (slot >= 0 && slot < 50) s_->objectSlotIds_[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] = -1;
}

// `Actor_ReleaseObject(index, remove)`: the slot leaves the hand. Dropped
// (remove false) it stays a scene object at its stored placement; removed it
// is freed - `sub_418DC0(4, slot)` - and leaves the shown set too.
void Session::Hooks::releaseObject(int actor, bool remove) {
    const auto it = s_->heldSlot_.find(actor);
    const int slot = it == s_->heldSlot_.end() ? -1 : it->second;
    if (it != s_->heldSlot_.end()) s_->heldSlot_.erase(it);
    if (remove && slot >= 0) s_->shownSlots_.erase(slot);
    s_->propEvents_.push_back({remove ? "remove" : "drop", actor, slot, -1});
}

void Session::Hooks::holdObject(int actor, int slot) {
    s_->heldSlot_[actor] = slot;
    s_->propEvents_.push_back({"hold", actor, slot, -1});
}

void Session::Hooks::showObject(int slot) {
    s_->shownSlots_.insert(slot);
    s_->propEvents_.push_back({"show", -1, slot, -1});
}

void Session::Hooks::hideObject(int slot) {
    s_->shownSlots_.erase(slot);
    s_->propEvents_.push_back({"hide", -1, slot, -1});
}

bool Session::Hooks::propBySlot(int slot, PropRef& out) {
    auto p = findPropBySlot(s_->areaCopy_, ChunkKind::Area, slot);
    if (!p) p = findPropBySlot(s_->sceneCopy_, ChunkKind::Scene, slot);
    if (!p) return false;
    out = {p->slot, p->id, p->stateIndex};
    return true;
}

bool Session::Hooks::propById(int id, PropRef& out) {
    auto p = findPropById(s_->areaCopy_, ChunkKind::Area, id);
    if (!p) p = findPropById(s_->sceneCopy_, ChunkKind::Scene, id);
    if (!p) return false;
    out = {p->slot, p->id, p->stateIndex};
    return true;
}

void Session::Hooks::placeObjectAt(int objectId, int address) {
    s_->propEvents_.push_back({"place", -1, objectId, address});
}
```

Two things the coordinator should know when pasting:

* `Session::actorRecord` (area.cpp ~835) and `shownBitOf` (~745) are the same walks
  as `findActorRecord` / `findCharacterRecord` in `props.h`, over freshly-read chunks.
  With the copies above they can become one-liners over `areaCopy_` / `sceneCopy_` —
  and then `player.become`'s `actorRecord` read sees the record AS EDITED, which is
  what the engine's `rep movsd` copies (the target's current Vie, not the shipped one).
* `character.show`/`hide` (78/79) and `becomePlayer` write the DB, not the copies;
  nothing here conflicts with T2's arms.

## 8. Doc text

### 8a. `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md` — replace the last paragraph of "93 — `actor.stat.set`" ("This is the pair that moves health … Not yet ported at either end")

> This is the pair that moves health, money and every other stat a script changes.
> **Ported 2026-09-02 at both ends** (`engine/src/script/interp.cpp`, `props.h`),
> with two things the assembly settles that the decompilation only implies:
>
> * **the clamp is unsigned.** Every `Actor_SetProperty` case that caps at 200 is
>   `cmp esi, 0C8h ; jbe` (and Argent's `cmp esi, 0FFFFh ; jbe`), so a script that
>   subtracts damage past zero and writes the result back heals the actor to 200.
>   `verify.py: engine world ops` asserts `-5 → 200`;
> * **the player needs no actor table.** `Actor_FindById` returns `g_GameDB + 60`
>   before it scans a chunk whenever the id is −1 or the DB record's own `+272`, so
>   the player's stat block is the saved block itself — 736 of the 784 sites of 93
>   and 459 of the 460 of 86 — and only the other 49 reach a chunk record, through
>   `WorldHooks::getActorProperty` / `setActorProperty`.
>
> Properties 0, 6 and 9–15 fill the pointer slot, and 0x15, 0x16 and 0x22–0x24 use
> the value slot as an *input* index, so through 86 they store or index by stack
> garbage; the port leaves the variable on those (5 shipped sites, all property 0).

### 8c. `docs/GAME_STATE.md` §3 — append after T6's "What the four opcodes do to a list"

> **`inventory.remove_all list, −1` does nothing, and that is the engine's.** Its
> `id == −1` arm (`loc_40A7D8`; 37 shipped sites, every one `0, −1` — the
> reincarnation clean-out, since the flag it tests is the OBJECT record's "lost on
> reincarnation" bit copied into the cache at `+0x24`) finds the entry to remove

> the opcode's own operand into the inlined find, so it looks for the terminator
> inside the counted run and never reaches the removal. `GameState::listRemoveAll

> at a time — so they arrive reversed — with *n* from a variable (−1 = all), clamped to
> the source's count and the destination's free room, and written back to a second
> variable unless that is −1; a negative *n* moves nothing and is stored as it is.
> Its 3 sites are all SCENE 7, between lists 0 and 1, variable 270 on both ends.

> **Port status (2026-09-02):** 49, 50, 51, 52 and 128 execute in `engine/`

# T13 — the live zone registry: issue 10 (and 9 / 5 in the live replica)

Files created: **`engine/src/script/zones.h`**, **`engine/src/script/zones.cpp`**,
**`engine/tools/zones_probe.cpp`**, and this file. Nothing else was edited —
`world.{h,cpp}` (T4's), `area.{h,cpp}` (T11's), `interp.*` (T12's),
`tools/verify.py`, `docs/`, `engine/README.md` and the Makefile are untouched,
and `verify.py` was not run.

Built with `cd engine && make -s OBJDIR=build/obj-T13 build/zones_probe`.
`src/script/zones.cpp` is back at its post-fix state after the four mutations
below — `md5 389f6be32c6149e139580618b5e6ad30` before and after each.

---

## 1. What changed, and the engine line each transcribes

The port had a zone runtime and it was only ever a HARNESS. `World`
(`world.cpp`) takes one chunk of one kind and runs the scripts itself; the
thing `omk` and `omk-play` actually run — `Session` — had no zone model at
all, so in the live replica **no zone ever armed** and every conversation had
to come out of a startup script. That is issue 10, and it is what
`ZoneRegistry` closes.

It is deliberately **not a second scheduler**. `world.h`'s `Zone`, `zonesOf`,
`contains`, `centre` and the `kZoneUnit` quad conversion are reused verbatim,
and nothing here runs a script: every action the pump would queue comes back as
a `ZoneEvent` carrying the zone id, the action number, the script offset and
the chunk it is relative to. The activate DEDUPE stays where the engine keeps
it — in the context's own 4-deep FIFO and its `+32` — which is the Session's,
not the zone's.

### `Zones_RegisterAll` (0x00406560) — the four tables and both slots

```
Zones_Clear();
for (blocks = dword_69BC40; blocks < &dword_69BC60; blocks += 4, ++areaSlot) {
    if (blocks[2] != -1 && blocks[0])          // the AREA's table
        for (rec = u32(blocks[0], 48), n = i16(blocks[0], 76); n--; rec += 68)
            if (Zone_StateBit(u16(rec + 12, 52))) Zone_Add(rec + 12, areaSlot);
    if (blocks[3] != -1 && blocks[1])          // the SCENE loaded OVER it
        for (rec = u32(blocks[1], 16), n = i16(blocks[1], 44); n--; rec += 68)
            if (Zone_StateBit(u16(rec + 12, 52))) Zone_Add(rec + 12, areaSlot);
}
```

Two slots × two tables = four walks, and the guard is the id **and** the block.
`ResidentSlot` is that 16-byte record (`dword_69BC40/44/48/4C`) with the chunks
as spans; `registerAll` is the loop, gated on `StateArray::ZoneState` —
**confirmed as array 5** from `Zone_StateBit` (0x0040D500), which indexes
`u32(g_GameDB, 28)`, and `gamestate.h` already names `+28` array 5.

`Zone_StateBit` masks the id to 15 bits, so bit 15 — the one-shot flag — is
stripped for registration and read back whole by the pump. `Zone::stateBit()`
and `Zone::oneShot()` are `world.h`'s and are used as they stand.

### The prune — `Zones_RegisterAll`'s tail

```
for (ctx : the 32 context slots)
    if (ctx && u16(ctx, 42) != -1 && !Zone_FindScriptsById(u16(ctx, 42))) {
        for (ps : the 16 prompt slots)
            if (u32(ps,0) == ctx) { u32(ps,0)=0; ps[5]=-1; ps[4]=0; --dword_4E6B24; }
        Mem_Free(...); dword_4E61E8[u8(ctx,30)] = 0;
    }
```

Split in two because the contexts belong to the Session: `registerAll` does the
**prompt-slot** half itself (a slot whose zone no longer resolves is released
and reported by `detached()`), and `prune(contextZones)` returns the ids whose
contexts the caller must free.

`Zone_FindScriptsById` (0x00406760) searches the resident chunks' **full**
record tables, not the registered subset — so a zone whose save bit a script
has just cleared with `zone.disable` still resolves and its context survives.
Only unloading its area prunes it. `resolve()` reproduces that, over `all()`,
in the engine's own order (slot 0 AREA, slot 0 SCENE, slot 1 AREA, slot 1
SCENE).

### `Actor_ScanZones` (0x00467770) — and the arc is **not** what the file holds

Containment first, event 8 for every zone the point is inside, then the arc and
event 7. `Zone_ContainsPoint` (0x0048C880) is a crossing count over the four
corners and **ignores y** — the third argument is passed and never read, which
is why `Zone::contains(x, z)` is the right call.

The facing test is where a new fact came out of the loaders. `Area_Load`
(`01_file.c`, the per-zone relocation loop) converts the arc **in place**:

```
u16(rec, 62) = (int)((double)u16(rec, 62) * 0.087890625);   // 360/4096
u16(rec, 60) = (int)((double)u16(rec, 60) * 0.087890625);
```

so `Actor_ScanZones` compares whole **degrees** against the actor's facing
(`f32(actor, 420)`, a float in degrees) while the field on disk is a
4096-per-turn angle — the unit `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` §5b2b records and
`verify.py: zone records` asserts ("0 arcs past 4096"). Both readings are
right; they are one conversion apart, and nothing had crossed it because
`World` never had an actor with a real yaw in the same frame.

`zoneFacesDegrees` is the engine's test at the engine's unit, wrap arms
included:

```
if (u16(zone,50)) {                      // a zero WIDTH accepts any facing
    lo = mid - (wide >> 1); hi = mid + (wide >> 1);
    if (lo >= 0) { if (hi > 360 && facing < lo) facing += 360; }
    else if (!(facing < lo + 360 && facing <= hi)) { lo += 360; hi += 360; }
    if (!(facing >= lo && facing <= hi)) continue;
}
```

`Zone::faces` (world.h) is the same arc measured in the stored 4096 unit and
rounded differently; it is left alone for `World`, and the live scan uses this
one. The one line here that is **not** in the assembly is the `fmod` that wraps
the incoming facing into [0, 360) — labelled in the source, and a no-op for a
facing already in range.

### The 16 prompt slots — `Script_Pump` (0x00407DC0) and `Game_HandleEvent`
### case 7 (0x004067D0)

Modelled **as the state machine**, with the engine's own words, which is the
one thing T4 explicitly left implicit ("`World` derives *armed* from the
position and facing each step instead of keeping the 16 prompt slots"). The
slot is 16 bytes: `+0` context, `+4` the zone record, `+8` state, `+10` the
zone id, `+12` the area slot.

| state | name | who writes it | to what |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | empty | pump case 3/5, the prune | — |
| 1 | new | case 7, taking a free slot | pump case 1 → 3 |
| 2 | pressed | case 7, from 3 | pump case 2 → 3, or 5 if one-shot |
| 3 | armed | pump cases 1 and 2 | case 7 → 2; a pump that still finds 3 → leave |
| 4 | latched (scanned) | case 7, from 5 | pump case 4 → 5 |
| 5 | latched / leaving | pump case 2 (one-shot) and case 4 | case 7 → 4; a pump that still finds 5 → leave |

The ORDER is what makes this work and it is measured, not assumed:
`Script_Pump(1)` is `readable/src/05_sys.c:2107` and `Actors_TickAll()` is
`:2178`, both inside `Game_Tick`, with **no dialogue gate on the actor tick**.
So the pump always reads the states the *previous* frame's scan left, and 4/5
ping-pong for as long as the player stands in a one-shot zone — T4's correction
to issue 5, re-derived here from the same two functions and now expressed as
the states rather than as a `spent` flag.

That is why `pumpSlots` and `scanZones` are separate public calls: the Session
runs the first at the top of its frame and the second at the bottom, exactly
where `Game_Tick` runs them. `scan()` does both in that order for a probe.

Three details that are the engine's and would not be guessed:

* **the enter script is conditional, the leave is not.** Case 1 is
  `if (zoneScripts[0]) Script_QueueAction(ctx, 1);` with *both* arms writing
  state 3, so a zone with no enter script still holds its slot; cases 3/5 queue
  actions 3 and 4 unconditionally, and `Script_ProcessActions` consumes an
  action whose script slot is 0 and leaves the context idle. `world.cpp` guards
  both; this guards only the one the engine guards. (AREA 76 zone 1466 has no
  enter script and is the shipped case — its `Arm` event carries action 0.)
* **no activate script, no latch.** Case 2 tests `u32(ctx, 4)` before anything
  else, so a one-shot zone with an empty activate slot is spent by nothing.
* **the press is gated on the prompt table.** `Game_HandleEvent` case 6 is
  `if (g_DialogState == 3 || a2 != 4 || !dword_4E6B24) return 0;` — a press
  with no slot armed never becomes `dword_4E6C90` at all, so `pumpSlots` gates
  it on `armedCount()` rather than trusting its caller.

### What is NOT modelled, and is labelled in the source

* **the case-2 inline dry run.** The engine runs the context's current script
  as a dry run before queueing — `Script_Run`, or `Script_RunToOpcode75` while
  the player holds an object — and its return decides only whether the press
  counts as *consumed* (`dword_4E66B8`, issue 7), never whether the activate is
  queued: empty-handed both outcomes fall into `loc_407F93`. So with empty
  hands the queue is unconditional and this reproduces it exactly.
  `setHeldObject(true)` makes the registry *refuse* the queue rather than
  guess, because `Script_RunToOpcode75`'s answer is not modelled anywhere in
  the port.
* **seventeen simultaneous zones.** Case 7's free-slot search leaves `v26 = 0`
  and then writes `v26[5] = v24` **through it** — a null store, so the shipped
  game crashes on the 17th. Dropped and labelled; it is a bug, not a behaviour.
* **the context reuse arm** of case 1 (a zone re-armed while its free was still
  queued) is Session-side, because it manipulates the FIFO. Written out in §3.

```

          [leave z3791 a3 @0] [free z3791 a4 @0] [touch]

Reading them:

* **0 / 1 — the start pair.** AREA 118 declares **0 zone records**, which is
  the same fact `verify.py: intro script` rests on and the reason the intro can
  only come from a startup script. AREA 222 with SCENE 55 over it is **12 + 2
  records, 5 + 1 registered** under `IAM\START`'s save bits — the 12 and the 5
  are what `verify.py: sim: tutorial walk` already asserts from the Python
  side, reproduced here from C++, and the **+1 is the SCENE's own table**,
  which nothing in the port could reach before.
* **2 — a real walk through AREA 222 zone 3791.** In, arm, a press that does
  nothing (the zone has an enter script and no activate — the engine's case-2
  guard), then a **turn out of the arc**: still touched, no longer armed, and
  the next pump leaves and frees. 5 touches over 5 contained frames.
* **3 — two slots, and the one-shot latch.** AREA 146 in slot 0 and AREA 76 in
  slot 1: 109 records, 80 registered, and both walks resolve, which is the
  four-table/two-slot walk doing the thing `World` cannot. Under the *same*
  five held frames one-shot zone **35141** (`-30395` as an int16) emits **one**
  activate and ordinary zone **1466** emits **five**.
* **4 — the touch camera.** Zone 626's centre is inside 626 *and* 634. The
  player stands with his back to 626's arc: 634 arms, 626 does not, and 626's
  `+66` still reaches `Camera_FindWorld` — **camera 540, twice, on two
  frames** — because event 8 is raised before the facing test.
* **5 — the prune.** Arm 3791, then re-register with AREA 118 alone: the
  prompt slot is `detached` (armed 1 → 0) and `prune([3791, 3803])` returns
  both.

### Shown to fail (PORTING B2)

Four mutations, each built and run, each restored (md5 checked):

| mutation | what it is | what moves |
|---|---|---|
| walk **slot 0's AREA table only** | the reach `World` has, i.e. issue 10's "one chunk and one kind" | sc.1 `(14, 6, [...3803])` → `(12, 5, [...])`; sc.3 `(109, 80, 80, 1, 5)` → `(53, 49, 49, 1, 0)` and **zone 1466 is not resident at all** |
| **drop the one-shot latch** (`state 2` never writes 5) | issue 5's other half | sc.3 → `(109, 80, 80, **5**, 5)` — the one-shot zone activates five times |
| **drop the prune** (both halves) | issue 10's "the pruning has no counterpart either" | sc.5 `(0, [3791], [3791, 3803], 0)` → `(0, [], [], **1**)` — the slot stays armed on a zone whose area is gone |
| **test the arc before the touch** | the shape `World::step` had before T4 | sc.2 touches 5 → **3**; sc.4 `(4, 2, 540)` → `(2, 0, -1)` — the auto-cut camera never fires |

    // ---------------------------------------------------------- THE ZONES
    //
    // `Zones_RegisterAll` + `Actor_ScanZones`, the two halves `Session` did

In `Session::Ctx`, beside the existing fields:

        // ---- the ZONE half of Script_NewContext's 0x2C-byte block
        //
        // A startup or message context leaves `zone` at -1 and none of this
        // runs; a zone context is the same object with a FIFO under it.
        std::int16_t zone = -1;              // u16 +42, the owning zone id
        std::int32_t slots[3] = {0, 0, 0};   // +0/+4/+8, enter/activate/leave
        std::deque<int> queue;               // +24, its count at +28
        int  act     = 0;                    // +32, the CURRENT action
        bool running = false;                // u16 +22 != 0
```

(and `#include <deque>`.)

In the private section:

    ZoneRegistry zones_;
    bool actionPressed_ = false;
    // The resident chunks, COPIED - `ZoneRegistry` holds spans into them and
    // `IamArchive::chunk` points into a buffer local to the call.
    std::vector<std::byte> slotArea_[2], slotScene_[2];
    int slotAreaId_[2] = {-1, -1}, slotSceneId_[2] = {-1, -1};
    // Rebuild the registry from both slots and free what the prune reports.
    // Called from `loadArea`, `finishAreaTransition`, `sceneLoad`/`sceneUnload`
    // - the engine's three call sites, all of them area load or transition,
    // NONE of them per-frame.

### 3b. `area.cpp`

```cpp
void Session::registerZones() {
    std::vector<ResidentSlot> slots;
    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {
        ResidentSlot s;
        s.areaId  = slotAreaId_[k];
        s.sceneId = slotSceneId_[k];
        s.area    = {slotArea_[k].data(),  slotArea_[k].size()};
        s.scene   = {slotScene_[k].data(), slotScene_[k].size()};
        slots.push_back(s);
    }
    zones_.registerAll(slots, state_);

    // Zones_RegisterAll's tail: a context whose zone no longer resolves goes
    // with its area. `registerAll` has already released the prompt slots.
    std::vector<std::int16_t> ids;
    for (const auto& c : ctxs_)
        if (!c->done && c->zone != -1) ids.push_back(c->zone);
    for (const auto dead : zones_.prune(ids))
        for (auto& c : ctxs_)
            if (c->zone == dead) c->done = true;
}

Session::Ctx* Session::zoneContext(std::int16_t zone) {
    for (auto& c : ctxs_)
        if (!c->done && c->zone == zone) return c.get();
    return nullptr;
}

// Script_QueueAction (0x004063D0). The two refusals are one rule twice: a
// second ACTIVATE while one is queued or is the one being run. A FULL queue
// stores nothing and still returns 1.
int Session::queueAction(Ctx& c, int act) {
    if (c.queue.size() >= 4) return 1;
    if (act == 2) {
        for (const int q : c.queue) if (q == 2) return 0;
        if (c.act == 2) return 0;
    }
    c.queue.push_back(act);
    return 1;
}

void Session::applyZoneEvents(const std::vector<ZoneEvent>& ev) {
    for (const auto& e : ev) {
        if (e.kind == ZoneEvent::Kind::Touch) continue;   // the scan's half
        Ctx* c = zoneContext(e.zone);
        if (!c) {
            // Only an Arm creates one - Script_Pump case 1's
            // `Script_NewContext(areaSlot, s[0], s[1], s[2])`.
            if (e.kind != ZoneEvent::Kind::Arm) continue;
            auto n = std::make_unique<Ctx>(state_, table_);
            n->code.assign(e.code.begin(), e.code.end());
            n->zone = e.zone;
            for (int k = 0; k < 3; ++k) n->slots[k] = e.scripts[k];
            n->chunkArea = curArea_;
            n->vm.setCameraWaitSuspends(camWait_);
            n->vm.setObjectWaitSuspends(objWait_);
            ctxs_.push_back(std::move(n));
            c = ctxs_.back().get();
        } else if (e.kind == ZoneEvent::Kind::Arm) {
            // Case 1's reuse arm: the zone re-armed while its FREE was still
            // at the head of the FIFO -
            //     if (ctx && u16(ctx,42) == slot.zoneId && u8(ctx,24) == 4)
            //         { u8(ctx,24) = 0; --u16(ctx,28); }
            // - cancel the free and keep the context, its stack included.
            if (!c->queue.empty() && c->queue.front() == 4) c->queue.pop_front();
        }
        if (e.action) queueAction(*c, e.action);
    }
}

// Script_ProcessActions (0x00408220), the zone half: dequeue ONE action, point
// the context at the matching script slot, set the status word. It does not
// execute - keeping the two apart is what makes a park possible.
void Session::processActions(std::size_t i) {
    Ctx* c = ctxs_[i].get();
    if (c->zone == -1 || c->done) return;         // a startup/message context
    if (dialogState_ == 3) return;                // `if (g_DialogState == 3) return`
    if (c->running || c->queue.empty()) return;
    c->act = c->queue.front();
    c->queue.pop_front();
    if (c->act == 4) { c->done = true; return; }  // action 4 frees it
    const int slot = c->act - 1;
    const auto off = (slot >= 0 && slot < 3) ? c->slots[slot] : 0;
    // `case n: ctx->pc = slots[n-1]; if (slots[n-1]) status = 1;` - an action
    // whose slot is 0 is consumed and leaves the context idle.
    if (off > 0) {
        c->pc = static_cast<std::size_t>(off);
        c->started = false;
        c->running = true;
    }
}
```

At the top of `runContext`, after the existing `done`/wait guards:

```cpp
        // A zone context runs only while an action is armed.
        if (c->zone != -1 && !c->running) return;
```

and in its tail, wherever the run reaches `end` (the arm that today sets
`c->done = true` for a startup context):

```cpp
        if (c->zone != -1) {
            // Script_Execute's LABEL_8: only `end` and the error statuses end
            // an action, and only then is `+32` cleared -
            //   if (u32(a1,32) == 2 && !u16(a1,22)) u32(a1,32) = 0;
            // which is exactly how long the activate dedupe lasts. A PARK
            // (status 4/6/7, or `dialog.start` leaving it at 1) keeps
            // `running` true and the context resumes from its saved pc.
            c->running = false;
            c->started = false;
            if (c->act == 2) c->act = 0;
        } else {
            c->done = true;                       // a startup context is one-shot
        }
```

`Session::frame`, with the two calls in `Game_Tick`'s order — **the pump's slot
loop first, the actor scan last**:

```cpp
void Session::frame() {
    ++frameNo_;
    if (dialogState_ == 3) {
        /* ... unchanged: the dialogue owns the frame, the scene still ticks,
           and NOTHING below runs - `Script_Pump` opens
           `if (g_DialogState != 1) return 1;`. Actor_ScanZones is in the actor
           tick and is not part of the pump, so the engine does keep raising
           touches during a conversation; the port does not, and the only case
           that can tell is a player who walks through a zone and out again
           mid-conversation (the same limit `world.cpp` labels). */
        return;
    }

    // ---- Script_Pump(1), part 1: the 16 prompt slots  (05_sys.c:2107)
    {
        std::vector<ZoneEvent> ev;
        zones_.pumpSlots(actionPressed_, ev);
        applyZoneEvents(ev);
        actionPressed_ = false;                   // `dword_4E6C90 = 0;`
    }

    // ---- Script_Pump(1), part 2: ProcessActions then Execute, per context
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ctxs_.size(); ++i) {
        processActions(i);
        runContext(i);
    }
    if (pendingArea_ >= 0) finishAreaTransition();
    tickCamera();
    scene_.tick(static_cast<float>(frameSeconds_ * 30.0));
    trackPlayer();

    // ---- Actors_TickAll -> Actor_ScanZones             (05_sys.c:2178)
    //
    // AFTER the scripts, which is not a detail: the states this leaves are
    // what the NEXT frame's pump reads, and that one-frame offset is the whole
    // of the one-shot latch (case 7 writes 4, pump case 4 writes 5).
    {
        const double p[3] = {playerPos_[0], playerPos_[1], playerPos_[2]};
        std::vector<ZoneEvent> ev;
        zones_.scanZones(p, playerYaw_, ev);
        for (const auto& e : ev) {
            // Game_HandleEvent case 8: a touched zone whose +66 is not -1
            // hands it to Camera_FindWorld and points the camera at the
            // request block - a CUT, since case 8 fills the block directly and
            // no travel length is involved. The last touch of the scan wins.
            if (e.kind == ZoneEvent::Kind::Touch && e.camera != -1)
                applyCamera(e.camera, 0);
        }
    }
}
```

`registerZones()` goes at the end of `loadArea` and of `finishAreaTransition`
(after `residentWorld`), and at the end of `sceneLoad` / `sceneUnload` — the
engine's three call sites, `Area_TickLoad` case 9, `Game_HandleEvent` case 9
and the two scene handlers, **none of them per-frame**. Wherever `loadArea` and
`finishAreaTransition` set `curArea_` / `otherArea_`, they must also fill
`slotArea_[k]` / `slotAreaId_[k]` (and the scene pair) for the slot being
written, which is issue 15's two-resident-slot machine — T11's. Until that
lands, filling slot 0 alone gives the registry exactly the reach `World` has
today plus the SCENE table, and the `+1` of scenario 1 is that.

**The player's position and facing.** `playerPos()` / `playerYaw()` today is
where `actor.goto_address` last teleported him, so the scan is real but the
player does not move; E2's `PlayerController` replaces those two lines with
`player_->pos()` / `player_->facing()` and nothing else in this changes. The
facing must be **degrees** — see §1's note on the arc conversion, and the fact
that `f32(actor, 420)` is the engine's own degree field.

## 5. Doc text

### For `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md`, with the zone lifecycle (T10/T14 own the file)

> ### The 16 prompt slots, as a state machine
>
> `Script_Pump` (0x00407DC0) and `Game_HandleEvent` case 7 (0x004067D0) share a
> 16-entry table (`unk_4E6B30`, 16 bytes: `+0` context, `+4` the zone record,
> `+8` state, `+10` the zone id, `+12` the area slot). The pump reads it, the
> actor scan writes it, and **the pump runs first**: `Script_Pump(1)` is
> `Game_Tick`'s :2107 and `Actors_TickAll` its :2178, with no dialogue gate on
> the actor tick.
>
> | state | set by | what the pump does with it |
> |---|---|---|
> | 0 | the release, and the prune | nothing - the id at `+10` is -1 |
> | 1 | case 7, taking a free slot | make the context, queue action 1 if the zone has an enter script, → 3 |
> | 2 | case 7, from 3 | with the press: queue action 2, then → 5 if the zone id's bit 15 is set, else → 3. Without: → 3 |
> | 3 | the pump, from 1 and 2 | still 3 means nothing re-armed it - queue actions 3 and 4, release the slot |
> | 4 | case 7, from 5 | → 5 |
> | 5 | the pump, from 2 (one-shot) and 4 | as 3 |
>
> So an armed zone ping-pongs 3 → 2 → 3 for as long as the player faces into
> it, and a **one-shot** zone ping-pongs 5 → 4 → 5 instead: the bit does not
> free the zone, it latches the slot out of the press cycle, and the leave
> happens on leaving like any other zone. Three of the transitions are
> conditional and the conditions are not symmetric: the *enter* script is
> queued only if the zone has one (both arms still write 3), the *leave* and
> the *free* are queued unconditionally, and the press does nothing at all
> unless the zone has an **activate** script - which is also why a one-shot
> zone with no activate script is never spent.
>
> An action press with no slot armed never reaches the pump: `Game_HandleEvent`
> case 6 is `if (g_DialogState == 3 || a2 != 4 || !dword_4E6B24) return 0;`.
>
> ### The arc is converted at load
>
> `Actor_ScanZones` compares the actor's facing (`f32(actor, 420)`, degrees)
> against `u16(zone, 48)` / `u16(zone, 50)` — the record's `+60`/`+62` **after**
> `Area_Load` has multiplied both by `0.087890625` = 360/4096. The field on disk
> is a 4096-per-turn angle (FILE_FORMATS §5b2b); the runtime one is whole
> degrees. A zero width — authored, or small enough to truncate to zero —
> accepts any facing.

### For `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` §5b2b, one line beside `+60`/`+62`

> …4096-step angles **on disk**: `Area_Load`/`Scene_Load` convert both in place
> by 360/4096 as they relocate the record, so every runtime consumer
> (`Actor_ScanZones`) reads whole degrees.

### For `engine/README.md`, in the runtime section

> **The zones are LIVE.** `src/script/zones.{h,cpp}` is `Zones_RegisterAll`
> (0x00406560) and `Actor_ScanZones` (0x00467770): the four-table walk over
> both resident slots gated on the save bit, the 16 prompt slots with the
> engine's own state words, the per-frame touch (event 8, which asks for the
> zone's camera) and arm (event 7), the one-shot latch, and the prune that
> takes a context away with its area. It runs no scripts - it returns the
> `Script_QueueAction` calls the Session should make, because the activate
> dedupe lives in the context's FIFO. `World` (`world.cpp`) stays as the
> single-chunk harness the zone checks drive.
> `verify.py: engine zone registry`.

---

## 6. The check for `tools/verify.py`

Add after `c_engine_zone_pump`; it needs a build, so it belongs in `SLOW`.

```python
def c_engine_zone_registry():
    r"""`engine/`'s LIVE zone registry - both resident slots, all four tables.

    `verify.py: engine zones` and `engine zone pump` drive `World`, which takes
    ONE chunk of ONE kind and runs the scripts itself. This drives
    `ZoneRegistry`, which is what the SESSION was missing (issue 10): before
    it, nothing in `omk` or `omk-play` ever armed a zone and every conversation
    had to come out of a startup script.

    **`Zones_RegisterAll` (0x00406560)** walks both resident slots and, in
    each, the AREA's zone table (+48, count int16 +76) and the SCENE's loaded
    over it (+16, +44), registering `record + 12` for every zone whose save bit
    is set - `Zone_StateBit` (0x0040D500) indexing the game DB's +28 bitmap
    with `(id & 0x7FFF) / 8`, so bit 15, the one-shot flag, is masked away.
    Its tail PRUNES: a context whose zone id no longer resolves through
    `Zone_FindScriptsById` - its area was unloaded - is detached from the
    prompt slots and freed.

    **`Actor_ScanZones` (0x00467770)** raises event 8 for every registered zone
    the player's point is inside, BEFORE the facing test, and event 7 - which
    arms one of the 16 prompt slots - when the arc matches too. The arc is
    read in DEGREES because `Area_Load` converts it: it rewrites the record's
    +60/+62 by 360/4096 as it relocates, so the 4096-step angles
    `FILE_FORMATS` 5b2b records are whole degrees by the time anything
    compares them with the actor's facing at `f32(actor, 420)`.

    Six scenarios, one `GameState` apiece:

    * **0/1 - the start pair.** AREA 118 has **0 zone records**, which is why
      the intro can only come from a startup script; AREA 222 with SCENE 55
      over it is 12 + 2 records and **5 + 1** registered - the 12 and the 5
      are what `sim: tutorial walk` asserts from the Python side, and the +1
      is the SCENE's own table, which nothing in the port could reach.
    * **2 - walked.** AREA 222 zone 3791: touch, arm (enter script 2323), a
      press that does NOTHING because the zone has no activate script (the
      engine's case-2 guard is `if (u32(ctx, 4))`), a turn OUT of the arc -
      still touched, no longer armed - then leave and free.
    * **3 - two slots, and the one-shot latch.** AREA 146 in slot 0, AREA 76
      in slot 1: 109 records, 80 registered, both walks resolve. Under the
      same five held frames one-shot zone 35141 (`-30395` as an int16) emits
      ONE activate and ordinary zone 1466 emits five. The bit latches the slot
      out of the press cycle - `Game_HandleEvent` case 7 maps state 5 back to
      4 and the pump maps 4 back to 5, and the pump runs BEFORE the actor tick
      - it does not free the zone early (T4's correction to issue 5).
    * **4 - the touch camera.** Zone 626 of AREA 25 carries camera 540 at +66,
      and the player stands in it with his back to its arc: 634 (which
      overlaps it) arms, 626 does not, and 626 still asks for camera 540 on
      both frames. Testing the arc first loses it entirely.
    * **5 - the prune.** Arm 3791, then re-register with AREA 118 alone: the
      prompt slot is detached (armed 1 -> 0) and the context ids come back.
    """
    import subprocess, tempfile, shutil
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    iam = omkpaths.data("IAM")
    if not (os.path.isdir(eng) and os.path.isdir(iam)):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ or gamedata/IAM absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "zones_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"

    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    out = os.path.join(tmp, "z.bin")
    try:
        subprocess.run([binp, iam, os.path.join(iam, "START"), out],
                       capture_output=True)
        bb = open(out, "rb").read()
        o = 0
        n, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
        sc = {}
        for _ in range(n):
            f = struct.unpack_from("<7i", bb, o); o += 28
            nl, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
            live = list(struct.unpack_from("<%di" % nl, bb, o)) if nl else []
            o += 4 * nl
            ne, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
            ev = [struct.unpack_from("<4i", bb, o + 16 * k) for k in range(ne)]
            o += 16 * ne
            nd, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
            det = list(struct.unpack_from("<%di" % nd, bb, o)) if nd else []
            o += 4 * nd
            npr, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
            pru = list(struct.unpack_from("<%di" % npr, bb, o)) if npr else []
            o += 4 * npr
            sc[f[0]] = dict(records=f[1], registered=f[2], touches=f[3],
                            camReq=f[4], lastCam=f[5], armed=f[6],
                            live=live, ev=ev, det=det, pruned=pru)
        trailing = len(bb) - o
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def acts(evs, zone):
        return sum(1 for e in evs if e[0] == 2 and e[1] == zone)

    # event kinds: 0 touch, 1 arm, 2 activate, 3 leave, 4 free
    got = ((sc[0]["records"], sc[0]["registered"]),
           (sc[1]["records"], sc[1]["registered"], sc[1]["live"]),
           sc[2]["ev"], sc[2]["touches"],
           (sc[3]["records"], sc[3]["registered"], len(sc[3]["live"]),
            acts(sc[3]["ev"], -30395), acts(sc[3]["ev"], 1466)),
           (sc[4]["touches"], sc[4]["camReq"], sc[4]["lastCam"]),
           (sc[5]["registered"], sc[5]["det"], sc[5]["pruned"], sc[5]["armed"]),
           trailing)
    want = ((0, 0),
            (14, 6, [3790, 3791, 3795, 3799, 3801, 3803]),
            [(0, 3791, 0, 0), (1, 3791, 1, 2323), (0, 3791, 0, 0),
             (0, 3791, 0, 0), (0, 3791, 0, 0), (3, 3791, 3, 0),
             (4, 3791, 4, 0), (0, 3791, 0, 0)], 5,
            (109, 80, 80, 1, 5),
            (4, 2, 540),
            (0, [3791], [3791, 3803], 0),
            0)
    return got, want, \
           "AREA 118's zero zone records; AREA 222 + SCENE 55 registering " \
           "5 + 1 of 12 + 2 under IAM\\START's save bits; a walk through " \
           "zone 3791 - touch, arm, a press with no activate script, a turn " \
           "out of the arc, leave, free; TWO SLOTS registering 80 of 109 " \
           "with the one-shot zone activating once over five held frames " \
           "where the ordinary one activates five times; the touch camera " \
           "540 asked for with the player facing away; and the prune taking " \
           "a prompt slot and a context away with their area"
```

## 7. What I could not establish

* **`verify.py` was not run** (task rule), so the check is written and its
  parser exercised standalone, not as a `verify.py` check.
* **The Session wiring is TEXT, not code.** `area.{h,cpp}` is T11's this batch,
  and T11 is rewriting the transition machine that owns the two resident slots
  — so `registerZones()`'s `slotArea_`/`slotAreaId_` arrays are written against
  a slot model that does not exist yet (issue 15). Filling slot 0 alone is
  correct and gives the registry `World`'s reach plus the SCENE table; the
  second slot needs T11's.
* **`prune` is exercised only by unloading everything.** The interesting case —
  slot 1 replaced while slot 0 stays — needs the two-slot transition, so
  scenario 5 registers AREA 118 alone. The mechanism is the same either way
  (`resolve` over the surviving records), but the shipped A → B → A path has
  not been walked through it.
* **The inline dry run of pump case 2 is unported**, as it was in `World`. It
  decides `dword_4E66B8`, which is issue 7 (the unconsumed press → message 26),
  and with empty hands it cannot change whether the activate is queued. With a
  HELD object it can, and `setHeldObject(true)` refuses rather than guessing —
  so a use-object press through the registry is currently a no-op, and that is
  a labelled gap rather than a modelled behaviour.
* **The scan does not run during a conversation.** `Actor_ScanZones` is in the
  actor tick and has no dialogue gate, so the engine keeps raising touches and
  filling prompt slots while `Dialog_TickUI` owns the frame; `Session::frame`
  returns before the scan. The only case that can tell the two apart is a
  player who walks through a zone and out again mid-conversation, which is the
  same limit `world.cpp` labels.
* **`Zone::contains` casts its ray along the other axis** from
  `Zone_ContainsPoint` (0x0048C880), which crosses on X. Both are valid
  crossing counts over the same quad and they can only disagree exactly on an
  edge. Reused rather than re-transcribed, because it is `world.h`'s and the
  task says so — but it is a difference, and it is the one place a
  pixel-exact containment claim would need re-deriving.
* **No golden trace can adjudicate any of this.** `Zones_RegisterAll`,
  `Script_Pump` and `Actor_ScanZones` announce nothing to `Dbg_LogTagged`; only
  the opcodes an armed script goes on to execute do. The standard here is
  DATA-CONSTRAINED plus assembly-transcribed, not engine-verified — which is
  worth stating because `traces/impasse-walk.log` DOES contain the far side of
  it (the zones AREA 222 fires as the player walks the Impasse), so a
  Session-side replay once the wiring lands would be the first real oracle.

```
