## 5. One sentence for `engine/README.md`'s Session coverage row

> `Actors_SpawnFromTables` runs at every area load and every `scene.load`, so
> both resident slots carry the characters their AREA and SCENE tables place —
> model, `.CTL` bank, position, facing, runtime slot and the `ObjectShown` bit
> that decides whether each is attached — and `shown()` is derived from them
> (7 spawned and 4 attached for the Impasse, `verify.py: engine spawn from tables`).

## 6. What stays labelled, and where the code differs from the engine

* **No model is loaded.** `Actor_LoadModel(slot, name + ".3DO", area)` and
  `Actor_LoadBankList` have no counterpart: the Session holds no geometry and
  no `.CTL` runtime instance per world character. The names are recorded
  (`model`, `bank`) and a frontend opens them — that is T20 / `omk-play.md` 41.
  So a placement naming an actor whose `.3DO` is missing would fault in the
  engine and is silent here.
* **No actor object, so `Actor_SetPlacement`'s side effects are absent.** The
  engine writes the position twice (`[58..60]` and `[61..63]`), the yaw at
  `[105]`, rebuilds the 3x3 at `+288`, calls `o3de_SetNodePos` and
  `SpatialIndex_Update`, and zeroes seven fields when the actor IS the player.
  The port keeps the placement as data on `Character`; nothing consumes the
  spatial index yet.
* **`freeActorSlots` does not model the player exception.** `sub_40BEC0` skips
  the record whose `+0` equals `Actor_Player()`'s slot, so the player's runtime
  entry is never handed back. The Session has no runtime slot for the player at
  all, so there is nothing here that exception would protect; labelled rather
  than invented.
* **A record whose actor id resolves to nothing** is skipped with its runtime
  slot still handed out (the engine takes the slot before the lookup and then
  faults reading `+144` off a null record). No shipped record does this — all
  nine ids in the probe resolve — but the difference is deliberate.
* **The truncation is applied on read, not written back.** `Area_Load`
  rewrites the chunk's own bytes; `readPlacements` converts each time from the
  raw file bytes, which cannot double-convert and gives the same values. Only
  record `+0` is written back into the chunk, which is what
  `Scene_FindObjectRecord`'s callers read.
* **`Actor_Attach`/`Actor_Detach` themselves** (0x0041CCA0 / 0x0041CDD0, the
  o3de tree link) are still just the `attached` flag; the render tree is the
  viewer's.

## 7. Found wrong on the way

1. **The issue's placement numbers are rounded, the engine's are truncated**
   (§1). `7605 -80 2980` / `358` → `7604 -79 2980` / `357`. Found only by
   reading `Area_Load`'s conversion loop after the probe disagreed with the
   brief by one unit in three fields at once — which is the signature of a
   rounding difference, not of a wrong layout.
2. **The issue names one call site; there are two.** It says
   "called once from `Area_TickLoad` case 5", and `readable/src/01_file.c:4815`'s
   banner says `@callers 1`. Opcode 71 `scene.load`'s handler (0x403950) calls
   it too, with `a3 = 0` — verified with `tools/asmfn.py --op 71`, and already
   quoted (unremarked) in `area.cpp`'s own `sceneLoad` comment as
   `call sub_40BB90 / sub_409FC0 ; its props and actors`. The handler is not in
   the decompilation under any name, which is why the banner's count is short:
   CLAUDE.md §1's "a direct call site is what makes a `proc` label" trap seen
   from the other side — here the *callee's* count is wrong because the
   *caller* was never recognised as code.
3. **The issue predicts `attached_ids 212,218,219,57` at the Impasse; playing
   there gives `212,218,219,49`.** Both are right: the first is the cold load
   the bits describe, the second is after the intro's scripts have run. The
   probe reports both, because a check that only pinned one would have looked
   like a failure of whichever run it was not built from.
4. **`shown()`'s old contract survives unchanged for script-shown ids.** With
   the spawn skipped, `shown_` is exactly `scriptShown_` in push order — which
   is why `session_probe` and `run_intro_beat` print the same bytes in all
   three builds. Worth stating: it means the derivation is additive, and the
   four existing probes are not evidence for it.

```

## Check — for tools/verify.py

```python
def c_engine_session():
    r"""The Session's scheduling rules, one shipped fact each (`session_probe`).

    Each line is a rule the engine's own code settles and the port got wrong
    until 2026-09-02 (todo/iam-script-engine.md 2, 6, 8, 11, 17, 25, 28, 32);
    the numbers are the shipped data's, not chosen:

    * `become` - AREA 118's startup script opens `player.become 136` at pc
      1047. Handler 0x402F60 copies the actor record into the DB player
      record (`rep movsd`, 0x43 dwords from +8) and `strcpy`s its two bios
      into the +336/+592 slots. So after one frame the DB says the player is
      136, model KUM_FN, and the bio begins "A jur". START ships -1 / 0xFF.
    * `message25` - `Message_RunHandlers` runs message 25 INLINE: posted and
      run on the same frame, through GLOBAL's table (offset 5006, `set.var.i8`
      then `end`), and the variable GLOBAL +72 names (198) goes 0 -> 3.
    * `dialog_frame` - `Script_Execute`'s `if (v4 == 61) return` stops ONE
      context; a message-26 handler queued for the same frame still runs in
      it (ran == 2, the frame the conversation opens). Before: -1, because
      the Dialog arm returned out of the whole frame.
    * `shown_bit` - `character.show 310` writes the 20-byte record's +18
      (468) into the ObjectShown map: value 1. And `shown` stays ONE entry
      (310 HO1_FNM), because `character.hide -1` at pc 1050 hides the PLAYER
      the script has just made 136.
    * `derived_none` - a derived walk with no answer is a screen LEFT:
      `UI_OpenScreen` seeded -1, case 5 writes it and status 1. The variable
      (seeded 77 by the probe) reads -1, the context stays live and the
      script reaches `dialog.start` next frame. Before: 77, dead, no dialog.
    * `scene_load` / `scene_unload` - on the RESIDENT area (222) `scene.load
      55` creates the SCENE's startup context on the spot (created 1 -> 2)
      and `scene.unload` drops it (live 2 -> 1) with the DB back at -1;
      loaded again and ticked once, SCENE 55's script announces (37 lines).
    * `message_area` - AREA 222's own table answers message 23 at offset 2455.
    * `return` - A(118) -> B(222) -> A creates 222's startup context (1 -> 2)
      and then NOTHING for 118 (2 -> 2): `Area_LoadIntoSlot`'s "already in
      that slot" branch. Before: 3.

    Shown to fail: every starred line above differed on the reverted build
    (todo/pending/T2.md).
    """
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    if not os.path.isdir(eng):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "session_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"
    r = subprocess.run([binp, omkpaths.data_root(), os.path.join(ROOT, "tables")],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return ("no run",), ("ran",), "session_probe must run"
    L, bio = {}, None
    for ln in r.stdout.splitlines():
        f = ln.split()
        if f: L[f[0]] = f[1:]
        if f and f[0] == "become":            # the bio carries spaces: cut the raw line
            i = ln.find('bio0 "')
            bio = ln[i + 6:i + 11] if i >= 0 else None
    def g(key, *idx):
        f = L.get(key, [])
        return tuple(f[i] if i < len(f) else None for i in idx)
    got = (
        g("become", 1, 3, 5),                    # player_before, player_after, model
        bio,
        g("message25", 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13),  # found, table, offset, posted, ran, var, from, to
        g("dialog_frame", 1, 5, 7, 11),          # open, message, table, ran
        g("shown_bit", 3, 5, 7, 8),              # index, value, shown, first entry
        g("derived_none", 1, 3, 5),
        g("answer_minus1", 3, 5, 7),
        g("scene_load", 5, 7, 9, 11),            # db, created from, to, live
        g("scene_unload", 3, 5, 7),
        g("scene_script", 3, 5),                 # announced after, SCENES
        g("message_area", 1, 3, 5, 7),
        g("return", 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17),       # created a, b, back, other_at_B, other_back, current
    )
    want = (
        ("-1", "136", "KUM_FN"),
        "A jur",
        ("1", "global", "5006", "1", "1", "var198", "0", "3"),
        ("1", "26", "global", "2"),
        ("468", "1", "1", "310:HO1_FNM"),
        ("-1", "1", "1"),
        ("-1", "-1", "1"),
        ("55", "1", "2", "2"),
        ("-1", "2", "1"),
        ("37", "1"),
        ("23", "1", "area", "2455"),
        ("1", "2", "2", "118", "222", "118"),
    )
    return got, want, \
        "player.become into the DB (id, model, bio); message 25 inline; a " \
        "second context runs in the dialog.start frame; the shown bit and " \
        "the player hidden by -1; a screen left resumes at -1; scene.load/" \
        "unload on the resident area; the resident table a message resolves " \
        "through; A->B->A creates no startup context"
```

## Doc text

**docs/SCRIPT_VM.md** (the status/resume map, beside T10's):

> `dialog.start` (61) is the one opcode where `Script_Execute` RETURNS —
> `if (v4 == 61) return;` — and it returns for that context alone; the pump's
> slot loop continues and `Game_Tick` still ticks the camera. What stops the
> world during a conversation is `Script_ProcessActions`' `g_DialogState == 3`
> gate on the NEXT frame, not the return. A screen closed without a choice
> resumes its script too: `UI_OpenScreen` seeds the answer at -1, every close
> path posts event 5 with it, and case 5 does `Var_Set(var, -1)` and status 1.
> `Message_RunHandlers` (0x00409420) gives a handler a fresh context whose
> parameter block is `{message, sender}`; the shared fetch reads the block from
> its SECOND word, so `push.i16 0x4000` — all 22 shipped uses — pushes the
> sender. Message 25 runs inline; every other one is queued (actions 1, 4).
> `scene.load` / `scene.unload` (71/72) on an area in a resident slot swap the
> scene in the same frame: the old SCENE block's context is freed, the new
> block's `+4` script is queued. `Area_LoadIntoSlot` (0x00402B70) into a slot
> that already holds the area only refreshes the fog and returns, so an
> A -> B -> A return runs no startup script.

**docs/GAME_STATE.md** (the player record):

> `player.become` (56, handler 0x402F60) is what fills the player record at
> +60: `strcpy` of the actor record's two bio pointers into +336 and +592, then
> `rep movsd` of 0x43 dwords from the record's +8 into +68 — everything but
> the two pointers `State_Apply` plants. So the record's +272 is the player's
> actor id, `IAM\START` ships it as -1, and AREA 118's startup script writes
> 136 (`KUM_FN`) before anything else. `character.show`/`hide` (78/79) write
> the character record's +18 into the +20 bitmap (`ObjectShown`); `hide -1`
> is the player and writes no bit.

**engine/README.md** (the audit table): the actor-runtime and game-state rows
gain "player.become into the DB record and bios", "message dispatch
(`Session::postMessage`)", "scene.load/unload on the resident area", "the
resident-return skip", "the ObjectShown bit". `Actors_SpawnFromTables`
reading that bit back on load is NOT ported (below).

## Not done, and why

* **`Actors_SpawnFromTables`** — the bit's consumer — is not ported: on a
  fresh area load the Session's `shown_` is not rebuilt from the bitmap
  (START has 628 of 1032 bits set, none of AREA 118's two). Doing it would
  change what `omk-play` draws on every transition and belongs with the
  transition machine (T11), not with a bit write.
* The sender's slot -> id mapping (`Actor_IdBySlot` for messages 0..12 but 4,
  `ObjectSlot_Id` for 4/20/25): no slot tables in the Session; passed through.
* `Zones_RegisterAll` after 71/72: no zone model in the Session (issue 10).
* A `scene.load`/`unload` aimed at the OTHER resident slot's area would swap
  that slot's scene in the engine; the Session holds only its id (issue 15).
* On a resident return the returning area's `.SCX` is loaded FRESH (labelled
  in `finishAreaTransition`): the engine still holds it with its programs.
* Message 0 sets `byte_4C012C` (the "message-0 handler running" marker `end`
  clears, issue 38): not modelled.
* `dbWrite` is the const_cast stand-in for a `GameState` byte writer (above).

```

# T20 — `omk-play` stages EVERY character on screen (issue 41)

Integrated 2026-09-03: play.cpp kept; the log row (rewritten to the CORRECTED state) into docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md; the README coverage sentence; issue 41 moved to Fixed in todo/omk-play.md; plan T20 marked landed. TWO follow-up fixes were made in the main session after this deliverable: (1) a path-less scx.play.actor snaps the body to the clip's root key 0 (clipRootStart) instead of its 20-byte placement record, so the beat cameras frame it; (2) the program's placement is cached and re-asserted each frame, so a fromTable body's per-frame reset no longer adds the full root motion on top of the record. With both, Kay'l arrives dead-centre in the Impasse beat camera (frames 700/900).

Batch 3, task T20. One file changed: `engine/backends/sdl/play.cpp`
(2 986 → 3 494 lines). Nothing else was touched — not `area.*`, not
`verify.py`, not the docs, not the Makefile — and `verify.py` was not run.

## 1. What changed in `play.cpp`, by function, and the rule each piece follows

### The one `speaker*` body became a list

Removed: `speakerRest`, `speakerPosed`, `speakerTex`, `speakerFace`,
`speakerPelvis`, the file-global `sceneTracks`/`sceneClipWas`. What is left
under "THE SPEAKER" belongs to the LINE, not to a body: `speakerModel`,
`speakerVoice`, `speakerTracks` (the `.3DM`), `speakerMorph`, the camera solve
(`speakerAt`, now with `speakerSolved`).

Added, beside them:

* `struct CharModel` — one `.3DO`/`.3DT` per MODEL NAME (`rest`, `meshes`,
  `tex`, `face`, `root`, `texBase`), held in a `std::map<std::string,
  CharModel>`. Shared by every actor wearing it: the alley's three passers-by
  are one `PA1_FN`. Node-based map, so a pointer into it survives later
  inserts.
* `struct CharBank` — one `.CTL` per BANK NAME plus `idleClip`, the entry
  `Actor_LoadModel` → `Actor_LoadBankList` leaves the channel on. The
  resolution is `PlayerController`'s constructor transcribed:
  `Cef_DefaultGroup` is the group whose `flags` bit 0 is set, `Cef_DefaultEntry`
  its `defaultEntry`, then `clipOwner()`'s chain — an entry whose flags carry
  `0x8002` is an alias and hands the clip on through its GoTo.
* `struct Staged` — one per actor id: `posed` geometry, `at`/`facing`,
  `placed`/`pelvis`, the per-actor scene-clip cache, the idle tracks, the
  seat, and the pose source for the log. Held as
  `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Staged>>` — **never** a `vector<Staged>`: the
  Vulkan backend caches a vertex buffer by (pointer, revision), and a
  reallocation would hand it a moved object. `posed.revision = ++worldGeoRev`
  every frame it is drawn, so a freed address that is reused can never carry a
  revision the backend has already seen.

### `charModelFor` / `charBankFor` / `idleTracksFor` (new lambdas)

`idleTracksFor` is `PlayerController::poseTracks()`'s recipe transcribed: a
`.CTL` clip is an `.ani` DESCRIPTOR with no `"3.0V"` wrapper, its tracks resolve
to meshes by name, and **key 0 is the rest sentinel** so frame `f` reads key
`f + 1`. Only frame 0 is built — nothing here ticks a channel per actor.

### The sync, replacing "WHOEVER IS ON SCREEN"

Was: `if (!session.shown().empty() && speakerModel.empty())` — load
`front()`'s model, once. Now: every `Session::Shown` gets a `Staged`; a
`fromTable` row supplies `pos`/`facing` (a placement record names a spot on the
GROUND, so the anchor is the FEET); a row with `fromTable` false carries no
position, because `Session::showCharacter` pushes a bare record, and such a
body waits for a program path or a camera solve. In adventure mode the actor
equal to `session.playerActor()` is skipped, because the controller owns that
body — so he is not drawn twice. A body no longer in `shown()` is dropped, and
a model no staged body wears leaves the pool.

The conversation's speaker is staged even when no table places him and no
script shows him: keyed on `dialogue().conversation().speaker` (the DIALOG
chunk's word 0), falling back to a model-name match, and placed from the
camera solve when nothing else has placed him.

### The pose source, resolved PER ACTOR

The bug issue 41 names is here. The old loop took the LAST running `"actor"`
program for the one body:

```
for k in sc.started(): if how=="actor" && clip>=0 && running: sceneClip = ...
```

Now each `Staged` looks for the program that drives IT:

* `how == "actor"` → `Started.actor == s.actor` (`ScriptObject_StartOnActor`
  puts the CHARACTERS id in the call's first field);
* `how == "player"` → `s.actor == session.playerActor()`. **This was found by
  rendering**: keying on `"actor"` alone left Kay'l in his idle through his own
  arrival, because the Impasse's `A_1_KaylArrives` is a `scx.play.player`
  program and sets no `Started.actor` at all;
* a running program whose actor is nobody on screen drives the frame's ONLY
  body — LABELLED as a reconstruction. AREA 118's arrival needs it (the shown
  list carries Kay'l as 310, the program names another id) and it can never
  mis-assign once there is more than one body, which is the case the issue is
  about.

Then, in order: (a) that program's clip on its authored `.3DP` path
(`Path_Sample`, mode 1 LINEAR, plus the call's inch offset — the existing code
moved into the per-character loop); (b) the conversation line's `.3DM` and its
face, with `sub_42D120`'s two-sided fade unchanged and the root NOT cancelled
when a scene clip stages him; (c) the bank's default entry at frame 0; (d) the
rest pose.

### The anchor — and one correction the pictures forced

`composePose` leaves a hierarchy ROOT at its authored position, and character
models are **not authored about the origin**: `HO1_FN`'s `UBassin` is at
(2.9, −2.4, 17.9) but `DE1_FN`'s `D1Bassin` is at (507.1, −168.1, 39.2). The
old code placed the model ORIGIN on the placement, so the Demon drew 507 units
up the alley (measured: box x 8060..8164 for a placement at 7604). The pelvis
is what a placement names — the rule CLAUDE.md 6 settled for the web
viewers — so the model's own root offset is subtracted first. It also moves
the intro speaker by (2.9, ·, 17.9), which is why the intro frame is no longer
pixel-identical (§3).

Height: an authored PATH names the pelvis and its height is kept; a placement
record and a camera solve name the ground, so the FEET go there (largest y —
the game's Y points down), seated on `floorUnder(playerSoup, x, y−1, z)`,
which is `walk_set.cpp`'s own `seatOnFloor` direction. **The seat is taken
ONCE**, when the pose source or the clip changes, and the clip's root motion
moves him from there — re-seating every frame cancels every vertical a clip
has, so a jump would slide along the ground. If the walkable floor is more
than a body height (100 units) below the authored point the authored y is kept
and a line says so; that cut-off is this file's, not the engine's.

Facing (`Actor_SetEuler`) is applied only to a body no clip is turning: a
scene clip carries its own root orientation and a line's root is relative to
the actor's own frame.

### The texture pool

`worldTex`, then one section per staged MODEL (`CharModel::texBase`), then the
player's (`playerTexBase`), then the sprites' (`spriteTexBase`) — a batch's
slot is its material plus its owner's base, the engine's own indexing (the
bucket key's low six bits, ASSETS 4b). Rebuilt on a **composition** counter
(`poolComposition`, bumped by `rebuildWorld`, by a model loaded and by a model
dropped) plus the two booleans for the player and sprite sections — **not** on
the total size, which is exactly what cannot see two models of equal texture
count swapping. The pool prints one line per cast change, and warns once when
it passes 64 slots (it does: 154 with the sprite section resident, which is
pre-existing — the old pool was `worldTex + charTex + spriteTex` and overflowed
the same way).

### The draws, the set pieces, the summary

Every `drawn` body's batches are pushed with its own base; the player's now
uses `playerTexBase` instead of `worldTex.size()`. The mirror, letterbox,
camera and bucket-sort code is untouched. `setPieceLinks` type 2 (the
three-letter model tag, `sub_450FC0` case 2) now scans every staged body and
returns ITS position, falling back to the player. The exit summary gains
`staged N characters (ids …)` and one row per body still on screen.

### Two instrument additions

* `--eye` / `--at` / `--fov` now override the camera **with the Session
  running**, not only under `--scene`. Labelled in the code as an instrument
  and nothing the engine does. Without it none of the pictures below could be
  taken: the game's own beat cameras do not frame the bodies (§3).
* `OMK_STAGE_PROBE=1` prints, every 100 frames, each drawn body's world AABB,
  corner and batch counts and the live camera. That is what located the
  507-unit pelvis offset.

## 5. One sentence for `engine/README.md`

> `omk-play` now stages **every** character `Session::shown()` reports, one
> `Staged` per actor id with its own posed geometry and its own pose source —
> the scene program whose `Started.actor` is his (or, for `scx.play.player`,
> the player's id), else the conversation line's `.3DM`, else his `.CTL`
> bank's default entry at frame 0 — so the Impasse draws Kay'l and the Demon
> under two different programs in one frame instead of one body wearing
> whichever program ran last, and `--eye/--at/--fov` now aim the camera with
> the Session running, which is how that was confirmed by eye.

## 6. What stays labelled

* **The idle is frame 0 of the default entry's clip, not a running channel.**
  Nothing here ticks a `CefChannel` per actor: an idle body is a still.
* **The lone-program fallback.** A running program whose actor is nobody on
  screen drives the frame's only body. AREA 118 needs it; it is a
  reconstruction, not a rule read out of the engine.
* **The 100-unit floor cut-off** for keeping an authored y instead of the
  probed floor is this file's, not the engine's.
* **The seat-once rule** is the engine's shape (seat, then `Actor_MoveBy`),
  but where a clip's vertical ends up is not verified against anything.
* **No look-at, no shadows, no per-actor `.CTL` runtime, no `Actor_SetEuler`
  from `Started::euler`** (still unported, so a scene-driven body keeps only
  its clip's root rotation).
* **`--eye/--at/--fov` in Session mode is an instrument**, not a slice of the
  port.
* **The 64-slot ceiling.** A bucket key addresses 64 textures and the pool
  reaches 154 with the sprite section resident. Pre-existing, now reported
  once per run.

## 7. Found wrong in issue 41 or in T19's API

* **Issue 41's fix shape says "the running scene program whose `Started.actor`
  is this actor".** That is not enough: the Impasse's `A_1_KaylArrives` is a
  `scx.play.player` program, `Started.actor` is −1 for it, and Kay'l is the
  player. The `"player"` arm has to map to `session.playerActor()`.
* **The brief's "the three passers-by 212/218/219 (`PA1_FN`)" cannot be
  drawn.** `PA1_FN.3DO` is 1236 bytes: one mesh, `PBassin`, 8 vertices,
  12 triangles, flags `0x1` — rejected by the engine's own drawable mask
  `flags & 0x800043`. They have no body in the shipped data, so the question
  "a balcony or a window?" cannot be answered from a picture. Their authored
  y −239 is 160 units above the alley floor (−79), which the code now reports
  rather than silently seating.
* **T19's `Shown::pos`/`facing` are zero for a script-shown actor** —
  `Session::showCharacter` pushes a bare record — so `fromTable` is load-bearing
  for a frontend and `pos` must not be trusted without it. Handled here; worth
  a sentence in `area.h`.
* **`Shown` carries no flag for "this is the player's body"**, so a frontend
  must compare against `session.playerActor()` itself to avoid drawing him
  twice.
* Not a fault, but a trap that cost three runs and is already in CLAUDE.md 5:
  **this is zsh, and `set -- $var` does not word-split**, so a camera passed
  through a shell variable silently arrives as one argument and the override
  is skipped — the frame then looks broken and is merely un-overridden.

## 1. What changed, and the engine line each transcribes

### Issue 5 — the activate dedupe

`Script_QueueAction` (0x004063D0) is now transcribed as `World::queueAction`,
including the arm nobody would guess: a **full** FIFO stores nothing and still
returns 1.

```
v2 = count(+28);
if (v2 >= 4)  printf("%d\n", v2);          // full: nothing stored, returns 1
else {
    for (i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
        if (a2 == fifo[i] && a2 == 2) return 0;
    if (a2 == current(+32) && a2 == 2) return 0;
    fifo[v2] = a2; ++count;
}
return 1;
```

The second half of that rule needs `+32`, the context's **current** action, and
`+32` is not write-only: `Script_Execute`'s tail (0x00406460, the `LABEL_8`
arm) clears it —

```
if (u32(a1,32) != 1 && u32(a1,32) == 2 && !u16(a1,22)) { --dword_4E6B20; ...; u32(a1,32) = 0; }
```

— *only* for action 2, and *only* once the status word is back to 0. So the
dedupe is **"no second activate while the first has not finished"**, not "one
activate ever": a parked activate (a camera move, a screen, a conversation)
holds the refusal open, and one that reaches `end` releases it in the same
`Script_Execute` call, because the `end` handler drops the status and the loop
exits through `goto LABEL_8`.

Ported as `Context::act` (the field), `World::queueAction` (the refusal) and
the clear in `World::pump`, placed in **both** the "not running" path and the
finish path — the engine reaches it from either.

`activatesQueued()` is the engine's own `dword_4E6B20`; `activatesRefused()`
counts the returns of 0.

### Issue 5 — the one-shot bit, **with a correction to the issue text**

`Zone::oneShot()` reads bit 15 of the record's `+64`; `Zone::stateBit()` keeps
the mask, because `Zone_StateBit` (0x0040D500) indexes the save bitmap with
`(id & 0x7FFF) / 8`. **37 of the 4558 shipped zones carry it** (AREA 146, 178,
179, 181 hold most of them).

Issue 5 says the bit "puts the slot in state 5, which the next pump frees (leave
+ free) **whether or not the player is still inside**". The assembly says
otherwise, and this is the one place where the ported behaviour is not what the
issue asked for:

* `Script_Pump` state 2 (`sub_407DC0`, `loc_407FBE`) does
  `test byte ptr [esi+0Bh], 80h` / `mov word ptr [esi+8], 5` — the slot goes to
  state 5, as the issue says;
* but `Game_HandleEvent` case 7 maps **state 5 back to 4** (`if (v22[4] != 5)
  return 1; v22[4] = 4;`), and pump **case 4** maps 4 back to 5
  (`loc_407FD4: mov word ptr [esi+8], 5`);
* and case 7 is raised by `Actor_ScanZones` (0x00467770) **every frame** the
  player is inside the quad and inside the arc — it is not an edge;
* and the pump runs **before** the actor tick: `Script_Pump(1)` is
  `readable/src/05_sys.c:2107` (`dword_4E9740 &= sub_408410(1)`) and
  `Actors_TickAll()` is `:2178`, both inside `Game_Tick`.

So 4 and 5 ping-pong for as long as the player stands there. The bit does not
free the zone early — it **latches the slot out of the press cycle**, and the
free happens on leaving like any other zone (state 5 with no event 7 falls into
the shared `cases 3,5` body). Ported as `Context::spent`.

What the latch is *for* is exactly the gap the `LABEL_8` clear opens: an
ordinary zone whose activate script reaches `end` can be activated again by the
next press, and a one-shot one cannot. That is measured below (zone 1466 stays
at 5 activates; one-shot zone 35141 goes from 5 to 1).

**Coordinator: issue 5's last sentence needs amending.**

### Issue 9 — the touch camera

`World::step` now follows `Actor_ScanZones`'s order — containment first, the
arc second — so a zone that is touched but not faced is still seen. Every
contained zone counts as event 8; when its `+66` is not −1 the step records
`Camera_FindWorld`'s argument, last one winning, because each event 8
overwrites the same request block (`dword_4E6C40`).

New: `touchedCamera()` (the last camera a touch asked for **this step**, −1 if
none), `touches()` and `cameraRequests()` (cumulative). **Recorded only** — no
camera is modelled, and `World` has none to model.

**A count in issue 9 is off**: 54 zones carry a camera, over **40** distinct
camera ids, not 41. Re-derived from the shipped `IAM\AREA` + `IAM\SCENE`:
`[540, 708, 750, 751, 1227, 1230, 1232, 1457, 1553, 1566, 1641, 2121, 2175,
2632, 2999, 3001, 3024, 3025, 3839, 3845, 4140, 4221, 4308, 4311, 4312, 4313,
4384, 4385, 4386, 4411, 4412, 4413, 4414, 4421, 4426, 4755, 4756, 4854, 4855,
5086]`.

### Issue 13 — a parked script resumes

`Context` now owns its `Interpreter` (a `unique_ptr`, so the **stack** survives)
plus `entry` / `pc` / `started`, and `World::pump` calls
`vm->resume(code_, pc)` on a context that has already started. **Only `End` and
the error statuses finish an action**; every park keeps the context's status at
1, which is what stops `Script_ProcessActions` arming the next action
underneath it.

Per status, mirroring `Session::Ctx` in `area.h` so the two agree:

| status | what holds it | what releases it |
|---|---|---|
| `UiOpen` (6) | `waitingForUi` | nothing — a PERSON answers, and `World` has no screens |
| `CameraWait` (7) | `waitingForCamera`, a **countdown in frames** | the move's own length (`r.camTravel`) |
| `ObjectWait` (4) | — | resumes next pump: `World` has no resident scene, so the engine would have nothing to release it either |
| `Suspended` | — | the scheduler, i.e. next pump |
| `Dialog` | `dialogState_ = 3` | `endDialog()` |

`Dialog` is the odd one: the handler writes **no** status, so the context stays
running with its pc past the operand and the *pump* stops instead —
`Script_Pump` opens `if (g_DialogState != 1) return 1;`. `World::step` now
honours that (after the touch scan, which is in the actor tick and is not part
of the pump), and `Script_ProcessActions`'s own `if (g_DialogState == 3)
return` is in `World::process`. `dialogOpen()` / `endDialog()` are the caller's
handle on it.

`setCameraWait(bool)` / `setObjectWait(bool)` mirror `Session`'s pair and
default **off**, for the reason `Interpreter::setCameraWaitSuspends` gives — so
`walk_zone` and `launch_scene` are bit-for-bit unaffected.

Reading the four rows against the acceptance list:

* **(a) five held frames queue one activate — zone 933.** 5 queued / 0 refused
  becomes **1 queued / 4 refused**, and the activate script is entered **twice**
  instead of five times: once from the top and once as a *resume*.
* **(b) the one-shot zone — 35141 (`-30395` as an int16).** 5 activates become
  **1**, over five held frames, with an activate script that reaches `end` every
  time. The leave (`a3`) still runs when the player walks away, which is the
  corrected reading: latched, not freed early.
* **(c) a touch reports its camera — zone 626.** From nothing to 412 touches
  (two zones overlap at that spot), 206 of them asking for a camera, camera
  **540**. The 206 is 1 + 5 + 200 frames; the two "away" frames touch nothing.
* **(d) a parked context resumes — zone 933.** Before, `camera.set.wait` was
  treated as the end of the action and the script restarted from offset 508 on
  every press, so `dialog.start` was **never reached** (`dialogOpen=0`). After,
  it parks at status 7, counts the move's 80 frames down, resumes at pc 556 and
  reaches `dialog.start` — `dialogOpen=1`.

**Zone 1466 is the control, and it is why (a) is not a blanket rule.** Its
activate script reaches `end` inside the frame, so `Script_Execute`'s tail
clears `+32` and the next press queues another activate: **5 before and 5
after**. Holding the button does *not* collapse to one activate in general — it
collapses while the activate is unfinished, which is the engine's rule, and the
one-shot bit is what makes it one even when the script ends. A check that
asserted "one activate per hold" everywhere would be asserting something the
game does not do.

One more difference worth naming: before, zone 3732's **leave** script ran after
`dialog.start`; after, it does not, because the pump is stopped for the
conversation. That is `Script_Pump`'s own first line.

## 3. Check for `tools/verify.py`

Add after `c_engine_zones` (it needs a build, so it belongs in `SLOW`).

```python
def c_engine_zone_pump():
    r"""`engine/`'s zone pump under a HELD button, and a script that parks.

    `verify.py: engine zones` presses action once and looks at what ran. This
    presses it for five frames and looks at what the scheduler REFUSED, which
    is where three separate engine rules meet:

    **`Script_QueueAction` (0x004063D0) refuses a second activate** while one
    is in the 4-deep FIFO or is the context's current action (`+32`) - and
    `Script_Execute`'s tail (0x00406460) clears `+32` only when an activate
    reaches `end` (`if (+32 == 2 && !status) +32 = 0`). So the refusal lasts
    exactly as long as the activate is unfinished, a park included.

    **The one-shot bit** - zone id bit 15, 37 of the 4558 shipped zones - is
    the other half. `Script_Pump` state 2 latches the slot to 5 when it is
    set; `Game_HandleEvent` case 7 maps 5 back to 4 and pump case 4 maps 4
    back to 5, and case 7 fires every frame the player is armed, so the slot
    never re-enters the press cycle. It is a LATCH, not an early free: the
    leave script still runs on leaving.

    **A parked script keeps its context.** `camera.set.wait` writes status 7
    and holds for the move's own length; the pump resumes it from the saved pc
    and stack. Only `end` finishes the action.

    Four zones, five held frames each, one GameState apiece:

    * **933** (SCENE 11) - the activate parks on an 80-frame camera move.
      One activate queued, **four refused**, the script entered twice (once
      from the top, once resumed) and only then reaching `dialog.start`.
      Without the resume the script restarts from the top on every press and
      the conversation is never reached at all.
    * **35141** (AREA 146, `-30395` as an int16) - one-shot, and its activate
      script ENDS. One activate over five presses; the leave still runs.
    * **1466** (AREA 76) - the control, and the reason this is not a blanket
      rate limit: an ordinary zone whose activate ends re-arms, so five
      presses are five activates. That is the engine, and a check asserting
      "one per hold" everywhere would be asserting a bug.
    * **626** (AREA 25) - carries a camera at `+66`. `Actor_ScanZones` tests
      containment BEFORE the arc, so the touch is counted whichever way the
      player faces; case 8 asks `Camera_FindWorld` for camera **540**. Two
      zones overlap at that spot, which is why the touch count is twice the
      frame count.
    """
    import subprocess, tempfile, shutil
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    iam = omkpaths.data("IAM")
    tbl = os.path.join(ROOT, "tables", "vm_opcodes.json")
    if not (os.path.isdir(eng) and os.path.isdir(iam) and os.path.exists(tbl)):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/, gamedata/IAM or tables/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "zone_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"

    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    out = os.path.join(tmp, "z.bin")
    try:
        subprocess.run([binp, iam, tbl, os.path.join(iam, "START"),
                        "200", "1", out, "933", "35141", "1466", "626"],
                       capture_output=True)
        bb = open(out, "rb").read()
        o = 0
        n, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
        got = []
        for _ in range(n):
            f = struct.unpack_from("<14i", bb, o); o += 56
            ran = []
            for _ in range(f[13]):
                r = struct.unpack_from("<4i", bb, o); o += 16
                ran.append((r[1], r[3]))          # action, status
            npk, = struct.unpack_from("<i", bb, o); o += 4
            pk = []
            for _ in range(npk):
                p = struct.unpack_from("<5i", bb, o); o += 20
                pk.append((p[1], p[2]))           # action, status
            got.append((f[0], f[5], f[6], f[7], f[8], f[9],
                        f[10], f[11], f[12], ran, pk))
        trailing = len(bb) - o
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    # RunStatus: 0 end, 1 dialog, 2 ui.open, 3 camera.wait
    want = [
        # id, oneShot, camera, touches, camReq, lastCam, queued, refused,
        # dialogOpen, [(action, status)...], [parked]
        (933,     0,  -1, 206,   0,  -1, 1, 4, 1, [(2, 3), (2, 1)], [(2, 1)]),
        (-30395,  1,  -1, 206,   0,  -1, 1, 0, 0,
         [(1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0)], []),
        (1466,    0,  -1, 206,   0,  -1, 5, 0, 0, [(2, 0)] * 5, []),
        (626,     0, 540, 412, 206, 540, 0, 0, 0, [(1, 0), (1, 0)], []),
    ]
    return (got, trailing), (want, 0), \
           "five held frames on four zones: how many activates the FIFO " \
           "accepted and refused, whether the one-shot bit latched the slot, " \
           "what the touch scan asked the camera for, and whether the " \
           "camera-wait park resumed into its dialog.start"
```

Registration line, in `SLOW`, immediately after `("engine: zones", ...)`:

```python
    ("engine: zone pump",  c_engine_zone_pump,  "engine/README"),
```

(1466,   0,  -1, 0, 0, -1, 5, 0, 0, [(2,0)]*5,                  [])

## 5. Doc text

For `docs/SCRIPT_VM.md`, wherever the status/resume map lands (T10 owns that
file, so this is text to fold in rather than an edit):

> **An action is not over when its script returns.** `Script_ProcessActions`
> dequeues one action, points the context at the matching script slot and sets
> the status word to 1; `Script_Execute` loops `while (status == 1)`. A handler
> that PARKS its caller writes that word — 4 for a waiting `scx.play*`, 6 for
> `ui.open`, 7 for `camera.set.wait` — and the loop drops out with the pc and
> the stack intact. `Script_ProcessActions` then refuses to arm anything else
> for that context (`if (status) return`), so the queued actions wait behind
> the parked script rather than overtaking it, and the pump resumes it on a
> later frame. `dialog.start` is the exception that proves it: its handler
> writes **no** status and `Script_Execute` simply returns, leaving the context
> at 1 — what stops the world is `Script_Pump`'s own first line,
> `if (g_DialogState != 1) return 1;`.
>
> Only `end` ends an action. That is also what makes the activate dedupe work:
> `Script_QueueAction(ctx, 2)` refuses while `+32` reads 2, and
> `Script_Execute`'s tail clears `+32` only when an activate finishes with the
> status back to 0. Leaning on the action button inside a trigger therefore
> runs its activate script once and waits for it, however long it parks — and
> runs it *again* on the next press once it has ended, unless the zone carries
> the one-shot bit.

For `docs/FILE_FORMATS.md` §5b2b, beside the zone record's `+64`/`+66`:

> `+64` is the ZONES.TAG id **and a flag**. Bit 15 is not part of the id —
> `Zone_StateBit` (0x0040D500) indexes the save bitmap with `(id & 0x7FFF) / 8`
> — and `Script_Pump` tests it as `byte ptr [slot+0Bh] & 0x80` right after
> queueing an activate, latching the prompt slot into states 4/5 so it never
> re-enters the press cycle. It does **not** free the zone while the player is
> still standing in it: `Game_HandleEvent` case 7 maps 5 back to 4 every frame
> `Actor_ScanZones` still finds the player armed, and the pump's case 4 maps it
> back to 5, so the pair ping-pong until the player leaves and the ordinary
> leave-then-free path takes over. **37 of the 4558 shipped zones carry it.**
>
> `+66` is a world camera, `-1` for none. `Actor_ScanZones` raises event 8 for
> every zone whose quad contains the player — **before** the facing test — and
> `Game_HandleEvent` case 8 hands a non-`-1` `+66` to `Camera_FindWorld` and
> points the camera at the request block. **54 zones carry one, over 40
> distinct cameras.**

---

## 6. What I could not do

* **The pump's inline `Script_Run` is not modelled.** `Script_Pump` state 2
  runs the context's *current* script inline before queueing the activate —
  `Script_Run` (0x004060B0) normally, `Script_RunToOpcode75` (0x00406120) while
  the player holds an object — and both are **dry runs** (`g_ScriptDryRun = 1`;
  every handler consumes its operands and returns without writing). `World` has
  no held-object state and no dry-run mode, so it skips this. It matters for
  issue 7 (the unconsumed press, `dword_4E66B8`/message 26) rather than for
  anything here — but note that the one-shot latch's *other* effect is to stop
  those inline runs happening on later presses, and that half is unported.
* **`Script_Pump`'s slot state machine is still implicit.** `World` derives
  "armed" from the position and facing each step instead of keeping the 16
  prompt slots with their states 0..5 and letting `Game_HandleEvent` case 7
  drive them. The two agree on everything measured here, and the ping-pong
  above is modelled by its *effect* (`Context::spent`), not by the states. The
  one place they can differ is a zone entered *during* a conversation: the
  engine fills the slot then (case 7 is not in the pump) and acts on it when
  the conversation closes; `World` defers the fill, so a player who walks
  through and out again mid-conversation loses the enter script. Labelled in
  `world.cpp`.
* **`ObjectWait` resumes next pump rather than parking**, because `World` has
  no resident scene to run a program — the same call `area.cpp` makes, for the
  same reason. `setObjectWait(true)` only changes whether the interpreter
  *reports* the park.
* **Nothing releases a `ui.open` park**, by design: a person answers it. The
  context is listed by `parked()` and sits there.
* **The `Dialog` gate is context-local plus a pump stop**; `World` has no
  dialogue runtime, so `endDialog()` is the caller's. Issue 2 and issue 10 own
  the rest of that.
* **`verify.py` was not run** (task rule), so the check above is written but
  unexecuted as a `verify.py` check — its expected tuple is transcribed from an
  actual `zone_probe` run, and the failing "before" tuple from an actual
  pre-fix run.
* **No golden trace can adjudicate any of this.** `Script_QueueAction`,
  `Script_Pump` and `Script_Execute` announce nothing to `Dbg_LogTagged`; only
  the opcodes the resumed script goes on to execute do. So the standard here is
  DATA-CONSTRAINED + assembly-transcribed, not engine-verified — which is worth
  saying because the resume changes *when* announcements happen, and that is
  the one part a capture could eventually check.

```

# T5 — dialogue: the per-asset LINE STATES (issue 39)

**Files changed:** `engine/src/script/dialogue.h`, `engine/src/script/dialogue.cpp`.
**File added:** `engine/tools/dialogue_probe.cpp`.
Nothing else was touched. `tools/verify.py` was not run and not edited; the
check below is for the coordinator to paste in.

---

## 1. What the engine does

`Dialog_TickUI` (0x0046A200) case 4, at the point it has the line's asset
name, stamps the phase global with one of three values:

```c
dword_9103DC = 2;
if (!strcmp(v48, a125338))     dword_9103DC = 7;   // "125338"
if (!memcmp(v4,  a02e19a, 7))  dword_9103DC = 8;   // "02E19A" and its NUL
```

The second test is **seven** bytes over a six-character literal, so the
terminator is compared and it is an exact match, not a prefix — `02E19AB`
does not match. The two literals differ in their first byte, so the missing
`else` cannot matter.

Case 2/7/8 is the whole of what those three states do, and it is one
condition:

```c
if ((a2 & 0x10) != 0
 || dword_9103DC == 7 && (a2 & 0xFFFFFFF3) != 0
 || dword_9103DC == 8 && Morph_IsDone())
{ Morph_Stop(); dword_9103DC = 3; }
```

state 3 being "the line is over", which walks on to the reply menu. Bits 4
and 8 are up and down — `Actors_TickAll` calls `Dialog_TickUI(2, dword_90E0E0
| dword_4E9718 & 0xC)`, which is why they reach the test at all — and they
are the pair the menu moves on, so state 7 excludes exactly them.
`Morph_IsDone` (0x0042CBD0) is the morph-finished flag `dword_4EA84C`, or a
5000 ms cap in its one fallback mode.

**Both assets ship, and each exactly once** — a scan of all 420 `IAM\DIALOG`
chunks with `tools/omkdialog.parse`: 321 conversations, 1174 nodes,

| state | asset | where | conversation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 `AnyKey` | `125338` | conversation 272, node 0 | `Kay'l / Intro` — the line a new game opens with |
| 8 `SelfEnding` | `02E19A` | conversation 186, node 0 | `Telis Demon/Toit  (Scene)` |
| 2 `Confirm` | the other 1172 | | |

Conversation 186 is **one node whose four `param` are all −1** — no branch at
all. So in the engine it opens, speaks for 7.51 s and closes with the player
touching nothing, which is what a line inside a cutscene has to do. The port
made it wait for a press for ever.

`02E19A` is already named elsewhere in the image for the same reason:
`Morph_Play` arms the blend with `sub_42BE10(1, strstr(path, "02E19A") == 0)`
— it is the one line cut without a blend-out (RECONSTRUCTION 2026-09-02).

---

## 2. What changed in the port

`engine/src/script/dialogue.h`

* new `enum class LineEnd { Confirm = 2, AnyKey = 7, SelfEnding = 8 }`,
  carrying the engine's own phase-global values, with the transcription above
  in its comment;
* `static LineEnd DialogPlayer::lineEndFor(const std::string& asset)` — the
  classifier as a free function, so a caller can ask about a name it has not
  opened and so the two literals can be tested against names the corpus does
  not contain;
* `lineState()`, `anyKeyCuts()`, `selfEnding()` — what a frontend reads;
* `kConfirmBit = 0x10`, `kMenuBits = 0x0C`, `kAnyKeyMask = 0xFFFFFFF3` — the
  input constants named rather than re-derived by each caller;
* `bool cutBy(std::uint32_t input) const` — the whole of case 2/7/8's
  condition for one input word;
* the class comment's "**it never advances itself**" now carries its
  exception, and `tick`'s comment says which state changes phase and why.

`engine/src/script/dialogue.cpp`

* `enter()` stamps `lineState_ = lineEndFor(voice_)` when the line starts —
  case 4's point in the machine;
* `cutBy` transcribes the three clauses; `lineOver()` stands in for
  `Morph_IsDone` because the port's clock for a line is its decoded voice;
* `tick` ends with `if (phase_ == Speaking && cutBy(0)) next();`. `cutBy(0)`
  is case 2/7/8 with no input word, which only a `SelfEnding` line can
  satisfy, so `Confirm` and `AnyKey` lines still wait — the rule that was
  right — and a state-8 line walks on through `next()` **unchanged**,
  including its rule that a lone unnamed continue branch advances straight
  through. One node per tick at most, the same as one press per frame.

`anyKeyCuts()` is exposed and nothing in this task consumes it: honouring it
is the viewer's half (T9 / a later frontend task), and until then a state-7
line is cut by confirm only, which is what it was before.

### Two behaviours left as they are, on purpose

* **A `SelfEnding` line whose `.3DM` will not load** has `lineLen_ == 0` and
  is therefore over on its first tick. That is one frame later than the
  engine, which sets state 3 inside case 4 when `Morph_Play` returns 0. No
  shipped line reaches it — `02E19A.3DM` is present, 866792 bytes.
* **`Morph_IsDone`'s 5000 ms fallback cap** (mode 1) is not modelled; the
  port always has the decoded voice length.

---

## 3. Before and after — RUN

`engine/tools/dialogue_probe.cpp`'s `self8` section is deliberately written
against the API the port had **before** this change (`tick`, `phase`, `node`,
`lineSeconds`), so the same source compiles and runs on either side of it and
the difference is the port's behaviour rather than the probe's. That subset
was compiled standalone against the pre-fix objects for the "before" run.

**BEFORE** (`c++ -Isrc probe_before.cpp $(find build/obj-T5/src -name '*.o')`):

```
self8: conv 186 node 0, 7.51 s of voice, no press - STILL SPEAKING (tick -1, -1.00 s), phase now 0, still open
```

and the pre-existing tool says the same, from the other side:

```
$ build/play_dialog ../fr ../tables/vm_opcodes.json 186 out.txt ""
1 lines, 0 menus, 7.5 s of voice, STILL OPEN after 0 presses
line 0 02E19A 751 52 1005 1006 4725 0 1
end 1 0 751 0
```

**AFTER**, the same probe source:

```
self8: conv 186 node 0, 7.51 s of voice, no press - ended itself (tick 226, 7.53 s), phase now 2, closed
```

and the full probe:

```
$ build/dialogue_probe ../fr ../tables/vm_opcodes.json out.txt
scan: 321 conversations, 1174 nodes - 1172 confirm, 1 anykey (conv 272 node 0), 1 self (conv 186 node 0)
state7: conv 272 node 0 asset 125338 -> anykey; cut by 0/4/8/C/10/1/20 = 0000111
self8: conv 186 node 0, 7.51 s of voice, no press - ended itself (tick 226, 7.53 s), phase now 2, closed
rule: 02E19A=self 125338=anykey (empty)=confirm 02E19AB=confirm 1253380=confirm 02E19=confirm 125339=confirm 12533A=confirm

scan   321 1174 1172 1 1 272 0 186 0
state7 0 125338 7 1 0 0 0 0 1 1 1
self8  0 0 751 226 753 2 0 1
rule   8 7 2 2 2 2 2 2
```

`226` is not the port marking its own homework: `tools/morph3dm.read` gives
`02E19A.3DM` 7.5102 s and `ceil(7.5102 * 30) = 226`, which is the check's
`want`.

**The existing `verify.py: engine dialogue play` is unaffected** — it drives
conversation 272, whose first line is state 7 and therefore still waits.
Re-run by hand, both its rows are unchanged:

```
$ build/play_dialog ../fr ../tables/vm_opcodes.json 272 out.txt ""
1 lines, 0 menus, 30.7 s of voice, STILL OPEN after 0 presses      # idle row: 1/0/0
$ build/play_dialog ../fr ../tables/vm_opcodes.json 272 out.txt "n0n0n"
3 lines, 2 menus, 99.3 s of voice, finished after 5 presses        # full row: 3/2/9926/1
```

Every `engine/tools/*` binary still builds (`make -s OBJDIR=build/obj-T5`,
exit 0); the header change is purely additive.

### Shown to fail, three ways (PORTING B2)

| mutation | probe row that moves |
|---|---|
| `tick` drops the `cutBy(0)` line — the pre-fix behaviour | `self8 0 0 751 **-1 -1 0 1** 1` |
| `lineEndFor` matches `02E19A` as a PREFIX (a 6-byte `memcmp`) | `rule 8 7 2 **8** 2 2 2 2` |
| `kAnyKeyMask` = `0xFFFFFFFF` (up/down no longer excluded) | `state7 0 125338 7 1 0 **1 1 1** 1 1 1` |

*(Caution for whoever repeats this: the shared tree was being edited by other
tasks, and two of these mutations first "passed" because the rebuild had
failed on someone else's half-written `gamestate.h` and the stale binary ran
— the trap RECONSTRUCTION already records. Check the build's exit status
before believing a mutation result.)*

## 4. The check, for `tools/verify.py`

Registration line, next to the existing dialogue row:

```python
    ("engine: dialogue line states", c_engine_dialogue_line_states, "dialogue.h; FILE_FORMATS 5b2a"),
```

```python
def c_engine_dialogue_line_states():
    r"""A line's END RULE is per-ASSET, and two shipped lines are not ordinary.

    `Dialog_TickUI` (0x0046A200) case 4 stamps the phase global from the line's
    asset name - `strcmp` against "125338" gives 7, a SEVEN-byte `memcmp`
    against "02E19A" (so the terminator too, an exact match) gives 8, anything
    else 2 - and case 2/7/8 is one condition over those three:

        if ((a2 & 0x10) != 0
         || dword_9103DC == 7 && (a2 & 0xFFFFFFF3) != 0
         || dword_9103DC == 8 && Morph_IsDone())
        { Morph_Stop(); dword_9103DC = 3; }

    So a **2** line is cut only by confirm; a **7** line by any input bit
    except 4 and 8, which are up and down and are the pair the reply menu moves
    on (they reach the test because `Actors_TickAll` passes
    `dword_90E0E0 | dword_4E9718 & 0xC`); and an **8** line ends BY ITSELF when
    the morph is done, with no press at all.

    **The port had none of it.** `DialogPlayer` waited for a press on every
    line, which is right for 1172 of the 1174 and hangs on the other two:
    conversation 186 - one node, all four `param` -1, the asset `02E19A` - is a
    conversation that in the engine opens, speaks for 7.51 s and closes without
    the player touching anything, and the port sat on it for ever.

    **Why the corpus scan is here and not just the two names.** "Two lines are
    special" is a claim about 1174 nodes, and this differences the port's
    classifier against `tools/omkdialog`'s own reader of `gamedata/IAM/DIALOG` -
    conversation count, node count, and WHERE each special line is - so the two
    literals are not merely quoted back. The `rule` row then tests the
    classifier on names the corpus does not contain, because one example of
    each cannot show what is *not* matched: `02E19AB` must be 2, and it is 8 if
    anyone re-reads the `memcmp` as a prefix test.

    **And the tick count is external.** `02E19A.3DM` is 7.5102 s by
    `tools/morph3dm.read`, so at 1/30 s a tick the line is over on tick
    `ceil(7.5102 * 30) = 226`; the port is asserted against that, not against
    its own number.
    """
    import tempfile, shutil, math
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    fr  = omkpaths.data_root()
    if not os.path.isdir(eng):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "dialogue_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"
    ops = os.path.join(ROOT, "tables", "vm_opcodes.json")
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        out = os.path.join(tmp, "d.txt")
        r = subprocess.run([binp, fr, ops, out], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(out):
            return ("probe failed",), ("ran",), "dialogue_probe must run"
        rows = {}
        for ln in open(out):
            f = ln.split()
            if f: rows[f[0]] = f[1:]
        if not {"scan", "state7", "self8", "rule"} <= set(rows):
            return tuple(sorted(rows)), ("scan", "self8", "state7", "rule"), \
                   "the probe must report all four rows"
        scan  = tuple(int(v) for v in rows["scan"])
        st7   = rows["state7"]
        # asset, state, anyKeyCuts, then cutBy for 0/4/8/C/10/1/20
        got7  = (st7[1], int(st7[2]), int(st7[3])) + \
                tuple(int(v) for v in st7[4:11])
        self8 = tuple(int(v) for v in rows["self8"])
        rule  = tuple(int(v) for v in rows["rule"])

        # ---- the same scan, off the FILE, with tools/omkdialog's own reader
        sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools"))
        import omkdialog, morph3dm
        chunks = omkdialog.load_chunks()
        convs = nodes = 0
        ref7, ref8 = [], []
        for cid, blob in sorted(chunks.items()):
            p = omkdialog.parse(blob)
            if p is None: continue
            convs += 1
            for n in p[1]:
                nodes += 1
                if n["name"] == "125338": ref7.append((cid, n["index"]))
                if n["name"] == "02E19A": ref8.append((cid, n["index"]))
        if len(ref7) != 1 or len(ref8) != 1:
            return (len(ref7), len(ref8)), (1, 1), \
                   "one shipped line of each state - the check's premise"
        # the state-8 line's own length, and the tick it must end on
        pcm, _ch, _lay = morph3dm.read(os.path.join(fr, "MORPH", "02E19A.3DM"))
        secs = len(pcm) / 2.0 / 22050.0
        # `lineAt_` reaches k/30 after k ticks and `cutBy` tests AFTER the
        # increment, so the first tick with k/30 >= secs ends the line.
        wantTick = math.ceil(secs * 30)

        return (scan, got7,
                (self8[3], self8[5], self8[6], self8[7]),
                rule), \
               ((convs, nodes, nodes - 2, len(ref7), len(ref8),
                 ref7[0][0], ref7[0][1], ref8[0][0], ref8[0][1]),
                ("125338", 7, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
                (wantTick, 2, 0, 1),
                (8, 7, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2)), \
               "the SCAN (conversations, nodes, and how many lines end on " \
               "confirm / any key / by themselves, with where the last two " \
               "are), differenced against tools/omkdialog; then conversation " \
               "272's first line - its asset, its state, anyKeyCuts, and " \
               "whether input words 0/4/8/C/10/1/20 cut it (only 0x10 and the " \
               "bits outside 0xC may); then conversation 186 ticked with NO " \
               "PRESS - the tick it ends itself on (ceil of its own voice " \
               "length x 30, from tools/morph3dm), the phase it lands in " \
               "(2 = Finished), whether it is still playing, and how many " \
               "lines it played; then the classifier on eight names, six of " \
               "which the corpus does not contain"
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
```

  prints `ADVANCED WITHOUT A PRESS` for any self-advance, which is correct for
  the general rule and wrong for the one line that is meant to. Nothing runs

  `&& !p.selfEnding()`. I did not touch the file.

  in fallback mode 1, and the engine's setting state 3 inside case 4 when

# T6 — game-state foundations for issues 29, 30, 37

Files changed: `engine/src/script/gamestate.h`, `engine/src/script/gamestate.cpp`,
and one new tool `engine/tools/state_probe.cpp`. Nothing else was touched, and
no existing signature moved — every change is additive.

Build: `cd engine && make -s OBJDIR=build/obj-T6 build/state_probe` (green).

---

## 1. What was added, and what each transcribes

### Object lists (issue 29)

A list is `capacity` int16 ids terminated by `-1`, and no count is stored:
`ObjectList_SetCapacity` (0x00409B00) recovers it by scanning for the
terminator, capped at the capacity. That scan is `listCount`.

| method | engine |
|---|---|
| `listCount(list)` | `ObjectList_SetCapacity` 0x00409B00 |
| `listAt(list, i)` | — (a reader for probes and checks) |
| `listHas(list, id)` | op 49 `var.set.has_object` 0x0040A440 |
| `listAdd(list, id, noDuplicate)` | op 50 `inventory.add` 0x0040A4D0 → `ObjectList_InsertFront` 0x00409CB0 |
| `listRefusesDuplicates(list)` | the 50 handler's `cmp edi,3 / cmp edi,2` arm |
| `listRemove(list, id)` | op 51 `inventory.remove` 0x0040A5A0 |
| `listRemoveAll(list, id)` | op 52 `inventory.remove_all` 0x0040A6A0, main path |
| `listClear(list)` | **nothing** — port-side only, and labelled as such |

Two things about `listAdd` are not what "add" suggests, and both are the
engine's:

* **it inserts at the FRONT.** `ObjectList_InsertFront` is
  `memmove(base + 2, base, 2*capacity - 2)` then `base[0] = id`, so the newest
  item is index 0 and the terminator slides up one slot;
* **it refuses when the list is full** — `if (capacity == count) return 0` is
  that function's first line, which is also what makes dropping the last slot
  safe.

`noDuplicate` is per LIST, not per opcode: the 50 handler scans for the id only
when the list selector is 2 or 3.

Not modelled, deliberately: `Inventory_Insert` (0x004098E0)'s kind arithmetic,
which merges ammunition and money into an existing slot's *quantity* (kinds
2..6 and 7..11) instead of taking a slot. That lives in the 56-byte parallel
array `dword_69BD68` — a runtime cache copied out of `IAM\OBJECT` on insert,
not part of the DB and not saved — which the port rebuilds from the object
table by id. Only the stored id array is state, and only it is modelled.

### Prop state (issue 30)

`propState` / `propStateBits` / `setPropState` over `StateArray::PropState`,
from `ObjectState_Get` (0x0040B010) and `ObjectState_Set` (0x0040AFC0).

`propState` transcribes the getter **including its sign extension**, which is a
property of the shipped build and not a decompiler artefact — the assembly is

```asm
movsx   eax, byte ptr [eax+edx]   ; the byte, SIGNED
mov     dl, 3
shl     dl, cl                    ; cl = 2*(i%4); dl = 0xC0 at i%4 == 3
movsx   ecx, dl                   ; ... sign-extended too
and     eax, ecx
mov     cl, bl
shl     cl, 1
sar     eax, cl                   ; ARITHMETIC shift
```

so for `index % 4 == 3` state 3 reads back as **−1** and state 2 as **−2**.
Nothing in the game can see it: every shipped consumer masks the low byte
(`test al,1` in op 68/76, `or al,2` before the setter, `& 1` / `& 2` in
`Scene_LoadProps`). `propStateBits` is the plain 0..3 for tools and checks.

### The clock and the script timer (issue 37)

Neither is in the 8192-byte image — they are engine globals (`g_ClockTime`
= `dword_4C2BD0`, `g_ClockDay`, and the timer's `dword_930760/64/68`) — so
`raw()`, `walk()` and the save round trip are untouched. They are on
`GameState` because they are game state a script reads and writes, and because
the clock is the only thing the timer counts against. The save carries day and
time *beside* the DB (`savefile.h`'s 32 + 4 + 4 header); the timer is not saved
at all.

**The clock's unit is a MILLISECOND, and that is derived, not assumed.**
`Clock_Tick` (0x0041E600) accumulates the frame delta — which `Game_Frame` sets
to `30/fps`, so 1.0 is 1/30 s at any frame rate — and every 5.0 of those
(1/6 s) adds **166**. That is 996 units a real second. Two independent
corroborations agree: `Timer_Format` divides the same quantity by 1000 for
seconds and takes `% 1000 / 10` for hundredths, and op 113 multiplies its
operand by 1000 — so `timer.set 900` is the Tetra bombs' 15 minutes, and a
3600000-unit day is one real hour of play mapped onto 21 game hours.

Methods: `clock/setClock/clockDay/setClockDay/clockTick`, and
`timerReset/timerStop/timerStart/timerSet/timerMode/timerElapsed/timerCheckExpiry`
with a `TimerFlag` enum (`kTimerStopped` 1, `kTimerCountdown` 4,
`kTimerVisible` 8, `kTimerExpired` 0x10). `timerElapsed` returns whether the
timer was running, which op 115 ignores — it stores the value either way — and
does **not** apply the countdown flag: only `Timer_Format`'s display does.

---

## 2. THE FINDING: `tables/vm_opcodes.json` has ops 111 and 112 INVERTED

The table names 111 `timer.start` and 112 `timer.stop`. The mechanism is the
other way round.

Neither of the two functions the handlers jump to has a `proc` label
(CLAUDE.md §1's trap — they are reached only by a tail `jmp`), so this is read
out of `Runtime.exe.asm` at the addresses the handlers name:

```
op 110  0x00405340 -> sub_41E260   flags = 1                     (unnamed; 0 sites)
op 111  0x00405350 -> loc_41E2B0   requires !(flags & 1); flags |= 1
op 112  0x00405360 -> loc_41E2D0   requires  (flags & 1);
                                   g_TimerStart = g_ClockTime; flags &= ~0x11
```

so **111 halts and 112 runs**. Three things settle it beyond the assembly:

1. `Timer_SetValue` (0x0041E270) and `Timer_SetMode` (0x0041E290) both bail
   unless `flags & 1`, so the configure pair can only ever precede the start;
2. the shipped scripts do exactly that — all 12 sites of the bomb sequence are
   `timer.mode 12` (countdown | visible), `timer.set 900`, **then op 112**.
   Under the table's names that reads "configure the timer, then stop it";
3. the shooting range does `shoot.end`, **op 111**, then `var.set.timer` into a
   `TEMPS n` variable it shows with `ui.highscore` — a stop followed by reading
   the time off the stopped clock.

Sites: 13 of 111, 15 of 112, 12 each of mode (always `12`) and set (always
`900`), 5 of 115, **0 of 110**.

`tables/vm_opcodes.json` is T8's file and was not edited here. The port's
methods are named for what they DO, so **T12 must wire op 111 → `timerStop`
and op 112 → `timerStart`**; `gamestate.h` says so at the declarations.

## 3. A second correction: issue 29 states op 49's operands backwards

Issue 29 says "49 scans list `field1` for object `field0`". The handler at
0x0040A440 does the reverse: the FIRST fetch indexes the list table
(`lea eax, [esi+esi*2]` → `word_69BD62[eax*4]`) and the SECOND is what is
announced to `OBJECTS` and compared against the entries. So **field 0 is the
list and field 1 is the object** — which is what `tools/script_dump.py`'s
`DOMAIN_FIELD` has had all along ("field 0 selects one of four object lists"),
and what ops 50 and 51 do too.

---

## 4. The check

Shown to fail first: `engine/tools/state_probe.cpp` compiled against a
reconstructed pre-edit `gamestate.h` gives **79 `no member named …` errors**
(`c++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -I<pre-edit> -Isrc tools/state_probe.cpp`) —
none of these accessors existed, which is issues 29/30/37's whole complaint.

Insert beside `c_engine_inventory`:

```python
def c_engine_game_state():
    r"""`engine/`'s game-state FOUNDATIONS - object lists, prop state, timer.

    The three things issues 29, 30 and 37 need before an opcode can be wired to
    them, run over `IAM\START` rather than described.

    **A list is not an array with a count.** `ObjectList_SetCapacity`
    (0x00409B00) recovers the count by scanning for a `-1` terminator, capped
    at the capacity, which is why no count is stored - and every operation
    below has to leave that scan true afterwards.

    **`inventory.add` inserts at the FRONT and refuses when full.**
    `ObjectList_InsertFront` (0x00409CB0) is `memmove(base + 2, base,
    2*capacity - 2)` then `base[0] = id`, over a `if (capacity == count)
    return 0` guard. So the shipped carried list `[6, 171]` becomes
    `[300, 6, 171]`, not `[6, 171, 300]` - an "append" would be
    self-consistent, pass every count test here, and put the wrong item under
    the inventory screen's cursor. The duplicate refusal is per LIST, not per
    opcode: the handler's `cmp edi,3 / cmp edi,2` arm means lists 2 and 3
    refuse an id they hold and lists 0 and 1 do not.

    **`ObjectState_Get` sign-extends.** The byte is loaded `movsx`, the mask
    `3 << 2*(i%4)` is built in a byte register and sign-extended too, and the
    shift is a `sar` - so at index % 4 == 3 state 3 reads back as **-1** and
    state 2 as **-2**. No shipped consumer can see it (they all mask the low
    byte), and the port reproduces it rather than tidying it, with the plain
    0..3 available beside it. The neighbours in the same byte are asserted
    unchanged, because a 2-bit setter that gets its mask wrong is invisible
    until it eats one.

    **The clock counts MILLISECONDS**, derived rather than assumed: `Clock_Tick`
    accumulates the frame delta - `30/fps`, so 1.0 is 1/30 s at any frame rate
    - and every 5.0 adds 166, i.e. 996 units a real second. 300 frames is 59
    ticks of 166 = 9794, and a day is 3600000 units, so the day counter has to
    roll at exactly that boundary.

    **Ops 111 and 112 are named the wrong way round in the table.** 0x00405350
    jumps to `loc_41E2B0` (needs the timer running; sets flag 1) and 0x00405360
    to `loc_41E2D0` (needs it stopped; `start = clock`, clears flags 1 and
    0x10), so 111 HALTS and 112 RUNS - which is also the only order the shipped
    scripts can mean, since `Timer_SetValue`/`Timer_SetMode` refuse unless
    stopped and every bomb site is `mode 12`, `set 900`, then 112. The port's
    methods are named for the mechanism; this asserts each refusal, so a
    wiring that swaps them fails here rather than 15 minutes into a bomb.
    """
    import subprocess, tempfile, shutil
    eng = os.path.join(ROOT, "engine")
    if not os.path.isdir(eng):
        return ("skipped",), ("skipped",), "engine/ absent"
    b = subprocess.run(["make", "-s"], cwd=eng, capture_output=True, text=True)
    binp = os.path.join(eng, "build", "state_probe")
    if b.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(binp):
        return ("build failed",), ("built",), "engine/ must build"
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    out = os.path.join(tmp, "s.bin")
    try:
        subprocess.run([binp, omkpaths.data_root(), out], capture_output=True)
        v = struct.unpack_from("<65i", open(out, "rb").read(), 0)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    return v, (
        # IAM\START as it ships: carried [6, 171], second 2, memos empty
        2, 6, 171, 2, 0,
        # add 300 to the carried list: it lands at the FRONT
        1, 3, 300, 6, 171, 1, 0,
        # the duplicate rule is per list - 0 allows, 2 refuses
        0, 1, 1, 4, 1, 0, 1,
        # a full list refuses, changes nothing, and keeps its front-insert order
        9, 0, 9, 0, 608,
        # remove shifts the tail down and re-terminates the LAST slot
        1, 8, -1, 1, 0, 3, 2, 0,
        # the 2-bit prop state, its sign extension, and the neighbours
        0, 3, 0, 3, -1, -2, 3, 0, 0,
        # the clock: 59 ticks of 166 in 300 frames, and the day boundary
        9794, 53,
        # the timer: idle, configure, start, refusals, elapsed, expiry, stop
        1, 0, 0, 1, 13, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, 1, 12345, 0, 1, 0, 28, 0, 900000,
        1, 29, 0,
        # and the shipped block is untouched by any of it
        2), \
        "IAM\\START's three lists; then the list operations transcribed from " \
        "their handlers - front insert, the per-list duplicate rule, the " \
        "full-list refusal, the shift-down remove; the 2-bit prop state with " \
        "ObjectState_Get's sign extension and its untouched neighbours; the " \
        "clock in milliseconds and its day roll; and the timer, whose ops " \
        "111 and 112 the opcode table names the wrong way round"
```

Registration, next to `("engine: inventory", …)`:

```python
    ("engine: game state", c_engine_game_state, "engine/README"),
```

## 6. Doc text for `docs/GAME_STATE.md`

### 6a. Append to §3, "The object lists", after the four-row list table

> ### What the four opcodes do to a list
>
> The list is a plain array with a terminator and no stored count, so every
> operation has to leave that recoverable. All four are transcribed in
> `engine/src/script/gamestate.cpp`; `verify.py: engine game state` runs them.
>
> | op | function | what it does |
> |---|---|---|
> | 49 `var.set.has_object` | 0x0040A440 | scans the first `count` entries of the list in **field 0** for the object in **field 1**, and writes 1 or 0 into the variable in field 2 |
> | 50 `inventory.add` | 0x0040A4D0 → `Inventory_Insert` 0x004098E0 → `ObjectList_InsertFront` 0x00409CB0 | inserts at the **front**, refusing a full list |
> | 51 `inventory.remove` | 0x0040A5A0 | removes one copy, shifting the tail down and writing `0xFFFF` into the **last** slot |
> | 52 `inventory.remove_all` | 0x0040A6A0 | the same removal repeated until the id is gone |
>
> **The insert is at the FRONT, not the end.** `ObjectList_InsertFront` is
> `memmove(base + 2, base, 2 * capacity - 2)` and then `base[0] = id`, so the
> newest item is index 0 and the terminator slides up one slot; dropping the
> last slot is safe because the function's first line is
> `if (capacity == count) return 0`. An append is self-consistent — it keeps
> the terminator scan true and every count right — and it puts the wrong item
> under the inventory screen's cursor, which is the shape of error §1 warns
> about.
>
> **The duplicate refusal belongs to the list, not to the opcode.** The 50
> handler scans for the id first only when its list selector is 2 or 3
> (`cmp edi, 3 / cmp edi, 2`), so the memo journal and the shop stock cannot
> hold two of anything and the two carried lists can.
>
> Each list also has a **parallel 56-byte record array** (`dword_69BD68`,
> copied out of `IAM\OBJECT` on insert) that the removals shift in step. It is
> a runtime cache, not state: it is not in the DB, it is not saved, and a
> replica rebuilds what it holds from the object table by id.

### 6b. Append to §2's accessor table, under "prop state"

> **`ObjectState_Get` sign-extends, and the port reproduces it.** The byte is
> loaded `movsx`, the mask `3 << 2*(i % 4)` is built in a byte register and
> sign-extended as well (0xC0 at `i % 4 == 3`), and the result is `sar`'d — so
> for indices ≡ 3 (mod 4) state 3 reads back as **−1** and state 2 as **−2**.
> Nothing in the game can see it: op 68, op 76 and `Scene_LoadProps` all mask
> the low byte (`test al, 1`, `or al, 2`). It is recorded because a replica
> that "corrects" it and a replica that keeps it are indistinguishable until
> something compares the value rather than masking it.

### 6c. A new section, after §5 (the clock)

> ## The script timer
>
> Five opcodes and one read, over three globals — `g_TimerFlags`
> (`dword_930768`), `g_TimerValue` (`dword_930764`) and `g_TimerStart`
> (`dword_930760`). None of them is in the 8192-byte block and none is saved:
> the timer does not survive a reload, while the clock it counts against does
> (day and time travel in the save slot's own header, `GAME_STATE` 8).
>
> | op | address | jumps to | what it does |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 110 | 0x00405340 | `sub_41E260` | `flags = 1` — a reset. Unnamed in the table, **0 shipped sites** |
> | 111 | 0x00405350 | `loc_41E2B0` | requires `!(flags & 1)`; `flags \|= 1` — **STOP** |
> | 112 | 0x00405360 | `loc_41E2D0` | requires `flags & 1`; `start = clock`; `flags &= ~0x11` — **START** |
> | 113 | 0x00405370 | `Timer_SetValue` 0x0041E270 | `value = field * 1000`, refused unless stopped |
> | 114 | 0x004053D0 | `Timer_SetMode` 0x0041E290 | `flags = field \| 1`, refused unless stopped |
> | 115 | 0x00405420 | `Timer_Elapsed` 0x0041E430 | `Var_Set(field, elapsed)` |
>
> **The names in `tables/vm_opcodes.json` for 111 and 112 are inverted.** The
> table calls 111 `timer.start` and 112 `timer.stop`; the two functions they
> jump to say the opposite, and neither carries a `proc` label — they are
> reached only by a tail `jmp`, so they are absent from the decompilation and
> have to be read at the addresses the handlers name. Three things settle the
> direction:
>
> * `Timer_SetValue` and `Timer_SetMode` both bail unless `flags & 1`, so the
>   configure pair can only precede the start;
> * every one of the 12 Tetra-bomb sites is `timer.mode 12`, `timer.set 900`,
>   **then op 112** — under the table's names, "configure the timer, then stop
>   it";
> * the shooting range does `shoot.end`, **op 111**, then `var.set.timer` into
>   a `TEMPS n` variable it shows with `ui.highscore` — stop, then read.
>
> Sites: 13 of 111, 15 of 112, 12 each of 113 and 114 (always `900` and `12`),
> 5 of 115, 0 of 110.
>
> **The flags**, from `Timer_Format` (0x0041E300) and the HUD tick
> (`sub_41E480`): bit 0 halted — `Timer_Elapsed` reads 0 when the flags are
> *exactly* 1; bit 2 count **down** (the display shows `value - elapsed`, and
> `Timer_Elapsed` does **not** apply it); bit 3 draw the `HH:MM:SS` readout;
> bit 4 expired — set when the clock passes `start + value`, which also raises
> event 43 with parameter 18 and freezes the reading at the value. Mode 12 is
> `countdown | visible`, and with the `| 1` the setter adds it is the only mode
> the shipped scripts ever ask for.
>
> **The unit is a millisecond**, which is the clock's (§5): `Clock_Tick` adds
> 166 units per 5 frame units — 996 a real second — `Timer_Format` divides by
> 1000 for seconds, and op 113 multiplies by 1000, so `timer.set 900` is
> fifteen minutes.

---

## 7. Where the engine did not settle it — every choice made here

1. **`listClear` has no engine counterpart.** Op 52 with id −1 is not a clear:
   it removes every entry whose 56-byte cache record has bit 1 of `+0x24` set,
   which needs the array the port does not keep. `listClear` writes the
   terminator into every slot — the state a fresh DB ships with — and its
   comment says it is port-side only.
2. **`propState` keeps the sign extension; `propStateBits` does not.** Both are
   provided because no shipped caller distinguishes them, so the corpus cannot
   choose. The exact transcription is the default.
3. **The clock and timer live on `GameState`** though they are exe globals, not
   DB fields. The alternative was a new type; this keeps the state a script
   touches in one place. They are excluded from `raw()`, `walk()`,
   `relocate()` and the save path, and the header says so.
4. **`timerSet` takes milliseconds**, and the ×1000 stays in the opcode where
   the handler does it. `Timer_SetValue` itself takes the raw value.
5. **Method names follow the mechanism, not the table** — `timerStop` is op
   111 and `timerStart` is op 112. Naming them after the table would have made
   `timerStart()` the one that halts.
6. **`timerCheckExpiry` is split out of `sub_41E480`.** That function also
   draws the readout and raises event 43; only the state half is here, and the
   caller raises the event.
7. **`Inventory_Insert`'s quantity merge is not modelled** (see §1). A script
   that gives the player a second clip of the same ammunition will take a list
   slot in the port where the engine bumps a quantity. This is the one known
   gap in the list layer, and it needs the 56-byte cache, i.e. the inventory
   channel, not the DB.
8. **`objectList()` in `inventory.cpp` disagrees with `listCount`** and was
   left alone (not this task's file): it collects every slot with `v > 0` over
   the whole capacity, where `ObjectList_SetCapacity` stops at the first
   terminator and would count a legitimate id 0. No shipped list has a hole or
   an id 0, so the two agree on all shipped data today. Worth unifying when
   somebody owns that file.

```
